Title: Speech at the ceremony of the 61st anniversary of the BC
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: aaniversaario delBC Speech by Governor Hector Valdez Albizu, in commemoration of the sixty-first anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, on October 23, 2008. Today, with great emotion, we commemorate a new anniversary of the creation of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, whose origin undoubtedly marked a before and after in the economic history of the country. Sixty-one years have passed, in which this institution has traveled a stellar and ascending trajectory, contributing decisively to the macroeconomic stability and economic development of the nation, which is why we must feel proud and committed to continue moving forward, sustaining our entity with the work and values that have characterized the Central Bank since its inception. In my fifth term as Governor of the institution, thanks to the trust placed in us by His Excellency the President of the Republic, Dr. Leonel Fernandez Reyna, I appear for the eleventh time before this illustrious audience, formed by authorities, former governors, officials, employees and friends of always. This time, after several weeks of absence for health reasons, I address you imbued with an eternal feeling of gratitude to God, our creator, for allowing me to stand today before you, who were present with your infinite prayers and displays of affection. I allow myself to share with you, all friends, that during that time I was out of the country, I received the selfless care of my beloved Wife Fior; the deep affection of my beloved son Hector Manuel, the example of faith of my dear mother, the unconditional support of my brothers, their wives and my close relatives; and especially, the gesture of solidarity and attentiveness that the President of the Republic and his distinguished Wife, the First Lady, Dr. Margarita Cedeno de Fernandez, as well as the Secretary of State for Finance, Mr. Vicente Bengoa Albizu, to whom I am united by close ties of familiarity and blood; Because they graciously altered their busy official schedule to visit me and have been continuously aware of my health. To all of them and to you friends of always, thank you from the soul! Certainly those weeks away from the country, which allowed me to see things from an objective and serene perspective, were not only physical tests, but also spiritual temperance and deep reflection on the destiny of our country in the present moments. The truth is that never before in more than six decades of existence has it befallen the Central Bank to face a global financial crisis whose magnitudes, dimensions and complexities have shaken the fundamental foundations of the world economy, which can be comparable only to the Great Depression of 1929. Currently, we are witnessing strong questions and debates regarding paradigms that had practically been accepted as irrefutable in the jargon of economic liberalism, such as the deregulation of markets in the face of greater regulation or control of them. Undoubtedly, dear friends, that the current volatility of the markets has ruined the quarterly and half-yearly forecasts, and we have now moved to a scheme that urges us to permanently monitor indicators and economic and financial variables, in order to estimate and weigh the potential effects that could be derived from this international situation on the economic events of small and open countries such as the Dominican Republic. Allow me now, as is part of the tradition on this anniversary occasion, very briefly to refer to the recent performance of the economy, especially the results of monetary policy and GDP growth, and then present to you a summary of the main institutional advances achieved this year. Monetary Policy Decisions and Results I must tell you that, following the policy strategy based on a monetary targeting approach, a monetary program was designed for 2008 that incorporated unfavorable external economic conditions and the strong increase in domestic demand in the first months of the year, as has always happened in the country's pre-election periods. This situation was manifested at the domestic level, due to the signs of overheating evidenced by the fact that real production was growing above its potential level, and bank credit to the private sector was in turn showing growth rates that were almost double nominal output. On the other hand, at the external level, it was evidenced by the high prices of oil, food and raw materials, which is reflected in a deterioration of the current account of the Balance of Payments. In this context of strong external and internal restrictions, and taking into account the lag in the transmission mechanisms of the measures that fall within the scope of the Central Bank, the monetary authorities, in a proactive and responsible manner, adopted a more restrictive monetary policy to maintain macroeconomic stability. In this vein, and based on the Monetary Program planned for 2008, it was decided to adjust the rate of short-term remunerated deposits of multiple banks, which serves as the reference monetary policy rate, from 7.0% to 8.0% in January, to 9.0% in February and 9.5% in September 2008. Similarly, the Central Bank also made use of its international reserves as a policy instrument to accelerate the required demonetization process. In this regard, I must point out that none of these measures have been isolated from the regional context, since practically all Latin American countries adopted policies very similar to ours, in many cases, significantly more drastic to face the current international crisis scenario. Additionally, with the consent of the Monetary Board, the Central Bank took other monetary policy measures to address the potential impact of the external crisis on domestic prices, on two fronts: On the one hand, in order to guarantee positive real profitability to investors in the face of the increase in inflation, the interest rates of the certificates of direct placement to the public by window of the Central Bank were revised, reaching in August of this year up to a maximum of 18.0% per year for the term of three years, And in September the so-called redeemable window was opened again to the public, at a maximum rate of 16.0% for investments to that same term. Despite these rate adjustments in the Central Bank's policy instruments, their effects on the quasi-fiscal deficit have been minimal. On the other hand, changes were made in the composition and periodicity of calculation of the legal reserve percentage that applies to multiple banks without altering their percentage. It should be noted that at the end of September, monetary policy had managed to maintain monetary issuance within the range established for the first three quarters of 2008, despite the difficult conditions in which it has operated this year. As a result of the measures adopted, monetary issuance grew in annualized terms by 12.1% compared to September 2007, this variable standing at RD 120,143.2 million at the end of the third quarter of this year. Within the components of the same, the tickets issued increased by 5.3% in the same period, which indicates a slowdown in its growth rate. On the other hand, demand deposits in the Central Bank grew by 17.9%, reflecting the change in the composition of the legal reserve mentioned above. An aspect that we must not fail to highlight is that the rate of growth of the stock of securities issued by the Central Bank began to fall. We see how in the period between January and September 2007, this stock grew by 17.1%, equivalent to an increase in RD 25,868.7 million, while from January to September 2008, this growth in relative terms was only one 12.3%, equivalent to an increase of RD20,896.1 million. It should also be noted that despite the increase in absolute terms of the aforementioned stock, going from RD 169,829 MM to RD 190,725 MM from January to September 2008, the monthly interest payment for the placement of these certificates are lower by 3% during the same period. This means, in other words, that although there was an increase in the stock within the estimated parameters, the payment of interest was lower than what was paid in the same period of the previous year. Friends, I think this is the time to highlight the increase in the average maturity of the total number of securities issued by the Central Bank, which benefits greater flexibility in monetary policy and the promotion of a long-term culture in the financial market. Since August 2004, a strategy has been developed to extend the term of securities issued by this institution in the context of monetary instruments. And thanks to this strategy, currently 98% of investments are placed with maturities of 1 year or more, and 43.4% of the total Central Bank securities are with maturities of 3, 5 and 7 years, terms truly unimaginable just recently, for a market of little financial depth such as the Dominican. This strongly evidences the confidence of investors in Central Bank securities. As everyone knows, the financial crisis affecting the world economy has its origins in two central phenomena. The first is a period of low interest rates, excess liquidity, and rapid economic growth brought about by a combination of expansionary fiscal and monetary policies in the United States. The second is the strategy of banks, in a context of low interest rates and excess liquidity, to seek higher returns by granting mortgage loans to individuals with low payment capacity, called sub-prime loans. To cover up the risk of these transactions, the credits were securitized, and in many cases, taken off the banks' balance sheets, becoming derivative instruments that were traded on stock exchanges. All this conceived in an environment of increasing deregulation. Once individuals could not meet their payments, a domino effect was generated that has shaken the financial system worldwide. It is important to point out, ladies and gentlemen, that given the severity of the international crisis and the possible recession that the US economy could go through, the reactions of monetary policy around the world have taken two aspects. In developed countries, where growth prospects are low, their policy rates have been reduced with a view to reviving the economy. On the other hand, in emerging economies, such as the Dominican Republic, the policy decisions of central banks have focused on mitigating the negative effects of the external shock, mainly reflected in inflationary pressures and current account deficits, through the increase in their monetary policy rates, verifying that some countries in Latin America and the Caribbean have applied even higher policy rates than ours to make their adjustments. This divergence between the decisions of the central banks of developed and emerging economies, which to some extent could lead to confusion, is mainly due to the decoupling between the business cycles of both groups and the profile of each type of economy. On the one hand, countries such as the United States, England and the European Union, have experienced a significant slowdown as a result of the process of "destruction of wealth" due to the bankruptcy of financial institutions and the fall of the stock markets. On the other hand, developing countries, such as the Dominican Republic, continue to grow, albeit at lower rates, despite high price levels. This growth has helped to accelerate inflation levels, so its central banks have taken measures to make financing more expensive and slow domestic demand with the aim of reducing inflationary pressures. It is expected, however, that if the possible recession occurs in the United States, it will have a lagging effect on the whole world. In a scenario like this, oil, food and commodity prices have begun to fall. And this is a relief for the world economy, in particular for the Dominican Republic. Hence, once the inflationary pressures affecting our economy dissipate, the Central Bank will review the measures adopted on a temporary basis. However, in view of the fact that the risks in the international environment are still high, this institution will remain vigilant in preserving macroeconomic stability and will act with a sense of timeliness and prudence when circumstances so warrant. On the other hand, it is foreseeable that this dichotomy in the implementation of monetary policy between developed and developing countries in the region will be reflected in an increase in the interest rate differential, which makes us think that once conditions in international financial markets normalize, If this differential continues, it would present an opportunity for our economies to attract new capital in search of a greater return. In fact, the low return and uncertainty that today characterizes commercial banking in the United States could encourage Dominicans with deposits abroad to decide to bring their dollars to the country in search of higher real yields. I am convinced that in a passive scenario, in which the Central Bank had not taken any measures with a forward-looking perspective, the control of inflation, which is the central objective of monetary policy, would have reached unsustainable levels at present, not to mention possible disastrous effects on other key variables of the economy. significantly affecting not only wage earners who receive fixed incomes, but the segment represented by the most vulnerable and dispossessed sectors, which are the vast majority of the population. In this regard, I want to reiterate that we have and will continue to fulfill our duty and legal mandate. Precisely, the monetary policy decisions that I have described here, informed to His Excellency the President of the Republic, Dr. Leonel Fernandez Reyna, to the other members of the Economic Team, to the economic agents and to the general public, were adopted with the aim of avoiding a deterioration of macroeconomic stability, which cost so much sacrifice to recover after the banking crisis of 2003. The recent strategies and programs announced jointly by the IDB and the IMF in this direction are part of the idea of making emergency financial facilities available to developing countries to deal with possible negative effects on economies such as ours. Hence, I appeal to the understanding of the economic sectors that have suffered the increase in their costs, aware that they have been difficult and unsympathetic measures, but necessary and unavoidable to preserve the aforementioned macroeconomic stability. Sector Real Economic growth Let me now announce as firsts the main indicators of the economy's performance during the first three quarters of 2008. In the midst of this panorama of international financial crisis and economic slowdown of our main trading partner, the United States, and in response to the monetary measures adopted, in this third quarter of the year the Dominican economy begins to show more moderate growth. Hence, it is verified that the GDP, after having registered in the first half of the year a percentage increase of 7.5%, for the period January-September 2008 has reached a growth of 5.4%, despite the effects of the external shock already mentioned. With these results, it is expected, according to recent preliminary estimates, that economic growth would be around 5.0% at the end of 2008, well above the population growth of the Dominican Republic. The truth is that in the midst of the financial turbulence and the generalized crisis that the world is experiencing today, it would result in an important achievement, even more so if we take into account that according to the projections of the International Monetary Fund, the economies of the United States, Europe and the World Economy will grow around 1.6%, 1.2% and 3.9% respectively, while Latin America will do so by 3.0%, according to the most recent estimates available. The sectors that drove GDP growth in the period analyzed were: communications 15.7%; financial intermediation and insurance 14.0%; energy and water 11.0%; trade 10.1% and construction by 5.3%, after having grown by 10% in the first half of this year. It is worth noting that the agricultural sector decreased by 8.0%, due to the six tropical storms that have hit it since last year, two at the end of 2007 and four between August and September of this year, considerably reducing the harvests of important food items, despite the massive assistance plans carried out by the superior Government to rehabilitate the damage caused to this important economic activity. Inflacion an average annual inflation of 7.1%, prices began to rebound from the end of last year until the accumulated variation of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) January-September stood at 10.76%, reaching for the first time the double digits in a presidential mandate of Dr. Fernandez Reyna, in line with the trend reflected in several countries in the region, that even register levels much higher than ours. On this occasion, these levels of inflation are explained by more than 72.5% by the effect of the external shock from the aforementioned increases in international prices, which had an impact on the domestic prices of the food, beverages and tobacco groups by 33.7% and on the transport group by a 38.8% due to the increases in hydrocarbons, as well as the effects of the passage of six storms that have affected our country since last year: two at the end of 2007 and four between August and September of this year. Recent declines in oil and commodity prices, however, suggest that inflationary pressures will ease by the end of 2008, with inflation expected to be around 12 per cent, while core inflation is expected to remain in single digits at the end of 2008. It is to be hoped, dear colleagues, that the high levels of imported inflation that have affected domestic prices will not continue to erode the purchasing power of Dominicans, and on the contrary, this trend will begin to decrease thanks to the significant reductions that in recent weeks they have been experiencing in the aforementioned international prices. External Sector It is undeniable to recognize, friends, that the international situation has generated significant changes in the development of the productive and financial activity of the world economy, and as expected, this situation has had an impact on the country's external transactions. It's not all bad news, though. Given that there has been a significant reduction in international oil and other commodity prices in recent weeks, it is expected that in principle this will partially offset the unfavourable impact of lower growth in the world economy on the country's current account results. According to preliminary information, the overall result of the balance of payments for the period January-September 2008 was negative by only US261.0 million, which was mainly covered by the use of the Central Bank's international reserves and shows an improvement over that recorded in the January-June period of this year, when this balance was in deficit of US409.0 million. As for available international reserves, these amounted to US1,306.2 million, an increase of approximately US140.0 million compared to June of this year, while gross international reserves rose to RD2,636 million at the end of September 2008. It should be noted that the recovery of this result is consistent with the greater flow of foreign exchange income received by the Dominican economy, which has cushioned the effect of this crisis. In fact, as of September of this year, income from foreign direct investment was registered for around US2,353 million, which represents an increase of US1,342.7 million over the same period last year, with an estimated record amount of approximately US3 billion by the end of the year. I must inform you, ladies and gentlemen, that for tourism to the month of September had been registered US 3,373.2 million, an increase of 4.7% over the same period last year, while remittances amounted to US 2,330.3 million, 5.1% higher than what was received last year. These two items together exceeded by US 265.0 million the income received for this concept in the same period of time. In addition, it should be noted that during the period analyzed the exchange rate has maintained a path of relative stability. Of the total domestic imports corresponding to the first 9 months of this year, whose preliminary figures are in the process of final revision, 43.8% corresponded to the increase in the oil bill, which amounted to US 3,603.9 million higher by US 1,330.0 million (58.5%) than the amount registered in the same period last year. In addition, food imports and some 16/11/2022 19:13 Raw materials represented 9.4% and steel reached 10.1%, so that together food, oil and steel products explain 63.3% of the growth of national imports, basically due to the aforementioned increase in international prices of the same. This shows conclusively the significant impact of external factors on the national economic situation. Another aspect to note, within domestic imports, is the growth of 32.0% registered in "Other Imports", which are related to the growth of economic activity. Of domestic imports, those of raw materials increased by 51.0%, those of consumer goods by 34.4% and the remaining 26.5% corresponded to those of capital goods, which is consistent with the growing behavior of foreign direct investment. Good news is that a positive result was obtained from the capital and financial account of the Balance of Payments, amounting to US3,114.7 million, equivalent to a growth of 131.2% compared to the same period last year when this balance amounted to US1,347.2 million, all thanks to the significant inflow of foreign capital to the country that has been registered, mainly in the form of foreign direct investment. Another encouraging development, ladies and gentlemen, is that given that downward movements in international oil prices have been observed, placing these at around US74 per barrel, by the end of the year an improvement in the current account would be expected, since for every US10.0 that the international price of oil decreases, the oil bill decreases in annual terms US400.0 million. If this price continues to fall, the estimated amount of this bill would be lower by approximately US 840.0 million this year, compared to the estimated mid-year value of US 5,200.0 million, which is equivalent to it reaching about US 4,360 million in 2008. Quasi-fiscal deficit and Central Bank Recapitalization Let me now, all friends, turn to the issue of the quasi-fiscal deficit of the Central Bank. After the reduction of this indicator from 3.6% of GDP in 2004 to 1.8% in 2007, the 2008 Monetary Program has estimated that it will reach a level of 1.3%, which remains within these forecasts, despite the interest rate increases indicated above. It should be noted that so far this year this entity has received RD 4,110.0 million for the payment by the Government of the interest on the bills and bonds issued in accordance with the Recapitalization Law of the Central Bank, approved in July 2007, which constitutes the legal and financial tool to definitively eradicate these losses of our institution. As for the remaining RD 5,050.0 million originally planned for these purposes in the 2008 National Budget, these were reprogrammed by the Law that approved the Supplementary Budget of this year, to be paid in the first months of 2009. As a complement to the Plan for the reduction of the quasi-fiscal deficit, we also want to share with you, the progress that has been made in terms of realizing the assets of the rescued entities, and others that the Central Bank kept in the folder. In the period between 2005 and September 2008, COPRA, the body responsible for these purposes, has managed to make the sum of RD 6,111.8 MM, which represents 30.5% of the total assets that were transferred to it, a percentage that despite the low quality of the assets received, already doubles the international standard in the matter, which is 15% according to information from the IMF. Financial Sector It is important to mention that the regulatory and supervisory authorities that make up the Monetary and Financial Administration, after the banking crisis of 2003 and within the framework of the Stand-By Agreement with the International Monetary Fund, designed and implemented a Banking Regulation and Supervision Program that has allowed today's financial system to present indicators of strength in the face of an unfavorable external environment characterized by the international financial crisis. As you will recall, among the measures implemented under the supervision of a Superintendency of Banks that has been greatly strengthened in its capacities and that has played a stellar role in the process of restructuring and strengthening the Dominican Financial System, the following stand out: 16/11/2022 19:13 recapitalization of banks, the adaptation of banking standards to international best practices, including measures such as the elimination of gradualness for the requirement of provisions, the incorporation of new complementary regulations to the Monetary and Financial Law, among which those related to Supervision on a Consolidated Basis, Corporate Governance, Preparation and Publication of Consolidated Financial Statements stand out. Certainly, as a result of this Strengthening Program, the financial situation of banks as of September 2008 is characterized by:  Growth of Multiple Banking assets of 10%, highlighting the loan portfolio, which registered an increase of 20.6%. Likewise, public deposits have shown an expansion of 25.1%, of which 6.1% corresponds to foreign currency. This continued growth in these indicators is the main indication of the confidence of economic agents in the national financial system.  The quality of the assets, reflected in delinquency levels of only 3.8%, with a coverage of the overdue portfolio of 132%, that is, it has RD 1.32 of provisions constituted for each peso of overdue portfolio, which shows that the bank has been proactive in protecting its assets against risk scenarios.  Equity strengthening policy, through fresh injections of resources in the order of 15.7% that have allowed the solvency indicator of 14.7% to be higher than the minimum required level of 10%, which reflects that banks currently have risk assets protected.  The return on assets (ROA) of 2.4% and equity (ROE) of 27.9% exhibit to date levels that guarantee the strength of the system, evidencing a good climate for financial intermediation. Friends all, as can be seen, the indicators currently presented by the financial sector show a situation of strength to face the current international crisis. However, the monetary and financial authorities remain vigilant of the evolution of this crisis, with the aim of identifying and controlling in a timely manner any possible effects on this sector. Institutional Developments We have indicated above that the financial crisis that humanity is going through will produce a severe shake-up to the foundations of the international financial architecture. Hence, the global trend is towards strengthening prudential regulations and risk control, not only of financial intermediation entities in general, but also of their regulators and supervisors. For all the above, the Monetary and Financial Authority requested the Honorable President of the Republic, Dr. Leonel Fernandez, to withdraw from the National Congress the draft amendment to the Monetary and Financial Law to review and confirm that the proposed modifications respond correctly to the recommendations and regulatory changes that the new international environment is demanding. With respect to the payment system, it fills me with great pride to inform the nation that in April a real-time gross settlement system came into force, to which practically all existing entities have already been incorporated, which has positively impacted the fluidity and efficiency of our system of payments and settlement of securities. as well as in the improvement of the mobility of the flow of capital and the ability to make any transaction with the outside. With regard to the advances in the field of organizational structure for the Central Bank of the future, I am very pleased to report that in November the comprehensive management system of the Central Bank's most valuable asset, its human capital, will go into production. From that date each of you will be evaluated based on your contribution to the objectives of the institution. Likewise, slowly but surely, important progress has been made in terms of operational risk management and business continuity inherent to the Central Bank, as well as in everything related to the issue of transparency, disclosure of data through the website, accountability and compliance with the law on access to public information. 16/11/2022 19:13 I also want to emphasize that the Central Bank's Document Digitization Project is now a reality, optimizing this entire process of administration of its documents and serving as a model for other institutions in the country. On the other hand, allow me, friends, to take advantage of this forum to announce that the Central Bank, in its policy of transparency and permanent improvement of the economic information it produces, with the technical assistance of the Central American Monetary Council, is preparing a monthly indicator of economic activity, better known at the level of the Central American region as IMAE. With this indicator, economic agents will be able to have a timely variable for making their decisions, which measures the monthly physical evolution and growth trend of economic activity. I am also pleased to inform you that the Project for the Harmonization of Monetary and Financial Statistics of Central America and the Dominican Republic is already in its final phase, with the aim of facilitating regional analysis and referential comparison among the participating countries. The next steps to readjust this Central Bank to the new world order will be to improve the management mechanisms to consolidate our corporate governance, through the identification of indicators integrally aligned to risk, human capital, management information system, strategic plan, optimization of processes and spending; All under a performance that facilitates the monitoring of the established goals and that at the same time, in the medium term, allows to insert a variable compensation scheme to reward achievements achieved or exceeded at the departmental level. Challenges and Challenges Today more than ever, the need to promote, with a country vision, a comprehensive strategy aimed at competitiveness, efficiency and maximization of our productive potential, under the implementation of a prudent fiscal policy and in perfect harmony with monetary policy, on the basis that both correspond to our internal realities and the current international context, is urgent. These are difficult times, but as His Excellency the President, Dr. Leonel Fernandez, pointed out in his Inauguration Speech on August 16: "The Dominican Republic as a nation has to look beyond the crisis. It has to consider medium- and long-term strategic objectives that guarantee the continuity of its modernization and development process, which is socially and territorially inclusive and compatible with the nature of these strategic objectives." Definitely, next year will bring great challenges for the world economy, to which the Dominican economy is no stranger. As the IMF's Managing Director said in his speech at the fall meeting: "We can overcome the crisis to the extent that we act quickly, comprehensively, and coordinated." At the national level, I would like to reiterate, friends, that we are ready to take up these challenges and to take the necessary actions to maintain confidence and macroeconomic stability, with an optimistic vision and to bet on the union of efforts between all sectors, because as the English philosopher and economist, John Stuart Mill, said: "There is no better proof of the progress of a civilization than that of the progress of cooperation". I wish to conclude my words by saying that adversity must certainly strengthen our Christian spirit, and in that vein, as the culmination of this discourse, I echo some of the messages of St. Paul embodied in the Sacred Scriptures, when he exhorted everyone to reconciliation, in order to join wills with a view to doing good without discouraging us. I am convinced that with consultation among the sectors of society, and the responsible fulfillment of the obligations of each of its actors, in due time, we will reap the fruits of progress and well-being for all Dominicans. May God bless you all! Thanks a lot.

Como complemento al Plan para la reducci<97>n del d<8e><de>cit cuasi-<de>scal, tambi<8e>n queremos compartir con ustedes, los avances que se han logrado en materia de realizaci<97>n de los activos de las entidades rescatadas, y otros que manten<92>a en carpeta el Banco Central. En el per<92>odo comprendido entre 2005 y septiembre de 2008, el COPRA, instancia encargada a esos <de>nes, ha logrado realizar la suma de RD$6,111.8 MM, la cual representa un 30.5 % del total de activos que le fuera traspasado,porcentaje <8e>ste que a pesar de la baja calidad de los activos recibidos, ya duplica el est<87>ndar internacional en la materia, que es de un 15% seg<9c>n informaciones del FMI. Sector Financiero Es importante traer a colaci<97>n que las autoridades reguladoras y supervisoras que conforman la Administraci<97>n Monetaria y Financiera, luego de la crisis bancaria de 2003 y en el marco del Acuerdo Stand By con el Fondo Monetario Internacional, dise<96>aron y pusieron en ejecuci<97>n un Programa de Regulaci<97>n y Supervisi<97>n Bancaria que ha permitido que el sistema <de>nanciero de hoy presente indicadores de fortaleza ante un entorno externo desfavorable caracterizado por la crisis <de>nanciera internacional. Como ustedes recordar<87>n, entre las medidas implementadas bajo la <de>scalizaci<97>n de una Superintendencia de Bancos ampliamente fortalecida en sus capacidades y que ha jugado un rol estelar en el proceso de saneamiento y fortalecimiento del Sistema Financiero dominicano, se destacan: la 16/11/2022 19:13 recapitalizaci<97>n de la banca, la adecuaci<97>n de las normas bancarias a las mejores pr<87>cticas internacionales, incluyendo medidas como la eliminaci<97>n de la gradualidad para el requerimiento de provisiones, la incorporaci<97>n de nuevos reglamentos complementarios a la Ley Monetaria y Financiera, entre los que resaltan los relativos a Supervisi<97>n en Base Consolidada, Gobierno Corporativo, Elaboraci<97>n y Publicaci<97>n de Estados Financieros Consolidados. Ciertamente, como resultado de este Programa de Fortalecimiento, la situaci<97>n <de>nanciera de la banca a septiembre de 2008 se caracteriza por: <a5> Crecimiento de los activos de la Banca M<9c>ltiple de un 10%, destac<87>ndose la cartera de cr<8e>ditos, que registr<97> un incremento de 20.6%. Asimismo, las captaciones del p<9c>blico han mostrado una expansi<97>n de 25.1%, de los cuales un 6.1% corresponde a moneda extranjera. Este contin<9c>o crecimiento en estos indicadores, son el principal indicativo de la con<de>anza de los agentes econ<97>micos en el sistema <de>nanciero nacional. <a5> La calidad de los activos, re<df>ejada en niveles de morosidad de apenas un 3.8%, con una cobertura de la cartera vencida de 132%, es decir, que dispone de RD$1.32 de provisiones constituidas por cada peso de cartera vencida, lo que muestra que la banca ha sido previsora en proteger su patrimonio ante escenarios de riesgos. <a5> Pol<92>tica de fortalecimiento patrimonial, mediante inyecciones frescas de recursos por un orden del 15.7% que han permitido que el indicador de solvencia de 14.7% sea superior al nivel m<92>nimo requerido de un 10%, el cual re<df>eja que en la actualidad los bancos tienen protegidos los activos de riesgos. <a5> El retorno de los activos (ROA) de 2.4% y el patrimonio (ROE) 27.9% exhiben a la fecha niveles que avalan la fortaleza del sistema, evidenciando un buen clima para la intermediaci<97>n <de>nanciera. Amigos todos, como se puede apreciar, los indicadores que presenta actualmente el sector <de>nanciero muestran una situaci<97>n de fortaleza para enfrentar la presente crisis internacional. Ahora bien, las autoridades monetarias y <de>nancieras se mantienen vigilantes de la evoluci<97>n de dicha crisis, con el objetivo de identi<de>car y controlar oportunamente cualquier posible efecto sobre dicho sector. Avances Institucionales Hemos indicado precedentemente que la crisis <de>nanciera por la que atraviesa la humanidad producir<87> una fuerte sacudida a los fundamentos de la arquitectura <de>nanciera internacional. De ah<92> que la tendencia mundial se oriente hacia el fortalecimiento de las regulaciones prudenciales y el control de los riesgos, no s<97>lo de las entidades de intermediaci<97>n <de>nanciera en general, sino tambi<8e>n de los entes reguladores y supervisores de las mismas. Por todo lo anteriormente expuesto, la Autoridad Monetaria y Financiera solicit<97> al Honorable Se<96>or Presidente de la Rep<9c>blica, Dr. Leonel Fern<87>ndez, retirar del Congreso Nacional el proyecto de modi<de>caci<97>n a la Ley Monetaria y Financiera para revisar y con<de>rmar que las modi<de>caciones propuestas respondan correctamente a las recomendaciones y a los cambios regulatorios que est<87> demandando el nuevo entorno internacional. Con respecto al sistema de pagos, me llena de mucho orgullo informar a la naci<97>n que en el mes de abril entr<97> en vigencia un sistema de liquidaci<97>n bruta en tiempo real, al que ya se han incorporado pr<87>cticamente la totalidad de las entidades existentes, lo cual ha impactado positivamente en la <df>uidez y e<de>ciencia nuestro sistema de pagos y liquidaci<97>n de valores, as<92> como en la mejora de la movilidad del <df>ujo de capitales y de la capacidad de hacer cualquier transacci<97>n con el exterior. En lo atinente a los avances en el campo de la estructura organizacional de cara al Banco Central del futuro, me complace sobremanera informar que en el mes de noviembre entrar<87> en producci<97>n el sistema integral de gesti<97>n del activo m<87>s valioso del Banco Central, su capital humano. A partir de esa fecha cada uno de ustedes ser<87> evaluado en funci<97>n de su contribuci<97>n a los objetivos de la instituci<97>n. Asimismo, sin prisa pero sin pausa, se han logrado avances importantes en materia de gesti<97>n de riesgo operativo y continuidad de los negocios inherentes al Banco Central, as<92> como en todo lo relacionado al tema de la transparencia, divulgaci<97>n de datos a trav<8e>s de la p<87>gina web, rendici<97>n de cuentas y cumplimiento con la ley de acceso a la informaci<97>n p<9c>blica. 16/11/2022 19:13 Quiero igualmente destacar que el Proyecto de Digitalizaci<97>n de los Documentos del Banco Central es hoy una realidad, optimiz<87>ndose todo este proceso de administraci<97>n de sus documentos y sirviendo como modelo a otras instituciones del pa<92>s. Por otra parte perm<92>tanme, amigos, aprovechar este foro para anunciarles que el Banco Central, en su pol<92>tica de transparencia y mejoramiento permanente de las informaciones econ<97>micasque elabora, con la asistencia t<8e>cnica del Consejo Monetario Centroamericano, est<87> preparando un indicador mensual de actividad econ<97>mica, mejor conocido a nivel de la regi<97>n centroamericana como IMAE. Con este indicador los agentes econ<97>micos podr<87>n disponer de una variable oportuna para la toma de sus decisiones, que mida la evoluci<97>n f<92>sica mensual y tendencia de crecimiento de la actividad econ<97>mica. De igual modo me complace informarles, que ya se encuentra en su fase <de>nal el Proyecto de Armonizaci<97>n de Estad<92>sticas Monetarias y Financieras de Centroam<8e>rica y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana, con la <de>nalidad de facilitar el an<87>lisis regional y la comparaci<97>n referencial entre los pa<92>ses participantes. Los pr<97>ximos pasos para readecuar este Banco Central al nuevo orden mundial, ser<87> elperfeccionar los mecanismos de gesti<97>n para consolidar nuestro gobierno corporativo, a trav<8e>s de la identi<de>caci<97>n de indicadores alineados de manera integral al riesgo, capital humano, sistema de informaci<97>n gerencial, plan estrat<8e>gico, a la optimizaci<97>n de los procesos y del gasto; todos bajo un desempe<96>o que facilite el seguimiento de las metas establecidas y que al mismo tiempo, en un mediano plazo, permita insertar un esquema variable de compensaci<97>n para premiar logros alcanzados o superados a nivel departamental. Retos y Desaf<92>os Hoy m<87>s que nunca resulta apremiante la necesidad de promover con una visi<97>n pa<92>s, una estrategia integral orientada a la competitividad, e<de>ciencia y maximizaci<97>n de nuestras potencialidades productivas, bajo la implementaci<97>n de una pol<92>tica <de>scal prudente y en perfecta armon<92>a con la pol<92>tica monetaria, sobre la base de que ambas se correspondan con nuestras realidades internas y el contexto internacional actual. Son momentos dif<92>ciles, pero como se<96>alaba el Excelent<92>simo se<96>or Presidente, Dr. Leonel Fern<87>ndez, en su Discurso de Toma de Posesi<97>n el pasado 16 de agosto: <d2>La Rep<9c>blica Dominicana como naci<97>n, tiene que mirar m<87>s all<87> de la crisis. Tiene que plantearse objetivos estrat<8e>gicos de mediano y largo plazo que garanticen la continuidad de su proceso de modernizaci<97>n y desarrollo, que sea social y territorialmente incluyente y compatible con la naturaleza de dichos objetivos estrat<8e>gicos<d3>. De<de>nitivamente, el pr<97>ximo a<96>o traer<87> grandes retos y desaf<92>os para la econom<92>a mundial, a los cuales no est<87> ajena la econom<92>a dominicana. Como dijera el Director Gerente del FMI en su discurso de la reuni<97>n de oto<96>o: <d2>Nosotros podremos superar la crisis en la medida en que actuemos de manera r<87>pida, amplia y coordinada.<d3> En el plano nacional quiero reiterar, amigos, que estamos dispuestos a asumir estos retos y a adoptar las acciones necesarias para mantener la con<de>anza y la estabilidad macroecon<97>mica, con una visi<97>n optimista y de apostar a la uni<97>n de esfuerzos entre todos los sectores, pues como dijo el <de>l<97>sofo y economista ingl<8e>s, John Stuart Mill: <d2>No existe una mejor prueba del progreso de una civilizaci<97>n que la del progreso de la cooperaci<97>n<d3>. Deseo concluir mis palabras expresando que ciertamente las adversidades deben reforzar nuestro esp<92>ritu cristiano, y en ese tenor, como colof<97>n de este discurso, me hago eco de algunos de los mensajes de San Pablo plasmados en las Sagradas Escrituras, cuando exhortaba a todos a lareconciliaci<97>n, a <de>n de sumar voluntades con miras a hacer el bien sin desanimarnos. Estoy convencido de que con la concertaci<97>n entre los sectores de la sociedad, y el cumplimiento responsable de las obligaciones de cada uno de sus actores, a su debido tiempo, cosecharemos los frutos del progreso y el bienestar para todos los dominicanos. <c1>Que Dios los bendiga a todos! Muchas gracias.

Title: Speech to the Association of Industrialists of the Northern Region, Santiago De Los Caballeros
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Speech by Governor Hector Valdez Albizu to the Association of Industrialists of the Northern Region Santiago de los Caballeros, November 25, 2009 Upon receiving the cordial invitation of the Association of Industrialists of the Northern Region (AIREN) to this conversation, I am very pleased to return again to this First Santiago de America, a heart city, witness of transcendent events and Hispanic figures, recognized as a thriving economic and cultural center of great relevance for our country. On this occasion, I appear before such a distinguished audience, with the interest of sharing among friends, some relevant topics of the current situation of the Dominican economy such as: the impact of the new agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the sustainability of the debt plica, as well as the recent economic behavior, the closing prospects for the present year and the projections for 2010. Agreement with the IMF The present global economic crisis, which has shaken the very foundations of capitalism and exposed the failures of financial deregulation in the United States and the excesses of Wall Street, differs from all those that have shaken emerging markets during the 80 years because of its global and, above all, to its magnitude. Many experts and economic policymakers considered the hypesis that, prior to the deepening of the crisis in September 2008, there had been a decoupling of the growth of the US economy with the rest of the world. In this regard, it was estimated that a recession in the United States would not seriously affect the growth of European and Asian economies, and to a lesser extent, of Latin America, whose sound macroeconomic policies had allowed it to weather the initial effects of this devastating global debacle better than expected. However, this hypesis was not sustained because the financial turbulence that began in the United States infected the industrialized countries and then spread to the emerging countries, mainly through a fall in external demand for our goods and services, and limitations on access to external liquidity, as a result of the suspension of credit lines from foreign banks to the private sector and restrictions on financing by of international organizations. In our case, it is no secret that these restrictions on external financing and the significant fall in government revenues derived from the reduction in domestic demand, made fiscal policy pro-cyclical, that is, they limited government spending, in contrast to what is advisable in situations such as the current one, which demands the adoption of anti-cyclical or expansionary measures. This called on monetary policy to ease financial conditions and take a proactive role aimed at stimulating activities aimed at reviving domestic demand. Against this background, it was necessary to identify additional sources of external financing that would make it possible to execute the plentiful expenditure allocated in the 2009 budget, while contributing to the return of economic growth levels similar to those recorded during the 2005-2008 period, in which an average annual growth of 8.5 percent was achieved. For these reasons, the President of the Replica, Dr. Leonel Fernandez Reyna, together with the economic team of the Government, considered it necessary to sign an Agreement with the IMF, as a strategic component for the relaunch of the Dominican economy. As is known, the new agreement Stand.By, approved on November 9, will have a duration of 28 months and includes the disbursement of Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) equivalent to about US 1,700 million, which will support the strategy to mitigate the adverse effects of the global economic situation. Traditionally, these IMF disbursements were applied as balance-of-payments support. However, for the first time, some US450 million will finance the Government, of which US300 million has already been disbursed, and US150 million will enter during 2010; while the remaining amount would be used to strengthen the Central Bank's international reserves. CENTRAL BANK OF THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC Table No. 1 Destination of IMF Disbursements during the Agreement US 450 MM Government US 1,250 MM Strengthening of RIN It is also important to note that this agreement with the IMF facilitates, before the end of the year, the Government's access to resources from other multilateral organizations (IDB and World Bank), amounting to US690 million, which were included in the 2009 national budget. Therefore, the total amount to be received during this quarter of the year would amount to about US990 million, which will undoubtedly help offset the drastic fall in tax revenues, finance investment already planned for the current fiscal year and increase social spending for the benefit of lower-income sectors of the population. In this regard, I want to emphasize that as is usual practice in these cases, the IMF will periodically follow up and monitor the use of the resources that the country will receive under it, which should dispel any concerns about the final destination of these loans. An interesting aspect to note is that on this occasion, IMF assistance is requested in circumstances very different from those that led to the signing of the Stand.By agreement in January 2005. The devastating effects caused by bank fraud in the country and the rescue modality used by the authorities of the time, generated a deep economic crisis characterized by high inflation, collapse of growth, capital flight and a historical depreciation of the exchange rate. Hence, at that time, the program with the IMF was aimed at covering a balance of payments gap of more than US300 million, while restoring lost macroeconomic stability, resuming fiscal sustainability and recovering international reserves, among other objectives, in order to redirect the economy after the aforementioned banking crisis. On the other hand, the recent agreement approved by the IMF Board arises to safeguard the achievements made at the macroeconomic level during 2005-2008 and mitigate the effects of the global crisis on the Dominican economy. Indeed, the Agreement signed in 2005 responded to the restrictive IMF tradition. However, the current agreement is expansionary and is based on the need to solve the financial position of the Dominican State that contributes to covering the fiscal financing gap and enables the application of an anti-cyclical policy in line with the monetary flexibility implemented by the Central Bank, while favoring the credibility of the policies applied to the economic agents. In addition, the current agreement with the IMF would allow the country, at the external level, to access the international capital market, would help anchor the expectations of investors and analysts abroad; It would promote a greater flow of foreign investment and improve the country-risk rating, which would translate into a lower cost for state and private external borrowing. I take this opportunity to tell this select audience full of important businessmen in the country, that the current program with the IMF does not contemplate a tax increase. Among its objectives is to strengthen the financial and tax administration, the institutional framework of the State and the achievement of improvements in the electricity sector. It also lays down conditions to ensure the sustainability of debt in the medium term. Let me at this point refer, very briefly, to a subject that has been commented on in the media. When the IMF visits the country annually, the IMF produces a report on the Dominican economy under Article IV of the IMF's Articles of Agreement. In this sense, most countries already allow the publication of its content. Now, I want to share with you the reasons that in our case have limited its publication. To date, there is no consensus to publish this report among the group of countries that make up, with the Dominican Replica, the Chair before the Executive Board of the IMF. However, we have expressed to our Executive Director, the representative of Brazil, our interest in this situation being defined within a reasonable time, in order to make known the details of them. Sustainability of Dominican public debt Dear friends, allow me now to refer to an issue that has occupied the attention of the opinion in recent weeks, and that is that relating to the sustainability of the Dominican debt Plea. Some business leaders, economists and politicians have expressed themselves about the level of indebtedness of the Dominican Government, contemplating as part of the total debt, among other lines, the recapitalization of the Central Bank and the stock of certificates of this entity, so we have considered it appropriate to take advantage of this worthy scenario to make some clarifications on the matter. In the interest of confusing and generating negative expectations regarding the management of the debt itself, it has been indicated that there are commitments in arrears, ignoring that one of the preconditions for agreeing an agreement with the IMF is that the country does not maintain arrears, especially external, or that it presents a plan to normalize them. if there are (see page 12 of the Letter of Intention to the IMF). In this order of ideas, it is important to bring to conclusion, that despite the impact of the global crisis on our economy, which has generated a reduction in tax revenues related to the budget in about RD 15,000 million as of October 2009, the Dominican Government has made timely payment of the service of its external debt, not generating situations of delay, so such comments should be discarded. It has been highlighted in the sensationalist analyses, that the total debt to date amounts to about US 18,000 million, coming to affirm that the pace of financing plico is very accelerated, and that in a short time the ratio debt / GDP could increase up to 50%. They have even proposed a slowdown in the pace of contracting the country's debt, curiously when at the moment all the countries of the world are managing financing to apply countercyclical policies. Let me tell you, dear friends, that if the concern is the Government's ability to pay, the attention of analysts should not focus on the consolidated debt but on the debt of the non-financial sector (NFPS), which includes that of the Central Government and other institutions whose expenses are covered with resources from the National Budget. On the other hand, consolidated public debt includes, in addition to the NFPS, the external and internal commitments of institutions such as the Reserve Bank, the National Bank for the Promotion of Housing and Production and the Central Bank, which have their own sources of income to guarantee the payment of their obligations, without compromising the National Budget. nor limit the Government's indebtedness. Therefore, in our view, to analyze the Government's ability to pay and borrow, the right thing to do would be to focus on NFPS debt. It should be noted that the Ministry of Finance currently registers and administers NFPS indebtedness in accordance with international standards, as recognized in its 2009 Debt Statistics Report, the Institute of International Finance, which matches the Dominican Republic with Chile, in terms of progress in transparency regarding the publication of statistics on debt reply. At the end of September of this year, according to official figures available on the website of the Secretary of State for Finance, the levels of the overall debt of the NFPS, both internal and external and expressed in dares, amounts to US11,435.4 million, as recently reported by the Secretary of State for Finance, Vicente Bengoa. Of the aforementioned amount, 62.9% corresponds to external debt, presenting a balance of US7,195.6 million, 0.6% lower than that registered at the end of 2008. While 37.1% is represented by domestic debt, amounting to the equivalent of US 4,239.8 million. With regard to the ratio of debt as a percentage of GDP, the question might arise: why is it important to analyse this indicator? Because it gives us an idea of an economy's ability to pay over time, establishing what proportion of national income should be used to cover debt commitments. That is why the important thing, according to experts in debt analysis, is not its level in absolute terms, but its sustainability. Hence, the international reference par excellence is the debt/GDP ratio. Total NFPS public debt fell from 29.1% of GDP at the end of 2004 to 25.3% of GDP as of September 2009. In the same vein, the external debt component of NFPS in relation to GDP has been declining steadily, from 24.5% in December 2004 to 15.9% in September 2009. Only when the external debt of the financial entities is added, which do not affect the budget plico, this percentage would rise to 18% of GDP. I share the concern of some economic agents about the risks arising from indebtedness, particularly the payment capacity of the public sector to honor its external debt obligations, since it is certainly an issue of great importance in highly indebted countries, but it does not comport with the reality of the Dominican economy. In general terms, in the four years the debt service is around US 1,400.0 million, which represented 12.2% of exports of goods and services for the year 2008. This gives us an idea that the Dominican economy generates the resources in foreign currency necessary to meet these obligations. In addition, to finally dispel the uncertainties around the ability to pay, if we add to the total of exports the income from remittances, it turns out that the service is only 9.6% of the total of these incomes, which do not include flows by foreign direct investment and disbursements of external loans. among others. In another vein, if one analyzes the evolution and composition of the NFPS debt since 2004, one can clearly verify the fact that the current authorities of the country, precisely to avoid cheerful indebtedness, have tried to improve its management and have managed to modify its profile favorably. In this regard, it is worth mentioning that during the aforementioned period 2004-2009, there was a substantial change in the external debt profile. This composition has changed diametrically today. The total external debt with official organizations (multilateral and bilateral), which is the most concessional and soft because it is agreed at lower interest rates and longer terms, has risen from 66.7% in 2004 to 79.1% in September 2009. While indebtedness to the private sector, which is the most onerous and constituted 33.3% in 2004, fell to 20.9% as of September 2009, that is, 12.4 percentage points. These results show a substantial change in the profile of external debt itself, returning to its composition of the late nineties, when the agreement with official agencies was approximately 80% and the private was placed at around 20%. It should be noted that the NFPS' external debt registered an average annual increase of US361.3 million from June 2004 to September 2009, approximately half of the average annual growth that occurred during the period June 2000 to June 2004, which was US665.1 million. CENTRAL BANK OF THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC TABLE No.5 AVERAGE ANNUAL DEBT GROWTH SITUATION OF EXTERNAL PUBLIC DEBT AT THE DATES INDICATED Figures in Millions of US Average Date Start Amount Final Amount Annual Variation JUNE 2000 - JUNE 2004 3,672.3 6,332.7 2,660.4 In another order, with respect to the internal debt plication, although it is true that in the period January 2004-September 2009, the internal debt of the NFPS has increased by the equivalent of US 3,198.9 million, it should be noted that the equivalent of US 2,294.8 million correspond to the debt documented under the Law of Recapitalization of the Central Bank. I want to take advantage of this occasion, in this enterprising Province of Santiago, to clarify once and for all, the concerns expressed by analysts regarding the participation of Recapitalization Bonds in the domestic debt. Let me emphasize that for these securities to be issued, the Government only has to budget annually for the payment of its interest. This is because the payment of the principal of the bonds will be covered by the surplus generated by the Central Bank, with the financial support represented by the payment of interest on these bonds and their income generated based on the projected growth of their international reserves, in accordance with the Recapitalization Law. Hence, we reiterate, that the bonds issued for the recapitalization of the Central Bank do not compromise or restrict the Government's borrowing capacity, since the payment of capital will not imply a financial burden for the National Budget. Moreover, within the framework of the new Agreement with the IMF, some amendments to the Recapitalization Law are foreseen, including extending the term from 10 to 15 as in order to guarantee its fiscal viability in the face of the new economic reality, which will give the Government greater slack to pay the interest on the bonds it issues under said Law. I think, ladies and gentlemen, that it is important to clarify some aspects related to the debated issue of the stock of certificates or securities issued by the Central Bank. It is striking to hear critical comments precisely from those who contributed most to generating the "original sin", with regard to the quasi-fiscal deficit and the increase in the stock of Central Bank certificates. It would seem that those who have made these proposals forgot that it was the monetary management of the banking crisis of 2003 that caused 80.4% of the Central Bank's capital losses, as well as the increase that since August 2004 the stock of certificates has had to experience. Therefore, it is necessary to differentiate that recapitalization bonds are documented as government debt, as I mentioned earlier, while Central Bank securities constitute an obligation of this institution, recorded in its monetary liabilities, and not a government debt. It is the Central Bank, which enjoys constitutionally enshrined budgetary autonomy, that is responsible for paying at maturity, these instruments acquired by the financial system, institutional investors and the plico in general. A tangible example is that, as part of the monetary policy strategy, since June of this year to date, the aforementioned stock has decreased by more than RD 10,000 million, and the return of the capital of these securities corresponded to the Central Bank and not to the Dominican Government. Another issue to which I would like to refer in this meeting is that related to the repeated criticism of the magnitudes of the additional debt that the country is assuming within the framework of the Agreement with the IMF, ignoring that this organization establishes in an exhaustive way a strategy for the sustainable management of the debt envelope, the development of the local debt market. and the improvement of its rating in international markets. In the case of the Dominican Republic, the agreement with the IMF aims to achieve fiscal sustainability in the medium term, foreseeing that the consolidated debt will increase from 35% of GDP in 2008 to 40% in 2011, to decrease to 35% in 2014 and continue to decrease in the following years. If these percentages made Dominican debt unsustainable, the IMF would never have supported the economic program presented in the letter of intent. The truth is that it would be inexplicable to deny a government the possibility of obtaining additional financing to face the problems of unemployment and poverty in the face of the dimensions of the current world crisis, especially at this time when the "spreads" for Dominican debt in international markets decreased by more than 1,000 basis points. By way of illustration, according to preliminary information published by the Central American Monetary Council, most of the countries of the region have increased their level of indebtedness and have signed agreements with the IMF. I have just returned from Central America and we were able to verify that the agenda of these nations has included the placement of sovereign bonds in international markets, in order to increase spending and make their monetary policy more flexible in order to boost their economic activities. On the other hand, it seems that the somewhat sensationalist estimates on the debt lie, erroneously start from the assumption that there will be no principal payments, so they add to the current level of indebtedness, the estimated disbursements under the agreement with the IMF. In other words, a realistic projection of the debt must include, in addition to the scheduled disbursements, the schedule of amortizations of said debt to avoid falling into bulky figures. Friends all, as could be seen, the reality about the debt stands in stark contrast with the questions raised by critics of this issue. The analysis based on official figures, and not on simplistic and somewhat light projections, reveals aspects and trends that, far from generating an atmosphere of concern, confirm a horizon of sustainability of Dominican debt in a context of macroeconomic stability, as contemplated in the Agreement with the IMF. Results of the Dominican economy in January.September 2009 Sector Real Dear friends, the time has come to address a topic that is long awaited by you, that relating to the recent behavior and prospects of the Dominican economy. It is undeniable that 2008 and the months that have elapsed in the present year have been extremely difficult and very complex for a small and open economy like ours. That is why we have separated on other occasions, that managing to overcome the international crisis and its effects, in order to preserve price stability and an adequate economic development that guarantees certainty in the productive agents, has demanded a lot of creativity, tenacious work, the synergy of great efforts and the adoption of transcendental decisions under the leadership of the President of the Replica, Dr. Leonel Fernandez Reyna. The terrible global crisis had a more acute impact on the country at the beginning of this year, evidenced mainly by a slowdown in the pace of growth of the economy, a significant fall in tax revenues, and a restriction on external financing. However, in September we can announce that economic activity has yielded encouraging results. We have chosen this important meeting in this city of Santiago, to announce to the country the scoop that during the period January-September 2009, the Dominican economy, measured through the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in real terms, registered a growth of 2.1%, due to the improvement experienced in the July-September quarter, reaching a growth of 3.4% with relation to the same quarter of 2008. This improvement in the pace of growth is largely due to the effectiveness of monetary policy, particularly the increase in credit to the private sector following the substantial drop in interest rates that has been taking place in recent months. It is important to note that during the July-September quarter, almost all economic activities, including some that until June had been decreasing significantly, began to experience improvement in their behavior, as is the case of the construction sector and local manufacturing. Overall, the economic growth achieved in January-September can be described as satisfactory, taking into account the slow rebound of the global economy. Outlook for the Dominican Economy I know that I have abused your patience, but I would not forgive myself for wasting this meeting to present our vision on the end of 2009 and the prospects of 2010 for the Dominican economy. I think it is undeniable to recognize that the government's announcement of the new Agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as of August, produced an improvement in the perception at national and international level of economic agents on the expectations of closing the present year. In this vein, the rebound in bank credit and the reactivation of the productive sectors associated with domestic demand that has been registered since August, unfailingly predict a more optimistic end of 2009 than what was perceived until mid-year. It is expected that the Dominican economy will register a growth close to 3.0% of GDP, a level of inflation between 6 and 7% as estimated by the Monetary Program, as well as the maintenance of the relative stability of the exchange rate, favored by a significant strengthening of the Central Bank's international reserves. Similarly, the adequate coordination of the monetary and fiscal policies contemplated in the agreement, together with the expected flow of foreign currency, will guarantee the maintenance of macroeconomic stability. It is expected that during 2010 the foreign exchange market will continue to show the relative stability that has characterized it during the scams. This is because a reactivation of international demand is expected, which will promote a moderate recovery of sectors linked to abroad, such as tourism and exports, in addition to an increase in the flow of foreign currency as a result of greater external financing, the sustained inflow of foreign direct investment and the increase in remittances. With regard to bank credit, the agreement contemplates for 2010 that it would continue to grow at a moderate rate of around 5% per year. However, the 11.7% increase in the growth of credit to the private sector from April to date, together with the favorable expectations of economic growth during the quarter of the year, foresee a higher behavior than originally estimated. For 2010, the economic programme envisages an increase in budgetary expenditure on infrastructure and social. This plan also includes the reform of the electricity sector to improve efficiency in distribution and marketing, and the elimination of generalized subsidies to alleviate the burden on finance and close 2010 with an NFPS deficit of 2.6% of GDP. Final Thoughts Undoubtedly, the fundamentals of the Dominican economy and the Agreement with the IMF lay the foundations for redirecting it towards a gradual recovery, guaranteeing sustained growth in a context of macroeconomic stability, through a program that will allow the country to successfully face the adverse effects of the global economic environment. while promoting structural reforms that will result in fiscal consolidation in the long term. Dear friends, in the face of the prevailing international crisis environment, the country faces great challenges as a small and open economy that we are. The current moment demands that everyone, both the public and private sectors, join forces to achieve the sustainable and equitable development that Dominican society aspires to so much. I would like to end my appearance by leaving in the minds of all those present here the words pronounced by His Excellency Being President of the Replica Dr. Leonel Fernandez Reyna, on the occasion of his speech at the Eleventh Meeting of Economists in Cuba: "Although we are living very dark moments, of great anguish and uncertainty, let us not allow hope to die. As has happened before, the current crisis will also be overcome, as in every dawn, day prevails over night." Therefore, dear friends, let us bet without fear, with confidence and optimism on the future of our Nation. Thanks a lot.

Acuerdo con el FMI La presente crisis econica mundial, que ha removido los cimientos mismos del capitalismo y ha puesto en evidencia las fallas de la desregulacin financiera en Estados Unidos y los excesos de Wall Street, se diferencia de todas las que han sacudido a los mercados emergentes durante los timos 80 aos, debido a su car<87>cter global y, sobre todo, a su magnitud. Esto conmin<97> a la pol<92>tica monetaria a flexibilizar las condiciones financieras y asumir un rol proactivo dirigido a estimular las actividades orientadas a reactivar la demanda interna. Ante este panorama, surgi<97> la necesidad de identificar fuentes adicionales de financiamiento externo, que permitieran ejecutar el gasto plico consignado en el presupuesto de 2009, al tiempo de contribuir al retorno de niveles de crecimiento econmico similares a los registrados durante el per<92>odo 2005.2008, en el que se alcanz<97> un crecimiento promedio anual de 8.5 por ciento. Por estas razones, el Presidente de la Replica, Dr. Leonel Fern<87>ndez Reyna, junto al equipo econico del Gobierno, consideraron necesaria la firma de un Acuerdo con el FMI, como un componente estrat<8e>gico para el relanzamiento de la econom<92>a dominicana. Como es conocido, el nuevo acuerdo Stand.By, aprobado el pasado 9 de noviembre, tendr<87> una duracin de 28 meses y contempla el desembolso de Derechos Especiales de Giro (DEG) equivalentes a unos US$1,700 millones, que respaldar<87>n la estrategia para mitigar los efectos adversos de la situacin econica mundial. Sin embargo, por primera vez, unos US$450 millones financiar<87>n al Gobierno, de los cuales US$300 millones ya fueron desembolsados, y US$150 millones entrar<92>an durante el ao 2010; mientras que el monto restante se destinar<92>a al fortalecimiento de las reservas internacionales del Banco Central. Sobre este particular, quiero enfatizar que como es pr<87>ctica habitual en estos casos, el FMI estar<87> periicamente dando seguimiento y monitoreando el uso de los recursos que recibir<87> el pa<92>s al amparo del mismo, lo cual debe disipar cualquier preocupacin sobre el destino final de estos cr<8e>ditos. Un aspecto interesante a resaltar es que en esta ocasin, la asistencia del FMI se solicita en circunstancias muy diferentes a las que motivaron la firma del acuerdo Stand.By en enero de 2005. Los devastadores efectos provocados por los fraudes bancarios en el pa<92>s y la modalidad de salvamento utilizada por las autoridades del momento, generaron una profunda crisis econica caracterizada por alta inflacin, desplome del crecimiento, fuga de capitales y una depreciacin histrica de la tasa de cambio. Efectivamente, el Acuerdo firmado en 2005, respondi<97> a la tradicin fondomonetarista de corte restrictivo. En adicin, el actual acuerdo con el FMI permitir<92>a al pa<92>s, en el plano externo, accesar al mercado internacional de capitales, coadyuvar<92>a a anclar las expectativas de los inversionistas y analistas del exterior; propiciar<92>a un mayor flujo de inversin extranjera y mejorar<92>a la calificacin riesgo.pa<92>s, lo cual se traducir<92>a en un menor costo para el endeudamiento externo estatal y privado Aprovecho la oportunidad para selar ante este selecto auditorio lleno de importantes empresarios del pa<92>s, que el programa actual con el FMI no contempla un aumento de impuestos. No obstante, le hemos manifestado a nuestro Director Ejecutivo, el representante de Brasil, nuestro inter<8e>s de que esta situacin sea definida en un plazo razonable, a fin de dar a conocer los detalles de los mismos. Sostenibilidad de la deuda pblica dominicana Apreciados amigos, perm<92>tanme ahora referirme a un tema que en las timas semanas ha ocupado la atencin de la opinin plica, y es el relativo a la sostenibilidad de la deuda plica dominicana. Algunos dirigentes empresariales, economistas y pol<92>ticos se han expresado en torno al nivel de endeudamiento del Gobierno Dominicano, contemplando como parte de la deuda total, entre otros renglones, la recapitalizacin del Banco Central y el stock de certificados de esta entidad, por lo que hemos considerado oportuno aprovechar este digno escenario para realizar algunas puntualizaciones aclaratorias sobre el particular. Durante el citado per<92>odo la cuenta corriente arroj<97> un saldo deficitario de US$1,275.3 millones, inferior en US$2,475.4 millones al d<8e>ficit registrado en el pasado a. Esta significativa reduccin se explica por el hecho de que la merma experimentada en los ingresos por exportaciones, turismo y remesas, como consecuencia del deterioro de la econom<92>a mundial, fue compensada holgadamente por una disminucin mayor del monto de la factura petrolera y de las otras importaciones de bienes. De mantenerse las condiciones actuales, se espera que al cierre del ao este d<8e>ficit sea de aproximadamente un 6.0% del PIB. Esto constituye una buena noticia al comparar estos resultados a nivel regional. Como consecuencia de la crisis global, durante el per<92>odo enero.septiembre 2009 las remesas familiares, una de las principales fuentes de generacin de divisas para la econom<92>a dominicana, presentaron por primera vez, tras casi una d<8e>cada de crecimiento, una reduccin de 2.2% respecto a igual per<92>odo de 2008, al alcanzar USS$2,279.9 millones. En cuanto a las reservas internacionales brutas y netas del Banco Central, al finalizar el mes de septiembre del ao 2009, las mismas ascendieron a US$2,673.2 millones y US$2,210.9 millones, respectivamente. Pienso que es innegable reconocer que el anuncio gubernamental del nuevo Acuerdo con el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) a partir del mes de agosto, produjo una mejor<92>a en la percepcin a nivel nacional e internacional de los agentes econicos sobre las expectativas de cierre del presente a. En este orden de ideas, el repunte del cr<8e>dito bancario y la reactivacin de los sectores productivos asociados a la demanda interna que se ha registrado a partir de agosto, permiten augurar indefectiblemente, un cierre de 2009 m<87>s optimista que lo percibido hasta mediados de ao. Se prev<8e> que la econom<92>a dominicana registrar<87> un crecimiento cercano al 3.0% del PIB, un nivel de inflacin entre el 6 y 7% como estim<97> el Programa Monetario, as<92> como el mantenimiento de la estabilidad relativa de la tasa de cambio, favorecida por un importante fortalecimiento de las reservas internacionales del Banco Central.
