De igual modo, la adecuada coordinacin de las pol<92>ticas monetaria y fiscal contempladas en el acuerdo, aunadas al flujo esperado de divisas garantizar<87>n el mantenimiento de la estabilidad macroeconmica. Se espera que durante 2010 el mercado cambiario contine mostrando la estabilidad relativa que lo ha caracterizado durante los timos as. Esto as<92> porque se prev<8e> una reactivacin de la demanda internacional, que promover<87> una recuperacin moderada de los sectores vinculados con el exterior, como son el turismo y las exportaciones, adem<87>s de un incremento del flujo de divisas producto del mayor financiamiento externo, el ingreso sostenido de inversin extranjera directa y el aumento de las remesas. En lo que concierne al cr<8e>dito bancario, el acuerdo contempla para el 2010 que el mismo se mantendr<92>a creciendo a un ritmo moderado en torno al 5% anual. No obstante, el incremento en 11.7% del crecimiento del cr<8e>dito al sector privado a partir de abril hasta la fecha, aunado a las favorables expectativas de crecimiento econico durante el timo trimestre del ao, prev<8e>n un comportamiento superior al estimado originalmente. Para 2010, el programa econico contempla un aumento del gasto plico en infraestructura y social. Este plan contempla, adem<87>s, la reforma del sector el<8e>ctrico para mejorar la eficiencia en la distribucin y comercializaci, y la eliminacin de subsidios generalizados para aliviar la carga sobre las finanzas plicas y cerrar 2010 con un d<8e>ficit del SPNF de 2.6% del PIB. Reflexiones Finales Sin lugar a dudas, los fundamentos de la econom<92>a dominicana y el Acuerdo con el FMI sientan las bases para reencauzarla hacia una recuperacin gradual, garantizando un crecimiento sostenido en un contexto de estabilidad macroeconica, mediante un programa que le permitir<87> al pa<92>s hacer frente de manera exitosa a los efectos adversos del entorno econico mundial, al tiempo de promover reformas estructurales que redundar<87>n en la consolidacin fiscal en el largo plazo. Apreciados amigos, ante el entorno de crisis internacional prevaleciente, el pa<92>s tiene por delante grandes retos como econom<92>a pequea y abierta que somos. El momento actual demanda que todos, tanto el sector pblico como el privado, aunemos esfuerzos en lograr el desarrollo sostenible y equitativo que tanto aspira la sociedad dominicana. Quisiera finalizar mi comparecencia dejando en el <87>nimo de todos los aqu<92> presentes las palabras pronunciadas por el Excelent<92>simo Ser Presidente de la Replica Dr. Leonel Fern<87>ndez Reyna, en ocasin de su discurso en el D<8e>cimo Primer Encuentro de Economistas en Cuba: <d2>Aunque estamos viviendo momentos muy sombr<92>os, de gran angustia e incertidumbre, no permitamos que muera la esperanza. Como ha ocurrido con anterioridad, la actual crisis tambi<8e>n ser<87> superada, como en cada amanecer, el d<92>a se impone a la noche.<d3> Por lo tanto, apreciados amigos, apostemos sin miedo, con confianza y optimismo en el futuro de nuestra Nacin. Muchas gracias.

Title: Speech on the occasion of the Sixty-Third Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: SPEECH BY MR. HeCTOR VALDEZ ALBIZU ON THE OCCASION OF THE SIXTY-THIRD ANNIVERSARY OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC, DELIVERED ON OCTOBER 22, 2010. On such a special and memorable date, in which the creation of the Central Bank of the Dominican Replica is celebrated, it has been a custom for the governor on duty to present, as an account, the most relevant aspects on the recent evolution and prospects of the economy. In this morning, it is for those who speak to you a reason for pleasant satisfaction and deep emotion, to address for the thirteenth time all of you, dear members of the Monetary Board, officials, comparos, family and friends, to honor that tradition with almost the sixty-third anniversary. During the institutional life of this governing body of Monetary Policy, I have had the privilege of holding on six occasions the delicate responsibility of assuming its direction. After my first gesture as Governor in the 1994-1996 in the government of Dr. Joaquin Balaguer, His Excellency Being President of the Replica, Dr. Leonel Fernandez Reyna, for the fifth time has honored us with this designation, representing our ratification of last August 16, a new sign of confidence that I am infinitely grateful for and that further increases our firm commitment to the nation and its government. I would like to take this opportunity to recognize the respectful treatment with which the Honorable President Fernandez Reyna has always distinguished us, who, with a modern statesman's vision, has known how to respect the independence and autonomy of the Central Bank, becoming the main ally of the monetary policy initiatives that emanate from this institution, in order to preserve macroeconomic stability. As I have always said in my speeches and today I reiterate it again, I have been able to endure the sacrifice demanded by my functions in the Central Bank, thanks to God's blessing, which gives me back health and guides our steps, as well as the unconditional and loving support I receive from my family, especially my wife Fior and my son Hector Manuel. The truth is that I must recognize, dear friends, that the vertical example of my unforgettable and always remembered Father and the boundless selflessness of my main admirers, my dear Mother and brothers, also contribute to redoubling my strength and tempering my spirit to fulfill my duty. Likewise, I confess to you with heart that I would not have been able to concretize the institutional achievements and advances, without the intense daily day of the work team that accompanies me, including, as I have said repeatedly, from the most humble servant to the highest official of this great Bancentralian family. I want to testify to the relentless dedication of my closest collaborators, the Lieutenant Governor, the Manager, Assistant Managers, the economic advisor and other advisors, the departmental directors and other members of the Staff, who without conditions, or objection to the hours of work, make enormous efforts for the fulfillment of our institutional mission, together with the permanent support of the honorable members of the Monetary Board. I have no doubt that the honest and efficient work of all of you, strengthens every day, the image of credibility and professionalism that our institution projects, inside and outside the country. Precisely, just a few weeks ago, the prestigious international magazine Markets & Trends, in a work entitled The captains of the economy: first regional measurement of central banking, contained in its edition No. 42, published the results of a survey applied to renowned economists and academics of the countries of the Central American region and Dominican Replica to evaluate, during the period May 2008 to May 2009, the governors of the central banks of El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and the Dominican Replica performed. These evaluators rated the actions of the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic as the most outstanding of these countries, giving us the highest rating of 9.1 with respect to a maximum of 10.0, for the good management of monetary and exchange policy in the face of the adverse environment that we have had to face in the scams. This institutional recognition, which I have accepted with the humility that characterizes me, and which adds to that obtained in 2006 when the outstanding magazine The Banker selected us as the Governor of the Americas, is the fruit of the tenacious work of all Bancentralians. I want at this time, to present in the context of the current international economic panorama, of vital importance in an increasingly globalized and interdependent world, a tight synthesis of the recent performance that the Dominican economy has been exhibiting. INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC OVERVIEW After the longest and deepest global crisis since the Great Depression of the 30s, recent statements by the National Bureau of Economic Research of the United States, ensure that the recession that began in December 2007, officially ends in June 2009. However, this economy is growing below its potential, maintains an unemployment rate close to 10%, poverty levels that reach 14.3% and presents a delicate situation in its real estate sector. On the other hand, despite the fact that some countries in the euro area have been seriously affected by a deep fiscal and debt crisis, European economies are on average relatively stable in their real sector, maintaining positive growth, although like the United States, below its potential pace. In addition, it is undeniable that the relative instability of the euro in the months has disrupted international financial markets, causing strong appreciations in other currencies, such as the Japanese yen and the pound sterling. These recent fluctuations in the international exchange market come to add to the undervaluation of the Chinese currency, the yuan, which has been having an important impact, for some years now, on international trade flows. These situations explain why global attention on the exchange rate issue has intensified, escalating priority on the agendas of international organizations and bodies such as the IMF and the G-20. The IMF's timid projections point to growth for the global economy of 4.8% at present and 4.2% for 2011, with developed countries expected to grow at a much slower pace than emerging nations. In the case of Latin America, the reforms carried out in the nineties, allowed to successfully overcome the strong external shocks that have impacted the world in the scams. Both ECLAC, the IMF and the World Bank have agreed that average growth prospects for Latin America would be around 5.7 percent. In this sense, in the case of the economies of Central America and Replica Dominicana, the IMF's World Economic Panorama (WEO), published in October, has estimated that our country would grow 5.5% in 2010, while the rest of the countries that are part of the Central American Monetary Council would grow on average 2.5%, far below the Dominican economy. Concluding with regard to the external environment we could affirm that although it has been proposed that the "Great Recession" has been left behind, there is still some uncertainty about the economic performance of the United States and developed countries in general, so it is advisable to remain alert and in a proactive manner adopt the measures that are necessary to continue navigating successfully in still turbulent waters, with the objective of controlling inflation and maintaining stability, fundamental aspects to promote economic growth. RECENT PERFORMANCE OF THE DOMINICAN ECONOMY GDP growth I now want to share with this select audience, the scoop that the preliminary results of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) during January-September show a robust growth of 7.6%, consolidating its recovery process initiated at the end of 2009 after the global crisis, ranking among the countries with an economic growth above the aforementioned regional average. Quarterly Gross Domestic Product 2010/2009 Growth Rates (%) 10.0 9.0 8.0 7.0 6.0 5.0 4.0 3.0 2.0 1.0 - It is opportune to bring to the conclusion at this time, that the response capacity of the Dominican economy has far exceeded various prompts, some pessimistic and others conservative. In that sense, you will remember what happened in 2009, when we ended up with a growth of 3.5%, despite the fact that the Intelligence Unit of The Economist magazine had projected a fall of 1 percent. Likewise, when we signed with the IMF in October 2009, the original program had contemplated a range of GDP growth between 2.5 and 3.5%, which was later revised upwards by this Organization, taking its projection to the range of 4% to 5% in March, and then recently placing it at 5.5%-6% in the context of the second and third revisions of the Stand-by Arrangement. This shows that the economy is reacting positively beyond the expectations that had been originally conceived defined by both international organizations, the IMF and the Central Bank itself, also meaning that the economy is reaching its potential. In line with what has been said, I want to share with you, dear friends, that with the preliminary results of GDP growth of 7.6% during January-September and the information provided on the production programs of the companies that make up the main economic activities, the Department of National Accounts of the Central Bank is projecting that the Dominican economy will close 2010 growing, conservatively, around 7.0%, with low inflationary pressures. These expected achievements should be appreciated by all Dominicans. Monetary Policy and Economic Recovery We can affirm that Monetary Policy has met the challenge to date of stimulating economic growth through an expansionary stance, consistent with an uncertain international environment and a slower than expected recovery of the world economy. The prevailing low interest rates allowed a reactivation of bank credit and a significant increase in monetary aggregates, without affecting domestic price levels. The expansionary nature of the monetary policy implemented until the third quarter of this year, is clearly observed in the behavior of the circulating medium (M1), composed of money in circulation and transferable deposits, which grew September at an annualized rate of 17.6%, while simultaneously credit to the private sector in national currency expanded an annualized rate of 18.6 percent. Dear friends, the policies adopted by the Honorable Monetary Board and the Central Bank, together with the fiscal impulse in the context of the agreement, contributed to stimulating domestic demand. In this way, it contributes to the growth of productive activities or, what is the same, to preserve jobs of hundreds of thousands of people and the well-being of thousands of Dominican families. Highlights the fact that all activities in the January-September period registered positive growth rates, with the exception of the free zones, with particular emphasis on those oriented to domestic demand and which are also important generators of jobs, such as construction and trade, which experienced the highest growth rates within GDP, with 14.5% and 12.3% respectively. Communications during January-September grew 10.2%, Financial Intermediation and Insurance 9.7%, Energy and Water 8.0%, Local Manufacturing 7.5%, Ensenza 6.3%, Transport 6.3%, Agriculture 5.9%, Health 4.9%, Other Service Activities 4.1%, Housing Rental 3.2%, Mining 1.6%, Government 1.3% and Hotels, Bars and Restaurants 4.2%, this last growth being explained by the increase of 2.7% in the arrival of non-resident passengers, mainly from North and South America. I would like to invite attention to the fact that we consider the current favorable moments to create the conditions that allow the reformulation of the free zone scheme, through policies that facilitate its rebound and solve the structural issues that afflict this sector, and that are not associated with the exchange rate. because in a context where many of the currencies of our competitors have been appreciating, in the Dominican Replica there has been a moderate and gradual depreciation depending on the fundamentals of the economy. Once the foundations for the definitive economic recovery were laid, it was time for monetary policy, as has happened in the most important economies of Latin America, to begin to move towards a more neutral stance. This is because monetary policy is executed looking forward, correcting in advance potential deviations in our inflation target. In that sense, the Central Bank decided to increase, in a preventive manner, its monetary policy interest rate from 4.0% to 4.75% effective October 4. This measure seeks to prevent inflationary pressures in the first half of 2011. As can be seen, dear friends, the decision to increase the interest rate of monetary policy is a far-sighted measure that seeks to create the conditions so that the inflation target of the incoming one is met without major shocks, consistent with a long-term view of the Dominican economic behavior, in the context of the international environment. In this regard, we reiterate that the Central Bank has made progress in seeking to maintain macroeconomic stability and meet the inflation target established in the Agreement with the IMF for 2011. Inflacin As has been expressed in response, the accumulated inflation during January-September 2010 was 4.24% and the annualized inflation, measured between September 2009 and September 2010, reached 5.70%, resulting in Transport the group with the greatest incidence in the behavior of this indicator, due to the increases in domestic fuel prices. Secondly, the Food, Beverages and Tobacco group has had an impact by virtue of the extraordinary increase in demand for some food goods, which originates after the earthquake that occurred in the sister country of Haiti at the beginning of January of this year. IMF Agreement In addition to this Agreement, the Board of the International Monetary Fund is currently hearing the Letter of Intent, which contains details of the second and third revisions of the Agreement. On this point, it should be noted that the Dominican economic team, under the guidelines of His Excellency the President of the Replica, Dr. Leonel Fernandez Reyna, managed to meet the quantitative performance criteria and the structural measures established by the multilateral organization, as evidenced in the publication of the Letter of Intent, with a commitment to continue executing the actions and initiatives embodied in this Agreement that culminates in 2012, which strengthens the perception of confidence of local and external agents in the Dominican economy. Indeed, the IMF verified that quantitative monetary targets were met fairly loosely, both in terms of consolidated net international reserves and the net domestic assets of the Central Bank. In addition, the Government has been complying with the Central Bank Recapitalization Law, which is essential to preserve macroeconomic stability in the long term. Likewise, the commitment to present a plan aimed at making a transition in the monetary policy strategy towards an inflation-targeting scheme for 2012 was fulfilled. This Plan, in accordance with the transparency policy followed by this institution, is available on our website. The adoption of an Inflation Targeting scheme institutionalizes the commitment to work towards maintaining a low inflation rate in the long term, which benefits the ability of economic agents to plan their future activities in an environment of low uncertainty, in addition to promoting transparency and increasing the credibility of monetary policy. This strategy has been gaining ground globally, since New Zealand adopted it more than 20 years. In Latin America, Chile, Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, and Guatemala have assumed this scheme, while others are exploring the possibility of moving in the same direction. It is appropriate to recognize that within the institution we have strengthened the mechanisms of decision-making, accountability and transparency, as well as economic research, through the use of quantitative methods, including econometric modeling, in order to adequately understand the mechanisms of transmission of monetary policy, as well as their effectiveness in the development of the economy, which will facilitate the implementation of the aforementioned monetary scheme. With regard to the fiscal deficit targets, both those of the Central Government and that of the Consolidated Fiscal Sector, both were met with favorable margins. At the end of the first semester of the a, the deficit of the Central Government was RD 29, 741.10 million, an amount lower than the goal of RD 30,400 million established in the agreement with the IMF. On the other hand, the deficit of the Consolidated Plico Sector, that is, the one that includes the Non-Financial Plico Sector (NFPS) and the Central Bank, registered an amount of RD 44,394.86 million in the first half of 2010, a figure that is below the RD 45,300 million set as a goal for the end of June. It also highlights the fact that the quasi-fiscal deficit of the Central Bank as a proportion of GDP in 2010 will be lower than in the past. Dear friends, let me now give you the good news that preliminary figures that have been calculated for the fiscal sector reveal that the Central Government and the Consolidated Sector have also met, with ample ease, the goals established for September in the Agreement with the IMF. Specifically, at the end of September, the Central Government deficit was approximately RD 4,600 million lower than the goal programmed in the Agreement, registering an amount of RD 32,569.28 million. When considering the Consolidated Plico Sector, seras and seres, the clearance of compliance is greater, about RD 7,007.33 million below the goal, which is far from the astronicas figures of more than 60 billion that some economists have disclosed in an erroneous and decontextualized way in order to create negative expectations. Behavior of external accounts in the current environment As supported by the previous figures, the dynamism exhibited by the Dominican economy has been based on the boost of domestic demand, through monetary and fiscal policy. As expected, the higher growth has resulted in requirements for imported goods, in an environment in which external demand from the economies of our main trading partners is somewhat lagging. At the same time, during this period, the country has been the recipient of significant flows of external resources that have had a positive impact on the level of economic activity. At the end of the third quarter of 2010, the available information indicates that the overall balance of payments, as contemplated since its inception in the Agreement with the IMF, given the magnitude of the impact of the global crisis, was negative at US624.4 million, being covered mainly by the use of international reserves of the Central Bank. for which a wide margin is left with respect to the floor established for these purposes. It is important to ensure that, despite the delay in the execution of the disbursements of the multilateral organizations contemplated in the Agreement with the IMF, the reserve position of the Central Bank at the end of September allowed the objective agreed in the aforementioned agreement for consolidated net international reserves to be met with ease. Despite the adverse external environment, according to preliminary estimates, national exports exceeded by US429.4 million the level registered in the same period last year, evidenced in particular a greater external demand for organic products, as well as the increase in demand for domestic products by Haiti. As for domestic imports, during the period under consideration they registered an increase of 33.4%, reflecting the growth experienced by the economy, as well as higher levels in both prices and demand for fuels. In fact, more than a third of the increase in imports corresponded to the oil bill, which had an increase of US 794.1 million (44.1%) compared to the same period last year. The indicators available to date reflect that tourism has had a positive growth throughout the year, while remittances show a lower level of slowdown than in 2009. In this sense, for tourism from January to September, the country received revenues of US 3,233.8 million, which represents an increase of US 94.4 million (3.0%) compared to the same period last year. In the case of family remittances, the country received US2,177.9 million as of September of this year, just a reduction of US110 million (4.8%) compared to 2009, which is practically offset by the increase in income generated by tourism. This variation in remittances, which from our point of view is not very significant, is not a phenomenon that affects only the Dominican Republic, but is consistent with the labor situation that the United States and Spain, the main countries of destination of Dominican emigrants, are going through. Good news is that a positive result was obtained from the capital and financial account of the Balance of Payments, amounting to US2,711.3 million, equivalent to a growth of 63.5% over the same period last year, all thanks to the significant inflow of foreign capital verified in the form of foreign direct investment. portfolio investment due to the placement of sovereign bonds in international markets, as well as higher disbursements of private loans. Let me briefly make some clarifications about the behaviour of foreign direct investment. In the Dominican case, this type of investment has had a positive evolution, despite the prevailing external environment. I should point out that effective foreign direct investment is close to US2 billion during the period analyzed, about US400 million more than those registered in January-September 2009. Hence, it is necessary to clarify that the apparent reduction of this line reflected in the balance of payments responds to methodological aspects, since an important part of said investment enters accounting through external loans granted to a multinational company based in the country and not with contributions of its investors, reason for which it is registered as portfolio investment, something very similar in the current environment of low interest rates internationally. I think, friends, that I must refer to a variable that, in some way, always generates concern in the economic agents, which is the exchange rate or the premium of giving as it is popularly known. It should be noted that during the period analyzed, relative exchange rate stability prevailed, registering moderate increases in the exchange rate, reaching a depreciation to date of only 3% compared to December 2009, a figure that is below the level of inflation (4.24%), and that places the country in an advantageous situation in terms of competitiveness, in a context in which the other countries of the area are experiencing significant appreciation in their currency. On the other hand, the recent approval of the new Basel III agreements represents a challenge that must be faced by the Monetary and Financial Administration, in order to continue improving the quality of assets and the levels of capitalization weighted by individual and global risks of our entities and the financial markets. In this situation, the recently promulgated Constitution of the Replica assigns a new role to the current functions of the Monetary Board. This role consists of coordinating regulation with the other regulatory and supervisory bodies of the national financial market, which includes, in addition to banking, the areas of securities, pensions and insurance. Under this ethic, efforts are made to facilitate the harmonized design and monitoring of macroprudential indicators that help achieve the stability of this market, with a view to avoiding aggregate systemic risks. Responding to these new guidelines, we are developing several projects that will allow us to adapt to the new standards and fulfill this new constitutional role, among which the revision of the Monetary and Financial Law stands out, as well as the realization of the corresponding regulatory adjustments. In this financial area, it is worth mentioning that significant progress has been made in modernizing the Payment System. Likewise, the Central Bank was chosen by the Central American Monetary Council (CMCA) as Institutional Manager of the Interconnection of Payments System (SIP). In other words, our RTGS System will be the regional payment hub for Central America and Replica Dominicana. On the other hand, it is pertinent to highlight that we have promoted the reform of the check, including the modification of its legal framework, which seeks to establish the norms and standards that must be met in order to facilitate its digitization and truncation, and reduce the risks inherent in the use of this payment instrument. The implementation of a new technological platform, with its center in the Central Bank, will make it possible to reduce transit times to one day, which will constitute a significant advance in favor of banking users. STRATEGIC INSTITUTIONAL VISION Briefly addressing the internal level, allow me to express that after concluding the first complete Strategic Planning exercise in the history of the Institution, carried out during the years 2006  2009, the Monetary Board decided to approve a new Strategic Plan for the Central Bank, to be executed in the period 2010-2013. This new Plan represents a renewal of efforts aimed at placing the Institution at the level of the most important central banks of the region, increasing its productivity and substantially improving its most important capital, the human, as declared by the vision to be achieved in 2013. To this end, a broad set of strategies has been designed to achieve eleven objectives that include the adoption of the inflation targeting scheme, as well as the readjustment of the structure, functionality and key processes of the Bank, in an environment conducive to transparency and accountability. MAIN CHALLENGES FOR THE DOMINICAN ECONOMY Already arriving at the final part of this dissertation, we consider the ocasi and adequate scenario, to refer in a timely manner to some crucial issues for the Dominican economy. Recent experience in the international economy has left many lessons. We have seen how countries that have applied responsible policies, that have saved and maintained a degree of social consensus around macroeconomic stability and the improvement of productive capacities, have managed to overcome the international crisis preserving much of the well-being gained in better times. As we have said on other occasions, macroeconomic stability is essential to promote the sustained growth of an economy such as the Dominican Republic, which due to its basic characteristics of being very small and open, is especially vulnerable to external and internal shocks. You will be and beings, it is simply not possible to aspire to greater job creation, poverty reduction, human and social development, as well as achieve fiscal sustainability, if there is no economic growth. The Managing Director of the IMF, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, has just spoken in the same direction at the recent meeting of the World Bank and the IMF in Washington. I would like to distract your attention from briefly addressing a very important issue concerning whether the current Econico Model is adequate or should be replaced, which has been the subject of debate in recent months, mainly by the various business associations. First of all, it would be worth noting that the aforementioned economic model has allowed an average growth of the Dominican economy of 5.7% between 1995 and 2009, higher than the average of Latin America. As several emerging market analysts have recognized, the result of precisely this above-average growth is that the Dominican Replica, together with Chile, are the countries of the Latin American region that have managed to advance in terms of reducing the per capita income gap in recent decades. I particularly think that Dominicans have an extraordinary capacity for recovery. We demonstrate this after the turbulent financial episodes of 2003-2004, when the economy, after experiencing a recessionary process, managed to grow at an average rate of 7.5% during the period 2005-2009, despite the adverse international environment of scams, being able to achieve the highest growth in Latin America in 2009. In other words, dear friends, in just six years the Gross Domestic Product and GDP per capita in Darfur have more than doubled. This accumulated economic growth has facilitated the reduction of poverty and indigence levels in the country, which increased significantly during the banking crisis, achieving a decrease of 10.2 percentage points compared to the poverty levels recorded in October 2004. Hence, from our humble point of view, it would not seem correct to say that the current economic model has not been instrumental in reducing poverty in the country. In addition, the Dominican Government has used the benefits of growth to improve income distribution, since since 2004 notable efforts have been made through the Single Beneficiary System (SIUBEN), creating social programs to benefit 818,340 low-income families. In the same way, the current economic model has been vital in creating new jobs. The results of the National Labour Force Survey for April 2010 reveal that the expanded unemployment rate stands at 14.4%, which represents a decrease of 5.3 percentage points compared to October 2004. This has been possible thanks to the process of reactivation that the Dominican economy has been registering, as a direct consequence of the correct and timely monetary and fiscal policy decisions. In fact, between 2004 and 2010, 559,235 net new jobs have been created in the country, an average of 93,206 jobs per year, as a result of economic growth and macroeconomic stability during that period. Undoubtedly, this has resulted in a remarkable growth in national per capita income in Darfur, standing at the end of 2009 at US4,815.6, reflecting an improvement in economic well-being during the scams. As for informality, which does not depend exclusively on the economic model but on other factors such as the educational levels of the population and the degree of oversight, the aforementioned survey shows that 56% of employed in the country were informal, meaning a reduction compared to 57.2% existing in October 2009. This phenomenon is not exclusive to our country. For example, Replica Dominicana, along with Mexico, Venezuela and Brazil, is among the Latin American countries with an average level (54-56%) of informal jobs, while countries such as Honduras, Ecuador, Per Colombia and Bolivia are among the economies with the highest level of informality in the region. Therefore, the evidence on poverty reduction and job creation in Replica Dominicana would seem to demonstrate, in our humble understanding, that the Dominican economic model would not exactly need to be replaced. What would be required is a greater emphasis on social investment and refocusing some of the policies that promote greater competitiveness, increased exports and sustainable growth. This adjustment process must reflect the thinking of all levels of our society and consider broad participation to attract the support of all sectors of national life. We are aware that there are major challenges on the national economic agenda. It is no secret to anyone that the electricity issue, fiscal consolidation, the improvement in the quality of social spending  basically in health and education  a greater reduction in poverty through a more equitable distribution of income, institutional strengthening and increasing competitiveness are issues in which we must continue to advance and deepen in favor of its definitive solution. but sustained economic growth will always be necessary as a confeci sine qua non to achieve these objectives, as the IMF's Managing Director has recently seen. It is undeniable that the construction of the infrastructure that demands sustained growth requires large investments that countries like ours cannot self-finance, given the limited domestic savings. Hence the need to address objectively what concerns plic indebtedness, as we did recently when presenting our considerations in an official document, demonstrating with sufficient evidence the sustainability of the current debt resistance. We are convinced that the joint work of the public and private sectors around the great national challenges must be the path to thresh to advance in the construction of the country that we all aspire to. A recent example of this unity of wills, materialize the elaboration of the Project for the development of the mortgage market and trust, which will have a double effect on growth and development, facilitating with innovative financial instruments the access of low-income families to decent housing and boosting the construction industry. One of the highest multiplier impact on the generation of wealth and jobs, in addition to deepening the stock market. Final Thoughts I want to end these words with a reflection on the need to reaffirm the ethical and moral values of the Dominican family. Just a few days ago I participated in an emotional act of the Office of the First Lady, Dr. Margarita Cede de Fernandez, for the launch of a campaign on the most important values of the human being. I confess that I felt very identified with the constructive messages of this happy initiative to redirect the ethical principles of our society. Every day we witness examples of antisocial and anti-value behaviors that are taking place, and that have a harmful influence on the mood of the generations in formation: of the nis and jenes who are growing up. When you have a healthy and growing economy, which creates jobs, positive externalities are generated in the social sphere, which directly influences the spiritual and emotional tranquility of Dominican families, who find in stability the favorable environment to develop fully and promote family ethical values. In that regard, I fully share the call of the philosopher and theologian Hans Kung, President of the World Ethics Foundation, that we need universally shared ethical values, stating that "the economy must function in the service of ethical objectives and be subordinated to the intangible dignity of the human being, guaranteeing his fundamental rights and duties". I humbly believe that Dominicans of good will should put aside our personal desires and think more about the national interest. The time has come for us all to work together for the good of our country, regardless of political banners, religious or philosophical creeds. Let us focus our vision towards progress, emphasizing the ideas and actions that bring us closer, leaving aside those that can divide us. I am truly convinced that we can make progress in building a more equitable society for all and based on values. I end my words, as usual, exhorting you to bet on the future, with faith in God and optimism in a better future! May God bless you all! Thanks a lot.

Este crecimiento econico acumulado ha facilitado la reducci de los niveles de pobreza y la indigencia en el pa<92>s, lo cuales aumentaron significativamente durante la crisis bancaria, logr<87>ndose una disminuci de 10.2 puntos porcentuales respecto de los niveles de pobreza registrados en octubre de 2004. De ah<92> que, desde nuestro humilde punto de vista, no parecer<92>a correcto afirmar que el actual modelo econico no ha sido il para reducir la pobreza en el pa<92>s. En adici, el Gobierno Dominicano ha utilizado los beneficios del crecimiento para mejorar la distribuci del ingreso, pues desde 2004 se han realizado notables esfuerzos a trav<8e>s del Sistema <f2>nico de Beneficiario (SIUBEN), creando programas sociales para beneficiar 818,340 familias de escasos recursos. De la misma manera, el actual modelo econmico ha sido vital para crear nuevos puestos de trabajo. Los resultados de la Encuesta Nacional de Fuerza de Trabajo a abril 2010 revela que la tasa de desocupaci ampliada se situen 14.4%, lo que representa una disminuci de 5.3 puntos porcentuales con respecto a octubre de 2004. Esto ha sido posible gracias al proceso de reactivaci que viene registrando la econom<92>a dominicana, como consecuencia directa de las acertadas y oportunas decisiones de pol<92>tica monetaria y fiscal. De hecho, entre 2004 y 2010 se han creado en el pa<92>s 559,235 nuevos empleos netos, un promedio de 93,206 empleos por a, derivado del crecimiento econico y la estabilidad macroeconica existente en dicho per<92>odo. Sin lugar a dudas, esto se ha traducido en un crecimiento notable del ingreso per-c<87>pita nacional en dares, al situarse al cierre de 2009 en US$4,815.6, reflejando un mejoramiento del bienestar econico durante los timos as. En cuanto a la informalidad, que no depende exclusivamente del modelo econico sino de otros factores como los niveles educativos de la poblaci y el grado de fiscalizaci, la referida Encuesta arrojque el 56% de ocupados en el pa<92>s eran informales, significando una reducci respecto al 57.2% existente a octubre 2009. Este feneno no es exclusivo de nuestro pa<92>s. Por ejemplo, Replica Dominicana, junto a M<8e>xico, Venezuela y Brasil, se ubica entre los pa<92>ses latinoamericanos con un nivel medio (54-56%) de empleos informales, mientras que pa<92>ses como Honduras, Ecuador, Per Colombia y Bolivia se ubican entre las econom<92>as con mayor nivel de informalidad en la regi. Por tanto, la evidencia en materia de reducci de la pobreza y creaci de empleos en Replica Dominicana parecer<92>a demostrar, a nuestro humilde entender, que el modelo econico dominicano no necesitar<92>a precisamente ser sustituido. Lo que se requerir<92>a hacer es un mayor <8e>nfasis en la inversi social y reenfocar algunas de las pol<92>ticas plicas que fomenten mayor competitividad, incremento de las exportaciones y sostenibilidad del crecimiento. Este proceso de ajuste debe reflejar el pensar de todos los estamentos de nuestra sociedad y considerar una amplia participaci para concitar el apoyo de todos los sectores de la vida nacional. Estamos contestes de que existen grandes retos en la agenda econica nacional. Para nadie es un secreto que el tema el<8e>ctrico, la consolidaci fiscal, la mejor<92>a en la calidad del gasto social <d0> b<87>sicamente en salud y educaci-, una mayor disminuci de la pobreza a trav<8e>s de una distribuci m<87>s equitativa del ingreso, el fortalecimiento institucional y aumentar la competitividad son temas en los que debemos seguir avanzando y profundizando en pro de su soluci definitiva, pero siempre ser<87> necesario un crecimiento econico sostenido como una condici sine qua non para alcanzar esos objetivos, como selrecientemente el Director Gerente del FMI. Es innegable que la construcci de la infraestructura que demanda el crecimiento sostenido, requieren de grandes inversiones que pa<92>ses como el nuestro no pueden autofinanciarse, dado el limitado ahorro interno. De ah<92> la necesidad de que se aborde con objetividad, lo concerniente al endeudamiento plico, tal y como lo hicimos recientemente al presentar nuestras consideraciones en un documento oficial, demostrando con suficientes evidencias la sostenibilidad de la deuda plica actual. Estamos convencidos de que el trabajo mancomunado de los sectores plico y privado alrededor de los grandes retos nacionales, debe ser la senda a trillar para avanzar en la construcci del pa<92>s que todos aspiramos. Un ejemplo reciente de esta uni de voluntades, se materializen la elaboraci del Proyecto de desarrollo del mercado hipotecario y fideicomiso, el cual tendr<87> un doble efecto en el crecimiento y en el desarrollo, facilitando con innovadores instrumentos financieros el acceso de familias de bajos ingresos a una vivienda digna e impulsando la industria de la construcci, una de las de m<87>s alto impacto multiplicador en la generaci de riqueza y empleos, adem<87>s de que profundizar<87> el mercado de valores. Reflexiones Finales Quiero terminar estas palabras con una reflexin sobre la necesidad de reafirmar los valores <8e>ticos y morales de la familia dominicana. Hace apenas unos d<92>as particip<8e> en un emotivo acto del Despacho de la Primera Dama, Dra. Margarita Cede de Fern<87>ndez, para el lanzamiento de una campa sobre los m<87>s importantes valores del ser humano. Les confieso que me sent<92> sumamente identificado con los constructivos mensajes de esta feliz iniciativa para reencauzar los principios <8e>ticos de nuestra sociedad. Todos los d<92>as somos testigos de ejemplos de conductas antisociales y antivalores que se est<87>n produciendo, y que influyen nocivamente en el <87>nimo de las generaciones en formaci: de los nis y jenes que vienen creciendo. Cuando se tiene una econom<92>a sana y creciendo, que crea empleos, se generan externalidades positivas en el <87>mbito social, lo que influye directamente en el sosiego espiritual y emocional de las familias dominicanas, que encuentran en la estabilidad el ambiente propicio para desarrollarse <92>ntegramente y promover los valores <8e>ticos familiares. En ese sentido, comparto plenamente el llamamiento del filofo y teogo Hans Kung, Presidente de la Fundaci <83>tica Mundial, de que necesitamos valores <8e>ticos compartidos universalmente, al afirmar que <d2>la econom<92>a debe funcionar al servicio de los objetivos <8e>ticos y subordinarse a la intangible dignidad del ser humano, garantizando sus derechos y deberes fundamentales<d3>. Creo humildemente que los dominicanos de buena voluntad debemos poner a un lado nuestras apetencias personales y pensar m<87>s en el inter<8e>s nacional. Ha llegado la hora de que independientemente de bander<92>as pol<92>ticas, credos religiosos o filosicos, todos trabajemos unidos por el bien com de nuestra patria. Enfoquemos nuestra visi hacia el progreso, haciendo <8e>nfasis en las ideas y acciones que nos acercan, dejando a un lado aquellas que nos pueden dividir. Realmente estoy plenamente convencido de que podemos avanzar en la construcci de una sociedad m<87>s equitativa para todos y cimentada en valores. Finalizo mis palabras, como de costumbre, exhort<87>ndolos a que apostemos al futuro, con fe en Dios y optimismo en un mejor porvenir! <c1>Que Dios los bendiga a todos! Muchas gracias.

text: Firefox about:blank DDiscurso GobernadorPerfilBC As is tradition for the Central Bank, I am pleased tonight to present the institutional profile 2009-2010, which on this occasion has been entitled: "The Central Bank before a new global financial order". This document is our cover letter to economic agents, the financial system, international investors and society in general, which sets out the background, procedures and results of the institution's executions, along with a profile of its authorities and officials. This profile is another example of the institutional commitment to transparency and the fulfillment of our original function of maintaining price stability in a context of openness and accountability. Over the past two decades, the development of central banking around the world has accentuated the relationship between autonomy, accountability and transparency as interdependent processes that determine the behavior of a modern central bank and contribute to the fulfillment of its legal mandate. In the work of monetary policy at the international level, transparency has become an indispensable element for the achievement of monetary policy objectives, as confirmed by a growing body of research. The advance of transparency as an essential characteristic of the exercise of monetary authorities, is not only an international trend but a necessity for the effective exercise of their functions in the face of society. Economic agents are now more aware of the role and importance of central banks in maintaining macroeconomic stability and have greater citizen awareness about the democratization of access to public information. Financial markets have also intensified the use of economic and financial information provided by central banks to support their forecasts and shape their expectations. Since the beginning of our management at the head of this Central Bank, we have assumed a formal, public and inescapable commitment to transparency. This is evidenced by the resumption of the publication of the institutional profile, the constant statistical disclosure on our website, the periodic publication of reports and working papers, the presentation of audited financial statements, monetary policy releases, the opening of our office of free access to public information, among other important initiatives. On this occasion, as you can see, our profile is framed during the period of greatest incidence of the global crisis in 2009 and the beginning of the recovery of the world economy in 2010, facts that constituted the most important challenges for central banks since the Great Depression of the thirties. In this context, the Central Bank, since the beginning of 2009, adopted a set of counter-cyclical measures with the endorsement of the honorable Monetary Board, aimed at increasing the flow of financing to the private sector and reducing financial market interest rates to stimulate domestic demand. These provisions included the reduction of the monetary policy interest rate, the relaxation of certain banking rules, the temporary closure of the direct placement window to the public, the reduction of the percentage and release of resources from the legal reserve, which made available to the main sectors of the economy more than RD 21 billion between 2009 and 2010. As a result of these measures, consolidated credit to the private sector rebounded from the second quarter of 2009, increasing by more than RD73 billion during 2010. Financial market interest rates also hit record lows over the past year in response to the central bank's policy signal. This process of monetary easing, together with the fiscal impulse after the signing with the IMF, allowed the country to successfully overcome the effects of the global crisis without losing macroeconomic stability, achieving growth of 3.5% in 2009, the highest in Latin America in that year, and 16/11/2022 19:14 1 sur 2 Firefox about:blank a real GDP expansion of 7.8% in 2010. A more detailed description of the background, evolution and effects of the international financial crisis on the Dominican economy is presented in the first chapter of this profile. Ladies and gentlemen, certainly, the solidity of the Dominican financial system after the lessons learned from the banking crisis of 2003 and the resulting financial reform, allowed the country to avoid external contagion with toxic assets and intensify its role as a channeler of resources to the national productive sectors. However, the opposite happened with international banking, particularly in the United States, which experienced a systematic process of deregulation since the late nineties, weakening prudential supervision and risk management. This fact has been pointed out by many experts as one of the main causes of the global crisis. Under the leadership of the G-20, the international financial system has embarked on a process of reform with the aim of designing a New International Financial Architecture. These issues are addressed in the second chapter of the profile, emphasizing the challenges they represent for monetary policy. The aim of this analysis is to introduce readers to the international debate on the perspectives of financial regulation processes. In this area, priority is given to the creation of adequate mechanisms that guarantee liquidity management focused on minimizing risks and preventing future crises. This new world economic order also implies a redistribution of economic power where emerging economies assume a role of great impact on the dynamics of world markets, as has already been manifested in the reform process of the Board of the International Monetary Fund. The Central Bank has also made significant progress in terms of integration with the rest of the region. For this reason, the third chapter of this document is entitled "The Central Bank of the Dominican Republic and Regional Integration", which describes the institution's participation in the negotiations of free trade agreements on services and investment issues. Finally, chapter four refers to "Advances in institutional development to face the new global financial order". It is clear that the financial crisis highlighted the need for monetary policymakers and financial regulators to gather managerial and institutional capacities to monitor indicators, increase efficiency and reduce risks, especially those associated with payment systems and financial stability. This section presents institutional progress in operational, management and governance matters. In short, distinguished friends, colleagues and officials, with the presentation of our institutional profile 2009-2010, the Central Bank seeks once again to keep economic agents and the general public informed about the achievements of the monetary authorities. In it, we offer a comprehensive vision of the prospects of the Dominican economy and the international environment, making known the officials who with their work and leadership contribute daily to the achievement of our institutional objectives. Before concluding my remarks, I wish to reiterate the commitment of the Central Bank and its authorities to macroeconomic stability and the control of inflation, non-negotiable responsibilities for this management, assuming them as our best contribution to Dominican society and to the normal development of economic activities, which guarantee growth with stability. Thanks a lot. 16/11/2022 19:14 2 of 2
