Title: Speech on the occasion of the 65th Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: SPEECH COMMEMORATING THE 65TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC. OCTOBER 23, 2012 Hector Valdez Albizu Governor 65 years ago, a memorable day like today, October 23, the issuing and governing body of Monetary, Financial and Exchange Policies was created in the Dominican Republic by constitutional mandate, through Law 15-47. As we commemorate a new anniversary of the Central Bank, addressing all of you in my capacity as Governor for the fifteenth time, dear Bancentralian friends, truly fills me with indescribable and profound emotion. On this occasion, I would like to express my gratitude to His Excellency the President of the Republic, Mr. Danilo Medina, for the trust placed in me by confirming me in such a high position. For those who speak to you, it is a sacred commitment before God and Dominican society to continue honoring with our best efforts this great responsibility that I have assumed. Certainly words are short to testify, that without the solidarity love of my family, and especially of my selfless mother, who supports me in every moment of my existence; As well as without the unconditional support of my close collaborators and all the staff of this institution, it would not be possible to accomplish the arduous task of contributing modestly to preserving macroeconomic stability and promoting growth in line with the best national interests. With humility I want to recognize before you, dear colleagues, that it is a high honor for me to belong for almost four decades to the Central Bank, whose mystique based on excellence, ethics and transparency, constitute without a doubt its best banner. On this occasion, our anniversary coincides with the discussion of transcendental economic issues, such as the Comprehensive Fiscal Reform and the possibility of a new Agreement with the International Monetary Fund, an opportune moment to share, as has been tradition on this date, some considerations that could be of interest to economic agents, the international community and public opinion in general. INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENT The international economic environment continues to face serious challenges. Every day we receive news of the fragile recovery of the United States (USA), the strong recession that Europe is experiencing and the slowdown of economies that until recently, were the engine of the world economy, as is the case of China. In fact, my friends, the IMF recently lowered its global growth projections for 2012 from 3.5% to 3.3%. The United States, our main trading partner, with an estimated growth of just 2.2% for 2012, continues to adopt measures aimed at reactivating its economy and creating new jobs, such as the announcement of the maintenance of the monetary policy rate between 0% and 0.25% until 2015 and the monthly purchase of US 40 billion in mortgage assets. In the old continent, the economic and fiscal problems of several of the countries that make up the Eurozone, keep these economies in recession and with high unemployment rates, constituting a threat to international financial stability, forcing them to adopt strong adjustment measures. With regard to Latin America and the Caribbean, the latest projections estimate economic growth of 3.2% for this year, lower than the 3.4% revealed in July by the IMF, mainly explained by the slowdown in Brazil and Argentina. Today, the main international forums are discussing whether expansionary or fiscal adjustment policies should be applied. Apparently, the trend would seem to be towards a combination of loose monetary policy with fiscal adjustment that does not harm growth and employment, but in turn reduces public debt over the medium term. In the midst of this adverse international environment, there are many risks and vulnerabilities faced by developing economies such as the Dominican Republic. However, this horizon highlights opportunities that we must take advantage of bearing in mind our foundations and promoting a country-strategy that maximizes our potential and that enables the legitimate aspiration for greater socio-economic equity, to which our Excellency the President of the Republic, Mr. Danilo Medina, referred before the recent Assembly of the United Nations. stressing the need for "the economy to be at the service of the people" and therefore, economic growth to translate into human development. RECENT OVERVIEW OF THE DOMINICAN ECONOMY I wish to take advantage of this select audience to present to the country the scoop that the Dominican economy in the period January-September 2012, measured through the Gross Domestic Product in real terms, experienced according to figures still very preliminary to date, a growth of 3.9%, behavior that could well be considered satisfactory, taking into account the slowdown in domestic demand associated with the uncertainty generated by the pre and post electoral period. This performance of economic activity, dear friends, has been achieved with accumulated inflation, measured by the variation of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), of just 2.37% during the period January-September 2012. Preliminary figures for the external sector in the first nine months of the year show that the Dominican Republic's current account deficit has narrowed by US117.4 million, mainly due to lower growth in total imports, which barely grew 1.9%. Of the total domestic imports, about 27% corresponded to the oil bill, which continues to have a high impact on the result of the current account, amounting to US 3,572.6 million, or US 127.4 million above the level of 2011. On the other hand, total exports registered an increase of US 139.8 million compared to the same period of 2011, explained mainly by free zones, which grew 4.3%, coffee, and the performance of minor products, which have registered flows close to US 1,900 million so far this year. Similarly, the tourism sector continues to maintain its dynamism despite the difficult international situation. The arrival of tourists grew 7.3%, equivalent to an increase of about 240,000 travelers compared to January-September last year, to reach about 3.5 million tourists. Likewise, tourism revenues grew by 5.7%, a lower rate than the arrival of passengers due to the decrease in the average stay, particularly of European tourists. However, its contribution in foreign currency meant US 189.2 million above the same period last year. With regard to remittances, they amounted to US2,247.2 million, corresponding to a decrease of -3.9% (US91.0 million). This behavior is similar to that recorded by remittances in several Latin American countries this year, such as Costa Rica (-4.4%), Colombia (-0.9%) and Ecuador (-9.2%), among others. However, we estimate that we will end 2012 with levels close to last year. Foreign direct investment reached US2,859.4 million in the period, an increase of US960.8 million over the same period in 2011, a real feat considering the uncertain global context. These new investments in the country show greater diversification, as they are mainly destined to the sectors: mining, commerce, electricity, real estate and free zones. ROLE OF MONETARY POLICY With regard to monetary policy, during the first half of the year the Dominican economy was characterized by low inflationary pressures and a level of production below its potential capacity. In this context, the Central Bank decided to modify its monetary stance, reducing its policy rate from 6.75% to 5.0%, between May and August 2012, as other countries in the region have been doing. This reduction of 175 basis points has begun to have an impact on a gradual decrease in interest rates in the financial market, which will favor the reactivation of credit. On the other hand, according to information from the Superintendency of Banks and the Department of Regulation and Financial Stability of this Central Bank, the financial sector shows robust management indicators at the end of September: The liquidity index was 32.3%; the profitability of the average equity of multiple banks reached 18.7%; while the solvency ratio of financial intermediaries was 17.6%. This confirms that the financial sector continues to be a fundamental axis for the stability and good development of the Dominican economy, being positioned favorably by the main risk rating agencies. TOWARDS A NEW AGREEMENT WITH THE IMF I think that this moment, when we have to report on the results of the economy, is a good opportunity to reflect and present some considerations about the future of our economy, particularly about our relations with the IMF. As everyone knows, in the last eight years, the Dominican Republic had two Stand-By Agreements with the Fund. In both programmes, significant progress was made in the areas of macroeconomic, financial and structural reforms. Currently, the Dominican Authorities are aware that the risks and vulnerabilities facing the Dominican economy, given the international environment and fiscal conditions, represent an enormous challenge for the country. For this reason, I fully agree with the position of the President of the Republic and the Economic Team, that it is necessary to consider signing a new agreement with the IMF, which supports the Government's efforts to balance its budget through a set of medium-term measures that sustain macroeconomic stability and allow access to capital markets. I take this opportunity to inform you that the IMF mission will arrive in the country this coming November 5 to complete the visit of Article IV of its Articles of Agreement, which is nothing more than the periodic, generally annual, consultations carried out by that organization bilaterally with its member countries, in order to examine the situation and the economic policies adopted by the latter. On this occasion, a post-program monitoring will also be carried out, contemplated at the end of the last agreement. This visit will be conducive to initiating formal talks in order to negotiate a new Stand-by. ACHIEVEMENTS As part of the permanent improvement of the economic statistics produced by this Central Bank, I wish to announce that next November we will present to the country and the international community, the results of the change of base year of the National Accounts of the Dominican Republic. The new base year of the Gross Domestic Product will be 2007, which was selected for being a year of recovery and macroeconomic stability. The completion of this project has been the result of an arduous work of more than four years carried out by national and international technical specialists experts in the field, for the application of best practices and methodological recommendations updated worldwide. There is currently an international trend to promote policies to increase financial inclusion. In this regard, the Monetary Board drafted the Microcredit Regulations to regulate the granting of credit to microenterprises and entrepreneurs. It also completed the Banking Sub-Agent Regulation, which will allow financial services to be taken to the most remote parts of the country, as well as the issuance of recently approved prepaid cards. Both projects are in the process of consultation and discussion, that is, available for comments, prior to their final approval. YEAR-END OUTLOOK FOR 2012 AND 2013 As is customary in this dissertation, I would like to refer briefly at this time to the prospects for the end of this year. Even with the difficulties we face, our economy will grow in 2012 around 4.0%, maintaining inflation levels close to 4.5%. In turn, Foreign Direct Investment will reach historic levels that will exceed US 3,000 million. This behavior of the real sector and the external accounts should continue in 2013, once the comprehensive tax reform is implemented and an agreement is reached with the International Monetary Fund. FINAL THOUGHTS Allow me, ladies and gentlemen, to express some points of view on the Tax Reform that is currently being discussed. Although this issue is not directly related to the functions inherent to the Central Bank, its importance affects all sectors of the economy, including the monetary sector, so I consider it pertinent to share with you some assessments, by way of reflection, on this process. To address the current situation of fiscal deficit, President Danilo Medina has proposed a comprehensive reform that has undergone a process of consultation with society, in which he contemplates a cut in spending and a tax reform that would increase collections. This reform would reduce the fiscal deficit, while allowing the implementation of a broad social investment program, while complying with the allocation of 4% of GDP to education. Personally, I am convinced that, by taking the appropriate measures in the shortest possible time, this problem would be overcome in two or three years, as other countries have done. I believe that these measures should be complemented by the strengthening of institutions related to fiscal enforcement in the country. In this sense, it would be advisable to design and implement a fiscal rule, which guarantees sustainability and avoids future deviations in budget execution. I know that the measures proposed in the Reform are not sympathetic, and that not all sectors can be pleased. Personally, I am convinced that in the face of this reality, if Dominicans fold our arms and put aside the search for a definitive solution to the fiscal deficit, we would be acting irresponsibly, sowing the seeds of a future deterioration of macroeconomic conditions and the loss of stability in the Dominican Republic. Dominicans have become accustomed to living with stability. In this regard, I take this opportunity to reiterate to those who have tried to "fish in troubled rivers", with the idea of hoarding foreign currency for speculative purposes with the aim of altering the normal behavior of the exchange market, that the Central Bank maintains an unavoidable commitment to the relative stability of the exchange rate and is willing to take the necessary measures to avoid unwanted movements of this variable so sensitive to the economic agents and the general public for its harmful effects on price stability. We are definitely facing a future that presents us as a nation with an enormous challenge. Therefore, I think that we must give a vote of confidence to President Danilo Medina, because although many could disagree with his reform proposal, we must recognize that he has courageously and responsibly assumed an enormous political cost at the beginning of his government, in order to seek a permanent solution to the fiscal problem. As Madame Lagarde recently said in her speech at the IMF's annual meeting in Tokyo: "The road before us is narrow and long. The key now is to move from deliberation to action to implement the policies we know are necessary, and move forward together on all fronts." Friends, despite the fact that today the Dominican economy faces an international environment that does not favor it and is at the door of a new fiscal reform, I am convinced that we will move forward and we should not be afraid of the future because the foundations of our economy are healthy. I invite you not to let ourselves be overwhelmed by uncertainty and pessimism. There is the capacity, the determination and the political will so that, with a joint effort between the public and private sectors, we can emerge successfully from this trance, as we have done in the past, in the face of more complex challenges. I do not want to miss this opportunity, to appeal to economic agents, representatives of the public and private sectors and other entities of civil society, to act sensibly and prudently in this search for a concerted action aimed at solving in the medium term a core issue such as the fiscal one. In a spirit of conciliation, let us put aside differences at this time, work together and guide our best abilities to preserve macroeconomic stability and social peace for all Dominicans. Let us therefore support the reform proposal of President Danilo Medina, who has shown ample integrity and that he will administer the National Budget with strict austerity and rationality in public spending, respecting the proper ordering of the market, in accordance with the institutional canons that regulate economic activity. I conclude my words, as usual, exhorting you to bet on the future, with faith in God and optimism in a better future. May God bless you all! Thanks a lot.

En esta oportunidad se realizar<87> adem<87>s un monitoreo post-programa, contemplado al finalizar el <9c>ltimo acuerdo. Esta visita ser<87> propicia para iniciar las conversaciones formales de cara a negociar un nuevo Stand-by. LOGROS Como parte del mejoramiento permanente de las estad<92>sticas econ<97>micas que produce este Banco Central, tengo a bien anunciarles que en el pr<97>ximo mes de noviembre presentaremos al pa<92>s y a la comunidad internacional, los resultados del cambio de a<96>o base de las Cuentas Nacionales de la Rep<9c>blica Dominicana. El nuevo a<96>o base del Producto Interno Bruto ser<87> el 2007, el cual fue seleccionado por ser un a<96>o de recuperaci<97>n y estabilidad macroecon<97>mica. La finalizaci<97>n de este proyecto ha sido fruto de un arduo trabajo de m<87>s de cuatro a<96>os realizado por t<8e>cnicos especialistas nacionales e internacionales expertos en la materia, para la aplicaci<97>n de las mejores pr<87>cticas y recomendaciones metodol<97>gicas actualizadas a nivel mundial. Actualmente existe una tendencia internacional de fomentar pol<92>ticas para incrementar la inclusi<97>n financiera. En tal sentido, la Junta Monetaria elabor<97> el Reglamento de Microcr<8e>dito para normar el otorgamiento de cr<8e>dito a las microempresas y emprendedores. Asimismo, complet<97> el Reglamento de Subagente Bancario, que permitir<87> llevar los servicios financieros hasta los lugares m<87>s rec<97>nditos del pa<92>s, al igual que la emisi<97>n de tarjetas pre-pagadas aprobadas recientemente. Ambos proyectos se encuentran en proceso de consulta y discusi<97>n, vale decir disponibles para comentarios, previo a su aprobaci<97>n definitiva. PERSPECTIVAS DE CIERRE DE 2012 Y 2013 Como es costumbre en esta disertaci<97>n, quiero referirme brevemente en estos momentos, a las perspectivas de cierre del presente a<96>o. A<9c>n con las dificultades que enfrentamos, nuestra econom<92>a crecer<87> en 2012 en torno a 4.0%, manteniendo niveles de inflaci<97>n cercanos a 4.5%. A su vez, la Inversi<97>n Extranjera Directa alcanzar<87> niveles hist<97>ricos que superar<87>n los US$3,000 millones. Este comportamiento del sector real y de las cuentas externas deber<87> continuar en 2013, una vez se implemente la reforma tributaria integral y se logre un acuerdo con el Fondo Monetario Internacional. REFLEXIONES FINALES Perm<92>tanme, se<96>oras y se<96>ores, externar algunos puntos de vista sobre la Reforma Fiscal que se discute actualmente. Aunque este tema no se relaciona directamente con las funciones inherentes al Banco Central, su trascendencia afecta a todos los sectores de la econom<92>a, incluyendo al sector monetario, por lo que considero pertinente compartir con ustedes algunas apreciaciones, a manera de reflexi<97>n, sobre este proceso. Para enfrentar la situaci<97>n actual de d<8e>ficit fiscal, el Presidente Danilo Medina ha propuesto una reforma integral que ha sometido a un proceso de consulta con la sociedad, en la que contempla un recorte del gasto y una reforma tributaria que incrementar<92>a las recaudaciones. Esta reforma reducir<92>a el d<8e>ficit fiscal, a la vez que permitir<92>a implementar un amplio programa de inversi<97>n social, cumpliendo a su vez con la asignaci<97>n del 4% del PIB a la educaci<97>n. Personalmente, estoy convencido de que, tomando las medidas adecuadas en el menor tiempo posible, este problema ser<92>a superado en dos o tres a<96>os, como lo han hecho otros pa<92>ses. Estimo que estas medidas deber<92>an complementarse con el fortalecimiento de las instituciones relacionadas con la ejecuci<97>n fiscal en el pa<92>s. En ese sentido, ser<92>a recomendable el dise<96>o e implementaci<97>n de una regla fiscal, que garantice la sostenibilidad y evite futuros desv<92>os en la ejecuci<97>n presupuestaria. S<8e> que las medidas propuestas en la Reforma no son simp<87>ticas, y que no se puede complacer a todos los sectores. Personalmente estoy convencido, que ante esta realidad, si los dominicanos nos cruzamos de brazos y dejamos de lado la b<9c>squeda de una soluci<97>n definitiva al d<8e>ficit fiscal, estar<92>amos actuando de manera irresponsable, sembrando la semilla de un futuro deterioro de las condiciones macroecon<97>micas y la p<8e>rdida de la estabilidad en la Republica Dominicana. Los dominicanos nos hemos acostumbrado a vivir con estabilidad. Sobre este particular aprovecho la oportunidad para reiterarles a aquellos que han pretendido <d2>pescar en r<92>o revuelto<d3>, con idea de atesorar divisas con fines especulativos con el objetivo de alterar el normal comportamiento del mercado cambiario, que el Banco Central mantiene un compromiso ineludible con la estabilidad relativa de la tasa de cambio y est<87> dispuesto a tomar las medidas que sean necesarias para evitar movimientos no deseados de esta variable tan sensible para los agentes econ<97>micos y el p<9c>blico en general por sus efectos perniciosos sobre la estabilidad de precios. Definitivamente estamos de cara a un futuro que nos presenta como naci<97>n un enorme reto. Por tanto pienso que debemos darle un voto de confianza al Presidente Danilo Medina, pues aunque muchos podr<92>an disentir con su propuesta de Reforma, hay que reconocer que de forma valiente y responsable ha asumido un enorme costo pol<92>tico al inicio de su gobierno, en aras de buscar una soluci<97>n permanente a la problem<87>tica fiscal. Como dijera recientemente Madame Lagarde, en su discurso pronunciado en la reuni<97>n anual del FMI en Tokio:<d2>El camino que tenemos ante nosotros es angosto y largo. La clave ahora es pasar de la deliberaci<97>n a la acci<97>n para aplicar las pol<92>ticas que sabemos son necesarias, y avanzar juntos en todos los frentes.<d3> Amigos, a pesar de que hoy la econom<92>a dominicana enfrenta un entorno internacional que no le favorece y est<87> a la puerta de una nueva reforma fiscal, estoy convencido de que saldremos adelante y no debemos tener miedo al porvenir pues los fundamentos de nuestra econom<92>a son sanos. Les invito a no dejarnos abrumar por la incertidumbre y el pesimismo. Existe la capacidad, la decisi<97>n y la voluntad pol<92>tica para que, con un esfuerzo mancomunado entre el sector p<9c>blico y el privado, salgamos airosos de este trance, como lo hemos hecho en el pasado, ante retos m<87>s complejos. No quiero dejar pasar esta oportunidad, para hacer un llamado a los agentes econ<97>micos, a los representantes de los sectores p<9c>blico y privado y dem<87>s entes de la sociedad civil, en el sentido de que actuemos con sensatez y prudencia en esta b<9c>squeda de una concertaci<97>n encaminada a solucionar en el mediano plazo un tema medular como lo es el fiscal. Con un esp<92>ritu conciliador, dejemos de lado en estos momentos las diferencias, trabajemos unidos y orientemos nuestras mejores capacidades en preservar la estabilidad macroecon<97>mica y la paz social de todos los dominicanos. Apoyemos pues la propuesta de reforma del Presidente Danilo Medina, quien ha dado amplias muestras de integridad y de que administrar<87> el Presupuesto Nacional con estricta austeridad y racionalidad en el gasto p<9c>blico, respetando el adecuado ordenamiento del mercado, con apego a los c<87>nones institucionales que regulan la actividad econ<97>mica. Finalizo mis palabras, como de costumbre, exhort<87>ndolos a que apostemos al futuro, con fe en Dios y optimismo en un mejor porvenir. <c1>Que Dios los bendiga a todos! Muchas gracias.

Title: Speech at the opening ceremony of the exhibition commemorating the bicentennial of the birth of Juan Pablo Duarte
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Remarks by Mr. Hector Valdez Albizu, Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, at the opening ceremony of the exhibition commemorating the bicentennial of the birth of Juan Pablo Duarte [1813-2013], in the lobby of the Numismatic and Philatelic Museum, on Tuesday, January 22, 2013. We are gathered here, with the pleasant company of all of you, whom I am pleased to welcome, to commemorate, with a representative sample, the celebration of the two hundred years of the birth of General Juan Pablo Duarte, Father of the Nation and symbol of the purest ideals. The Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, following a long tradition of honoring the figure of the illustrious patrician, opens today an exhibition in his memory, with numismatic and philatelic pieces of high symbolic value, books, sculptures, portraits and other allegorical objects. In August of last year, the Central Bank made its first contribution to the bicentennial of Duarte's birth, by putting into circulation, ahead of this memorable date, a key book, entitled Duarte revisited [1813-2013], which brings together original essays written especially for this work by five distinguished Dominican historians: Juan Daniel Balcacer, Jose Chez Checo, Orlando Inoa, Jose Miguel Soto Jimenez and Jorge Tena Reyes, who did their research independently and worked their texts with absolute intellectual freedom, with commendable results, collected in a book that since then is available to the interested public. On this work, I am pleased to announce that, as an additional contribution from the Central Bank, Duarte revisited [1813-2013] has been placed on the institution's website, for consultation by all those who wish to do so. The veneration for the memory of the Father of the Nation is a very old issue in the Central Bank, whose library bears his name, so, over many decades, we have tried to consecrate his memory among the young generations, with the issuance of coins and banknotes that bear his effigy, with commemorative exhibitions and publication of several books that enrich the national bibliography. Juan Pablo Duarte y Diez was born in Santo Domingo, on January 26, 1813, in the bosom of a large family procreated by the Spanish citizen Don Juan Jose Duarte and the Dominican Dona Manuela Diez. When Juan Pablo was still a child, the Ephemeral Independence took place, proclaimed in 1821 by Don Jose Nunez de Caceres; but the following year a fateful event took place: the Haitian occupation of Dominican territory, which was to last for twenty-two long years, a period in which it was uselessly intended to modify the idiosyncrasy of our people. Duarte was touched, dear officials and friends, an adolescence populated by shadows, so to speak, in which his patriotic aspirations to see his homeland free and sovereign from all foreign interference were germinating. This became evident after his experience as a traveler in the United States, England, France and especially Spain, when he was still a boy, sent by his father with a view to strengthening his education. In the Old World, between 1829 and 1832, Duarte assimilated the libertarian ideas that circulated everywhere in Spain, where the expulsion of the Napoleonic army had taken place, ending French domination in Spanish territory. Revolutionary winds were blowing that impacted the spirit of the teenager, who on his return to Santo Domingo began to work on his independence project, founding the clandestine society La Trinitaria with a group of young friends, idealists and romantics like him, until the proclamation of National Independence on February 27, 1844. The life of Duarte, my friends, from that decisive year of our Independence, was not the life of a hero, but that of an outlaw, product of an unjustified exile to which the government of General Pedro Santana subjected him. Twenty years later, that is, in 1864, in the midst of the restorative war, he interrupted his silence when he came to put himself under the orders of the revolutionary government that was fighting against Spanish domination, although he only received indifference and the disdainful treatment of some restorative leaders. Thus, his stay on our island was fleeting and soon he had to return to Venezuela, where he spent the last decades of his existence, surviving thanks to the modest business of a candle factory. Poor and in the most absolute anonymity, he died in Caracas on July 15, 1876. The truth is that, dear guests and friends, there is no example in national history of detachment as noble as that of Juan Pablo Duarte, liberator of the Dominicans, who never claimed for himself the laurels he deserved. He lived away from the heat of the country's political struggles, alone, sad and disappointed, renouncing the power and glory he had won in a good fight. But the ambitions, political intrigues and envy of certain individuals stood in the way of his star shining in all its glory. Today, two hundred years after his birth, we must rescue the integral Duarte  the inspirer, the fighter, the paradigm of selfless patriotism  so that his ideology, his integrity at all times and his nobility continue to encourage our people and their rulers in the search for a better country, and that his example of honesty without blemishes, and their altruism become guides to personal conduct and collective action. The exhibition that we will soon see is a modest contribution of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic to the exaltation of the Father of the Nation, Juan Pablo Duarte, on the bicentennial of his birth. Thank you for your honorable presence and for sharing with us the pride of being Dominicans and spiritual children of the most illustrious patrician of the nation. Thank you very much and good evening.

Title: Speech on the 66th Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: For those who speak to you, it is a high honor to address all of you, as we commemorate a new anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic. I believe that in this 66-year passing, we have reached sufficient institutional maturity to continue to respond efficiently to the various challenges inherent in an increasingly interconnected, dynamic and complex economy. I confess that I am deeply grateful to God, who has guided my steps in this service that I am providing to my country from the Governorship of the Central Bank, and to have the privilege of having magnificent officials and technicians, who with their dedication, loyalty and ability, have been extraordinary collaborators to carry out this arduous task. But just as important as the first thing has been for me the support, commitment and dedication of the honorable members of the Monetary Board, who have courageously taken up the challenges we have faced together. I have also been fortunate to have the unconditional support of my family: my wife Fior and my son Hector Manuel, who have borne all the weight that comes with daily life, to fulfill this great responsibility. Thank you from the bottom of my heart. You have been my support and sustenance in the most difficult times, the true support in times of storm. Undoubtedly, the constitutional autonomy consecrated to this Issuing Entity since 1947, the permanent professionalization and adherence to good practices, as well as the adoption of the monetary policy scheme based on Inflation Targets since January 2012, constitute key foundations in the preservation of price stability set forth in our Magna Carta, A sine qua non for a climate conducive to growth, savings, consumption and investment. After the global financial crisis that erupted in 2008, the longest and deepest in the last eighty years, an interesting debate on the role of central banks has resurfaced internationally. In addition to their essential objective related to price stability and ensuring the proper functioning of the payment system, they are being assigned other no less important functions, such as ensuring financial and exchange rate stability, financial market coordination and macro-prudential policy design, as well as contributing to a sustained level of economic growth. All of the above acquires greater relevance, if we take into account the consequences and challenges that remain today, as a horizon of gradual recovery is envisioned. INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENT Indeed, friends, in the international arena the various forecasts for next year 2014 are more auspicious than those of the current year, where the world economy continues to exhibit a slow recovery, particularly in developed nations, as well as slowdowns and volatilities in most emerging countries, especially in the so-called BRICS (Brazil, Spain, China Russia, India, China and South Africa). In that vein, just a few days ago, in the latest revision of the World Economic Outlook (WEO), the IMF projected global growth of 2.9% for 2013, raising it to 3.6% for 2014. In the case of the United States of America, our main trading partner, there are improvements in the labor market and a recovery in important economic activities, estimating a growth of 1.6% for this year and 2.6% for 2014. These projections have been strengthened with the recent agreement between the congressmen that will allow the US Government to continue operating normally in the remainder of the year, giving the economic authorities of that country a waiting time to achieve a definitive agreement at the beginning of next year. As for the old continent, although the growth projection for the Euro Zone is -0.4% for 2013 and high unemployment rates prevail, there are signs of recovery, registering many of the 16/11/2022 19:14 the new srri i o eel23 , eel66AniveersariodeelBanco CeentraldeelaDominican Republic 3120eddreubbctoedd Its economies performed positively in the second quarter of this year, estimating growth of 1% for 2014. For emerging economies, the most recent IMF projections call for growth of 4.5% for this year and a rebound of 5.1% for 2014. In the Latin American region, the IMF's latest growth forecast for Latin America and the Caribbean is 2.7% for 2013, rising to 3.1% for next year. As can be seen, dear friends, today more than ever economic policymakers, in addition to the analysis of the domestic situation, are called upon to constantly monitor the international environment for its appreciable impact, mainly in small and open economies such as the Dominican Republic, in order to adopt in a timely manner the measures that are necessary to prevent and mitigate the vulnerabilities and risks that have prevailed in recent times. And although we reaffirmed this approach in the monthly monetary policy communiques of the Central Bank, I have allowed, because it is a tradition of this discourse, to synthesize some of the most relevant aspects of Dominican economic work so far this year. ROLE OF MONETARY POLICY IN 2013 In this context, during 2013 a proactive and timely monetary policy was adopted to face adverse shocks and shocks of internal and external origin. As everyone knows, in the first quarter there was a significant slowdown in economic activity, with output growing only 0.3% in that period. This result was influenced by a process of fiscal consolidation, which included a significant reduction in public spending, especially on investment works, within the framework of the recent tax reform. In these conditions of weak aggregate demand and absence of inflationary pressures, the fiscal and monetary authorities coordinated a set of provisions to reactivate the economy, in which context the Government, headed by His Excellency the President of the Republic, Mr. Danilo Medina Sanchez, announced several actions aimed at boosting public investment, agricultural production and financing aimed at SMEs. in order to contribute to the generation of employment. In the field of monetary policy, as became public knowledge, the Central Bank implemented a series of expansionary measures that included: (1) The liberalization of RD 20 billion of the legal reserve resources of the financial system, to be channeled mainly to the productive sectors, at a fixed rate of 9.0% for 6 years; (2) the relaxation of requirements to improve access to credit for child debtors; and (3) the reduction by 75 basis points of the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR), from 5.0% to 4.25%. As expected, these monetary stimuli had a significant impact on the dynamization of bank credit. To illustrate this statement, it is worth highlighting the fact that between May and September, 80% of the total amount to be liberalized was channeled, that is, about RD 16,175 million, benefiting about 10,219 users, receiving the manufacturing industry about RD 4,600 million, the housing sector about RD 3,675 million, commerce and MSMEs about RD 3,200 million, agriculture also about RD 3,200 million and consumption around RD 1,500 million. Moreover, measures such as these have the virtue of boosting private sector financing beyond the initial amount of funds released, with what we call a spillover effect. In this way, credit expanded even in sectors that were not directly covered by the allocation of these resources, resulting in higher than estimated credit growth. To give you a better idea of the effectiveness of the decisions taken, it is appropriate to analyse the evolution of credit to the private sector in national currency so far this year, from 1 January to mid-October. In that period, these loans have increased by approximately RD 42,500 million, that is, 22 times more than the increase experienced in the same period last year, which was only RD 1,871 million. Now, if we measure the credit expansion in the period September 2012-September 2013, we verify a growth of more than 15%, an increase of RD 61,500 million, an amount almost 5 times greater than the total placed a year earlier in the same period. As can be seen, these data show that the flow of credit is moving in line with the reactivation of productive activities. Another variable that reflects the effectiveness in the conduct of monetary policy, is the level of accumulated inflation of 3.57% in the January-September period, and annualized inflation, measured from September 2012 to September 2013, was 5.13%. This low level of inflation, which is located within the 16/11/2022 19:14 The target range foreseen in the monetary program was highlighted by the IMF in its recent Country Monitoring Report. Also during the year, liquidity in the financial system has continued to grow as foreseen in the Monetary Programme. Specifically, as of September, banknotes and coins issued and the circulating medium (M1) grew in year-on-year terms by around 10% and 8.0%, respectively, rates consistent with the expected behavior of nominal GDP for 2013. However, between June and August of this year, several factors caused significant exchange rate volatility, despite the fact that there were no significant deviations in fiscal and monetary variables from what was programmed to justify such behavior, and the monetary authorities were compelled to review their policy stance. With the announcement that the withdrawal of Federal Reserve stimulus would begin, the reversal of capital flows from emerging economies to the United States of America intensified. To appreciate the magnitude of this reversal, only in the first seven months of the year, capital left emerging countries for more than US 102 billion, registering strong depreciations in the currencies of the Latin American region. Aunque hemos tenido que revestirnos de la armadura de que nos habla Efesios 6 en su vers<92>culo 10 en las Sagradas Escrituras, para con la paciencia de Job resistir los dardos provenientes de distintas direcciones, concentramos nuestros esfuerzos en dar cumplimiento al mandato Constitucional de velar por la estabilidad de precios de nuestra econom<92>a, ya que la in<df>aci<97>n es el <df>agelo que m<87>s afecta a los asalariados y a los grandes conglomerados sociales del pueblo dominicano. SECTOR REAL Perm<92>tanme ahora, como es ya una costumbre en cada aniversario, darles la primicia sobre el 16/11/2022 19:14 comportamiento de la econom<92>a dominicana correspondiente al per<92>odo enero-septiembre de este a<96>o 2013. En esta ocasi<97>n, los resultados del crecimiento econ<97>mico re<df>ejan que las decisiones adoptadas de manera coordinada entre las pol<92>ticas <de>scal y monetaria, surtieron efectos muy positivos. Como ustedes recordar<87>n a principios de a<96>o, la econom<92>a apenas creci<97> en 0.3% en enero-marzo, repuntando en 2.8% en el trimestre abril-junio, lo que permiti<97> un crecimiento acumulado de 1.6% en el primer semestre del presenta a<96>o. La notable recuperaci<97>n en este trimestre est<87> explicada mayormente por el dinamismo de sectores claves de la econom<92>a, como son agropecuario 8.3%, construcci<97>n 8.6%, y otros como hoteles, bares y restaurantes e intermediaci<97>n <de>nanciera y seguros que reportan cifras de dos d<92>gitos. Con este resultado, la econom<92>a dominicana, medida a trav<8e>s del PIB en t<8e>rminos reales durante el per<92>odo enero-septiembre, presenta un crecimiento acumulado de 2.9%. Por ejemplo, actividades como agropecuaria, miner<92>a, hoteles, bares y restaurantes, intermediaci<97>n <de>nanciera, salud, y otros servicios, este <9c>ltimo conformado principalmente por actividades informales que en su mayor<92>a no reportan a la DGII (salones de belleza, talleres de costura, sastrer<92>as, ebanister<92>as, es decir, b<87>sicamente PYMES), explican en conjunto el 84.6% del crecimiento acumulado del PIB enero.septiembre, siendo el aporte al <de>sco de estas actividades de apenas 32.3% de los impuestos tributarios. En cuanto al sector turismo, durante enero-septiembre se veri<de>ca un desempe<96>o satisfactorio, a pesar de la dif<92>cil situaci<97>n internacional, gracias a la diversi<de>caci<97>n en la procedencia de los turistas, in<df>uenciado por las campa<96>as publicitarias realizadas en los mercados internacionales. En tal sentido, el Banco Central est<87> trabajando en la Primera Encuesta Nacional de Educaci<97>n y Cultura Financiera, as<92> como en el Anteproyecto de Ley para la creaci<97>n de las Sociedades de Garant<92>as Rec<92>procas, que posibilitar<87>n un mayor acceso al cr<8e>dito bancario y en mejores condiciones a las MIPYMES, sector esencial en la pol<92>tica de generar empleos que est<87>n impulsando las autoridades gubernamentales del pa<92>s. Conforme a los datos disponibles a septiembre 2013, el sector <de>nanciero total exhibe un buen desempe<96>o, al presentar adecuados niveles de liquidez y rentabilidad, baja morosidad y un <92>ndice de solvencia de 19.08% al mes de agosto 2013. La banca m<9c>ltiple, que representa el 86% del sistema <de>nanciero, muestra una solvencia de 16.61%, ocupando el lugar 34 dentro de 105 pa<92>ses analizados por el Foro Econ<97>mico Mundial. Asimismo, la rentabilidad del patrimonio (ROE) alcanza 21.48% y del activo (ROA) 2.03%, presentando adecuados niveles de morosidad (2.38%) y provisiones (142.42%) que evidencian la sanidad del sector, mientras que los bene<de>cios netos ascienden a RD$13,190 millones a septiembre de 2013, superando en RD$2,800.0 millones a los registrados en igual periodo del 2012. En cuanto al Sistema de Pagos, en el presente a<96>o continu<97> su fortalecimiento, increment<87>ndose notablemente el volumen de operaciones en tiempo real y facilitando su plataforma para la realizaci<97>n de transferencias entre los pa<92>ses centroamericanos y nuestro pa<92>s. En el caso espec<92><de>co de los cheques, es una realidad la disminuci<97>n a un d<92>a del tiempo de acreditaci<97>n de los fondos, encontr<87>ndose a<9c>n pendiente la aprobaci<97>n congresual de la importante modi<de>caci<97>n a la Ley de Cheques. PERSPECTIVAS ECONOMICAS Queridos compa<96>eros y amigos, las proyecciones del Banco Central se<96>alan que el cr<8e>dito al sector privado en moneda nacional continuar<87> creciendo a un ritmo anualizado entre 10% y 12% en el presente a<96>o, contribuyendo a concretizar los planes de inversi<97>n y consumo de las empresas y las familias. Estamos convencidos de que esta dinamizaci<97>n del cr<8e>dito, conjuntamente con la inversi<97>n puntual del gobierno, permitir<87>n alcanzar un crecimiento econ<97>mico en torno al 3.0% para 2013, con una in<df>aci<97>n cercana al centro del rango-meta de 5% <b1> 1% establecido en el Programa Monetario y contenido en el Marco Macroecon<97>mico consensuado por los ministerios de Econom<92>a, Hacienda y el Banco Central. En cuanto a la tasa de cambio, proyectamos una senda de estabilidad relativa, tomando en cuenta que para el <9c>ltimo trimestre de este a<96>o se espera una mayor a<df>uencia de divisas al pa<92>s por concepto de la colocaci<97>n de los bonos soberanos, los desembolsos pendientes con organismos <de>nancieros multilaterales, el acuerdo con la Barrick y la tradicional llegada de dominicanos ausentes y turistas, todo lo cual redundar<87> en un fortalecimiento de las reservas internacionales netas del Banco Central. AVANCES INSTITUCIONALES En nuestra instituci<97>n seguimos comprometidos con el <de>rme cumplimiento de la misi<97>n que nos impone el mandato constitucional y la propia legislaci<97>n monetaria y <de>nanciera. En tal sentido, ha sido ejecutado exitosamente nuestro Plan Estrat<8e>gico 2010-2013, sobre la base de un trabajo en equipo, caracterizado por la excelencia y el apego a los valores <8e>ticos. Para tales prop<97>sitos, se introdujeron mejoras signi<de>cativas en procesos internos, en temas claves como el gobierno corporativo, la gesti<97>n de riesgos, la transparencia, la rendici<97>n de cuentas y el acceso a la informaci<97>n p<9c>blica. De igual modo, han continuado los programas de capacitaci<97>n a trav<8e>s de <d2>Aula Central<d3>, incluyendo diplomados para periodistas de los diferentes medios de comunicaci<97>n; as<92> como se incorpor<97> en la Web la secci<97>n P<87>gina Abierta, un nuevo espacio para que nuestros t<8e>cnicos puedan hacer p<9c>blicas sus opiniones sobre temas de inter<8e>s del quehacer econ<97>mico. Asimismo, relanzamos el Voluntariado del Banco Central, como parte de nuestra responsabilidad social institucional. Ahora tenemos por delante el reto del pr<97>ximo Plan Estrat<8e>gico 2014-2017, que impondr<87> nuevos desaf<92>os en la cultura organizacional, que estamos seguros ser<87>n superados satisfactoriamente, gracias a 16/11/2022 19:14 la m<92>stica de entrega y trabajo tesonero que constituye una insignia que caracteriza a todos los funcionarios y empleados que conformamos la familia bancentraliana. REFLEXIONES FINALES Ante el actual panorama internacional, econom<92>as peque<96>as y abiertas como la nuestra, deben seguir fortaleciendo los fundamentos de la estabilidad macroecon<97>mica y del crecimiento sostenido, adem<87>s de propiciar reformas estructurales y un clima de negocios que permita la generaci<97>n de empleos, en un ambiente de seguridad jur<92>dica, con<de>anza y paz social. Title: Speech before the Dominican Association of Exporters (ADOEXPO)
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Speech delivered by Mr. Hector Valdez Albizu, Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, before the Dominican Association of Exporters (ADOEXPO), on August 6, 2014 The Role of the Export Sector in the Performance of the Dominican Economy For those who speak to you, it is a high honor to appear again before this select forum that makes up the Dominican Association of Exporters (ADOEXPO), in response to a kind invitation made to us by its President, Mr. Sadala Khoury, to speak on " The Role of the Export Sector in the Performance of the Dominican Economy" . On this occasion, I would like to share with you, as a conversation between friends, some topics that I think could be of interest to this audience, especially with regard to: The Relevance of Exports in the Economy; the Current Performance of the Export Sector; Main Lessons of the so-called Asian Tigers; Brushstrokes of the International Context; Scoops of the Dominican Economy January-June 2014 and Perspectives and Final Reflections 1. I. Relevance of Exports in the Economy. Undoubtedly, there are multiple aspects that show the relevance of the export sector for a small and open economy like ours. We all recognize the potential of this sector as an engine of growth and an ally of macroeconomic stability, for its contribution to the generation of foreign exchange, jobs and added value in the economy. In the same way, it is known by all, the importance of the current account, a basic indicator in the calculation of country risk; as well as the balance of the Balance of Payments, which reflects the change in international reserves. Without going into more detail in this preamble, I would like to express that I am convinced that the Dominican Republic enjoys a privileged geographical position, in addition to presenting comparative and competitive advantages that, if we overcome some of the limitations faced by the Export Sector, could be beneficial in the context of DR-CAFTA, the Economic Partnership Agreement with the European Union (EPA, etc.). and other existing trade agreements, which have expanded the volume and niche markets that exceed more than 900 million consumers. 1. II. The Current Performance of the Dominican Export Sector. A retrospective look at the evolution of the Export Sector in the last decade reflects significant changes that motivate us to reflect. Although traditional exports (sugar, coffee, cocoa and tobacco) have significantly reduced their share of total exports, it is no less relevant to recognize that we have gained ground with other so-called non-traditional products. These minor products have grown significantly in recent years, contributing to diversify the exportable offer, as we will analyze below. As the graph shows, exports of total goods went from US 5,737 million in 2000 to US 9,504 million in 2013, a cumulative growth of 65.7%, projected to exceed ten billion dollars this year. This development could, in principle, be considered acceptable; However, when compared with the accumulated growth of the economy in those thirteen years (154.8% in nominal GDP in dollars), we could conclude that although we have certainly advanced, this performance could have been of greater importance. When disaggregating the composition of total exports of goods, into national and free zones, we observe below transcendental changes in the Dominican exportable matrix in recent years. We appreciate how national exports more than tripled, going from US966.1 million in 2000 to US4,584.2 million in 2013, a significant cumulative growth of 375.5%, producing a substantial recomposition of the exportable supply. Traditional exports decreased their relative share from 20% to 6.4%, with the exception of organic cocoa, which increased its representativeness and supplies more than 60% to the world market; and tobacco, due to the worldwide acceptance of the Dominican cigar, whose manufacture has benefited from the free zone regime. In contrast to the above, the share of non-traditional products went from 36.5% to 50.9% of total national exports in the thirteen years referenced, that is, they increased from US352.2 million in 2000 to US2,331.7 million in 2013, an extraordinary increase of 562.0%. Among these smaller producers that increasingly assume a leading role, are exports of: bananas, beer, biscuits, various organic products, as well as various fruits and vegetables, especially those from greenhouses, such as avocados, mangoes, melons, dried coconuts, bell peppers and processed fruits; along with new export products, such as gray cement, rum, rods, plastic containers, wheat flour, seasonings and condiments, pasta, cosmetics and chemical fertilizers, among others. This is undoubtedly good news, which should serve as a source of motivation for other branches of industry. We can see how within mining exports, ferronickel, which in 2000 represented 24.6% of national exports, has given way to gold exports, which represent 26.0% of national exports at the end of 2013 and 12.5% of total exports of goods, in just 14 months of operation of the Pueblo Viejo mine. As for the free zones, we observe a favorable rebound in them in the last three years, driven by their continuous diversification process. This behavior contrasts with the slow growth accumulated by these companies in the past decade, product of the loss of competitiveness due to the opening of Asian countries to the world textile market. This is a clear example of the ability to reinvent ourselves in the face of adverse exogenous factors. Textile clothing occupied 53.6% of exports from free zones in 2000, when several trade agreements, such as Multifibras, were still in force. Thirteen years later, textiles represent 24.8% of the total exported by the free zones, revealing a more diversified matrix with electrical products, pharmaceuticals, footwear and tobacco manufactures, jewelry articles, among others, standing out as a new line that did not exist in 2000, the manufacture of medical and surgical products, whose share amounts to 20.7% of the total exported by the free zones last year. When we talk about exports, we cannot ignore the boom in exports of services led by tourism. We see how in the period 2000-2013, tourism revenues registered an accumulated growth of 77.1%, consolidating tourism as the main activity generating foreign exchange, contributing 31.6% (US 5,064.8 million) of total income from exports of goods and services and generating 216,543 direct and indirect jobs at the end of 2013. Tourism activities are of particular importance because of their link with the rest of the economy, also maintaining a considerable demand for agricultural and industrial goods to supply the consumption of tourists who visit us. Undoubtedly, the Dominican Republic has become in recent decades one of the main tourist destinations in the Caribbean and Central America. This process of diversification in the exportable supply, both of national goods and of the free zones, implied the conquest of new market niches. Indeed, in 2000, 87 per cent of exports went to our main trading partner, the United States of America, and the remaining 13 per cent to other countries. This panorama has changed substantially in 2013, when it was verified that 47% is destined for the US market and 53% of our products are exported to other niches, such as Haiti (16%), the rest of America (18%), Europe (9%) and 10% to other nations, including China. Haiti is our second trading partner, with a total exported of US 1,498.9 million at the end of 2013, more than ten times the amount exported in 2000 to that country, corresponding 6% to agricultural goods, 37.3% to free zone goods and the remaining 56.5% and 0.2% to the national industrial branch and mining, respectively. Given this reality of the Export Sector, it is worth continuing to deepen a country-agenda to promote exports, taking advantage of the current environment of globalization and trade liberalization. We are all aware of the success achieved over the past five decades by the so-called "Asian Tigers". These countries are: Singapore, a small island with just 700 square kilometers and a little more than 5 million inhabitants; South Korea, already ranked as the thirteenth largest economy in the world; Taiwan, an island smaller than the Dominican Republic, with 35,980 square kilometers; and Hong Kong, an archipelago of islands that is the main financial center of Asia and the eighth largest trading power in the world. These South-East Asian countries, some of which were economies similar in size to ours, went from low growth to extraordinary economic development. In this regard, we have considered it interesting to reflect with you, the exporters and other economic agents, on what were the factors that explain these positive experiences, as well as the main strategic aspects that characterized the economic takeoff of these nations.  Economic stability, clear rules and a favorable investment climate.  Promotion of competition in domestic markets and exporting companies.  Granting of credits to key industries for the development of the country.  Setting export targets for specific companies and industries.  Coordination of export promotion agencies.  Investment in technologies, research and development.  Extensive exchange of information between the public and private sectors.  Adoption of a free trade regime. The results of these reforms and policies implemented are reflected in the substantial improvement in the current account balance as a percentage of GDP of these economies, showing how they go from being net importers of goods and services to net exporters in the last three decades. Also in the last twenty years, exports have significantly increased their share of GDP in these countries, which shows the relevance of their export-based approach to growth. In the case of Hong Kong and Singapore, exports are twice the size of GDP. 1. III. Main Lessons from the so-called Asian Tigers As can be inferred from the previous graphs, the promotion of exports merits a comprehensive strategy that involves structural reforms, public policies, private initiatives and all actions in different spheres of the national economic sphere. Assimilating these lessons learned from the so-called Asian Tigers, it is timely to recognize the importance of preserving macroeconomic stability, in order to generate a business climate conducive to the creation of wealth and jobs, in an environment of free market competition, low inflation, relative exchange rate stability and competitive interest rate levels. From the Central Bank, in line with its constitutional and legal mission, we are committed to maintaining price stability, assuming monetary policy positions based on the external and internal conditions that affect the control of inflation and the good development of the economy. It is no secret to anyone that the exchange rate is one of the most sensitive variables in small and open economies like ours. I am one of those who believe that the exchange rate must respond to the fundamentals of the economy and market forces, under a managed float scheme, which avoids sudden or speculative movements that could pressure domestic prices and the adequate performance of the country's productive activities. As I have reiterated, inflation is the worst scourge for the most vulnerable sectors with lower incomes and for eradicating poverty. The recent evolution of the Real Exchange Rate (TCR) has been favorable for the country's competitiveness. The current account deficit as a percentage of GDP has narrowed by 3.7 percentage points over the past four years. These results are consistent with both the technical studies of the International Monetary Fund and the Central Bank, which show that the Real Exchange Rate is aligned with the macro fundamentals of the economy and that the Dominican peso is not appreciated, as confirmed by the recent IMF mission that visited the country. With regard to other public and private initiatives, we do not intend in this discussion to develop the agenda of these issues, since they are beyond the competence of the Central Bank. However, by way of example, we will mention some aspects in progress, as well as challenges that we must assume by joining forces and building public and private synergies, with the vision of turning the country into an Export Leader in the Central American region and the Caribbean. With regard to improving access to credit, it is necessary to highlight the legal proposal recently presented to the National Congress by the President of the Nation, Mr. Danilo Medina, aimed at transforming the National Bank for the Promotion of Production and Housing (BNV) into a National Bank for Export Development (BANDEX), with the mission of financing the promotion of competitiveness and increasing the export capacity of the Dominican productive sector. especially in issues inherent to technological innovation and quality. It also highlights the attention of the President of the Republic to the Dominican countryside, from which comes a large part of the goods of the family food basket, also supplying the hotel demand of some 5 million tourists and exporting large quantities of food to Haiti, the United States and Europe. On this issue of financing, the Monetary Board has adopted measures that favor the channeling of resources to the productive sectors. Just to name a few, we have the regulatory flexibilizations for the evaluation and granting of bank credit to small and medium-sized enterprises, the creation of the figure of the Banking Subagent, which facilitates banking and financial inclusion, as well as the channeling of RD 20,000 million of the legal reserve to be destined to the productive sectors. On the other hand, the Draft Law that creates the Reciprocal Guarantee Societies was sent to the Executive Power, through which MSMEs will obtain financial guarantees that will allow them to expand their access to bank credit under better conditions of interest rates and terms. To this are added, the recent initiatives of the Dominican bank in support of the export sector, as well as the possibility of using the innovative figures such as the public offering trust, securitization and other options of the Dominican Stock Market, taking advantage of the long-term savings of institutional investors. With regard to opportunities for improvement in terms of competitiveness, it is imperative to promote clear and stable rules and public policies. In this situation, the challenges in terms of institutional, energy, port logistics, transport, non-tariff barriers, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, storage, among others, are aspects in which the Superior Government has shown its commitment to promote this agenda in favor of the Dominican export sector. Similarly, significant support to small and medium-sized enterprises through various legal and financial channels in order to facilitate their conversion into productive export units. It is propitious to recognize the advances experienced in the linkage of different sectors, that is, the associativity of the productive sets, the so-called clusters, to take advantage of economies of scale and improve competitiveness ratios. Given the emphasis of international experience on improving job training, we recognize that we have a long way to go, despite the efforts made in recent years in this area. For example, INFOTEP has trained 3,338,612 Dominicans in the last three decades, the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Technology has awarded a total of 20,849 national and international scholarships in 2013 alone, and the Government complies with the allocation of 4% of GDP to the education budget. As we can see, making the Export Sector a regional leader presents us with challenges as a nation to overcome the limitations and facilitate insertion in international markets. Before moving on to some final reflections, allow me now to take advantage of this scenario, to share with all of you, a very brief brushstrokes of the international context and the firsts in the period January-June 2014 of the recent performance of the Dominican economy. 1. IV. It is certainly not enough to have good geographical positioning, natural resources and logistics infrastructure. We must preserve macroeconomic stability, promote clear rules over time and work on issues such as competitiveness, quality of exportable supply, tax equity, harmonious labor relations, proper functioning of the single window and training of the workforce, among other key aspects, in an environment in which the rule of law and social peace prevail. From that perspective, as the standard-bearer of the optimism that I am, I urge you that with faith in God and supported by the collective effort of all, we bet on a better future for the common good of the Dominican nation. Thanks a lot.

Title: Speech at the launch ceremony of the new family of banknotes

text: Words of the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Replica, Hector Valdez Albizu, at the act of putting into circulation of the 6th. Banknote family 2014. It is for me of great pleasure, in my capacity as Governor, on behalf of the authorities of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, and in my own condition, to welcome you to this act of putting into circulation the New family of banknotes 2014, which corresponds to the sixth family in the entire history of the issues made by the Central Bank, institution in full exercise of the powers conferred on it by the Constitution of the Replica and the Monetary and Financial Law 183-02, in its capacity as the issuing entity of the banknotes and coins representing the national currency. The Central Bank authorities had long devised the release of a new family of banknotes and, as a result, specific instructions were given to specialists from the competent departments to work on preparing the technical specifications necessary for their preparation. This long process coincides with the happy circumstance of the enactment of Law No. 146, of July 12, 2011, whose article 4 establishes that the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic must include in the banknotes, from this a, the flower "Rosa de Bayahibe" (Pereskia quisqueyana Ala in). In this sense, the Central Bank, as of today, October 1, 2014, circulates the Sixth family of banknotes of the denominations of 2,000, 1,000, 500, 200, 100 and 50 Dominican pesos, which contain new designs and security features that are easy to recognize by the plico. The new banknotes, as announced in the press, will coexist with the existing banknotes of the same denominations until their replacement is completed, so that the current banknotes will maintain their liberatory force for the payment of all bidding and private obligations. Behind every momentous decision, as we know, there is always a story that serves as a background, an origin that has given rise to everything, and that is worth telling. In the aforementioned Law No. 146-11, which replaces the "mahogany flower" with the "Rosa de Bayahibe", it is established that this symbol, destined to strengthen our identity as a nation, was chosen because it represents in an idea way the national flora, according to authorized institutions, such as the National Botanical Garden of Santo Domingo, which proposed that the flower "Rosa de Bayahibe" be declared as National Flower of the Dominican Replica. The "Rose of Bayahibe" was discovered in 1977 by the French biogo Henri Alain Liogier, in the eastern region of the Dominican Replica, and published as new in the scientific journal Phytologia in 1980. The Central Bank, dear officials and friends, immediately initiated a process of investigation and technical proposals for the modification of the family of banknotes in force, with a contest in which several paper money manufacturers participated, who submitted to our institution different designs, being chosen the house De la Rue lnternational Limited, of England, which was the one that obtained the highest score in the economic and technical evaluations. The designs were carefully analyzed by the Committee of Competitions for the Printing of Banknotes and Currency Pressure of the Central Bank, headed by the speaker and in which several authorities of the honorable Monetary Board, the Vice Governance, the Management, the Deputy General Manager, the Deputy Management of Monetary, Exchange and Financial Policies, the Legal Consultancy, actively participate. and directors and officials of the Emisi and Custody, Treasury, Purchasing and Contracting and Cultural departments. The deliberations of the Committee for the Acuci of Banknotes and Coins subsequently continued with an exchange of views with the proponents of the house De la Rue lnternational Limited, to translate institutional expectations into attractive colourful designs, and the provision of security measures for the new banknotes, such as the latent image, the mark for the blind, the numbering, the security thread, the microprints, Tinta ticamente variable, watermark, iridescent band, etc. As you will soon see, the Sixth family of banknotes contains a series of attractive and innovative elements, both in the color and size of the neros, the disposition of the legends and the placement of the national figures, but the essence of each denomination has been preserved, what we can call the spirit of a monetary tradition that begins 1947 with the first family of banknotes and that continues to evolve Sixty-seven ace later, always with the purpose of improving through innovation, making each piece safer, more durable and manageable for the user fold. Dear authorities, officials and friends, today culminates a long and exciting project, full of challenges for all, and that happily yields more than satisfactory results, as you will see in a moment. I wish to thank all the instances, authorities, officials and technicians who participated in this process of monetary elaboration, and to thank those who have come to acomparnos in this important act, to be privileged witnesses of this putting into circulation of the Sixth family of banknotes 2014, thus complying not only with the provisions of the law given by the National Congress and promulgated by the Executive Power, but also with one of the basic precepts of the misi of the Central Bank of the Dominican Replica. Thank you very much and good evening. For stability and growth EJIH3DBancoCentralRD
