Title: Sixtieth Optimal Anniversary Address of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Logo BC Sixty-seventh Anniversary Address of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, October 23, 2014 With deep emotion I appear for the seventeenth time before the solemnity of this auditorium, to commemorate the sixty-seventh (67th) anniversary of the creation of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, with the purpose of rendering accounts before you and the country, as is customary, in relation to the recent performance and prospects of the Dominican economy, as well as on the institutional progress achieved during this year. I confess that it was for me of special significance to be honored for the eighth time as Governor of this Institution, thanks to the trust placed in me by His Excellency the President of the Republic, Mr. Danilo Medina Sanchez, when he ratified me for the second time during his administration. In truth, friends all, it fills me with gratitude to God and with great pride, the privilege of having 40 years of my life being part of the Central Bank, climbing from the position of technical assistant to the top, a long journey that, without a doubt, has left indelible traces in my heart. As is tradition, I always take advantage of this scenario to reiterate to my family, headed by my mother, my wife Fior, my son Hector Manuel and my brothers, all that their unconditional love, understanding and solidarity represents for me. In the same way, I want to deeply thank the great support I receive from the honorable members of the Monetary Board, as well as recognize the extraordinary dedication, effort and dedication of the Technical Staff and all the Bancentralians in each daily day. Without this valuable support, it would not have been able to assume before the nation the great constitutional commitment that corresponds to the Central Bank, to guarantee price stability, promote the regulation of the Financial System and the functioning of the payment system, in an increasingly complex and volatile international context. Certainly, we live in a world that is torn between great challenges to recover the path of growth, after the global crisis of 2008. There are a number of core issues today, such as the challenges of overcoming poverty for more than a third of humanity and the complicated geopolitical risks in the Middle East, Eastern Europe and elsewhere, in addition to the prevailing somewhat uncertain and vulnerable landscape. International Environment Just a few weeks ago, we participated in the traditional autumn meeting of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, which has just released the World Economic Outlook (WEO). In these projections it is expected that the world economy would reach a growth of 3.3% in this 2014, rising to 3.8% for the year 2015, driven largely by the performance of emerging countries. For the United States of America, there is good news. On the one hand, improvements emerge in the labor market, with the lowest unemployment rate in the last 6 years, registering 5.9% in September, with the expectation that its rate considered full employment would soon be reached, around 5.25%. On the other hand, there has been a recovery in consumption and private investment in that nation, estimating an economic growth of 2.2% this year and 3.1% for 2015. This scenario takes into account the withdrawal of the monetary stimulus that the Federal Reserve has been doing, envisioning that interest rates would remain low until at least mid-2015, which has been internalized by the Dominican markets and economic agents. These prospects should have a positive impact on our economy, given the close link that unites us with that country, with which we maintain a commercial exchange of about 60 per cent. As for the Eurozone, after two years of recession, an expansion of 0.8% is projected in 2014, largely influenced by the performance maintained by Germany and the recovery that Spain and Portugal have been having, expecting an improvement of 1.3% in 2015. These expected results also bode well for our economy. In the case of Latin America and the Caribbean, GDP is estimated to grow 1.3% this year, due to the poor expected results of three of its largest economies: Brazil, Argentina and Venezuela, a projection that would rise to 2.2% in 2015. According to this IMF publication, the Dominican Republic would be the second country with the highest economic growth in the region, only surpassed by Panama. In that vein, allow me now, as is tradition on each anniversary, to present the scoops of the economy for the third quarter of the year and the outlook for the end of 2014. SECTOR REAL I am pleased to announce that with the new national accounts referenced to 2007 and according to preliminary figures, the Dominican economy measured through the Gross Domestic Product in real terms, registered an accumulated growth of 7.0% in January-September 2014, continuing the process of dynamization initiated last year, when monetary and fiscal measures were adopted to boost economic growth, job creation, reducing the fiscal deficit and preserving macroeconomic stability. All economic activities show a positive growth in the added value of production in real terms, with the highest incidence being: mining 24.1%, construction 10.7%; hotels, bars and restaurants 8.2%, health 8.2%, financial intermediation and insurance 7.8%, education 6.7%, manufacturing 5.7%; transport 5.6%, agriculture 5.4% and trade 5.0%. This performance is consistent with the 7.6% increase in sales of companies reported to the DGII in January-August 2014, observing that the ones that increased the most were the activities with the highest growth within GDP. One aspect to highlight is that the most job-generating activities are growing. Between October 2013-October 2014, we had an increase of 165,799 net jobs, with a cumulative increase of 235,600 new employees from October 2012 to date. With these results, the open unemployment rate decreased from 7% to 6% and the expanded unemployment rate was reduced from 15% to 14.1%, which would indicate that before the end of his term in office, the President of the Republic, Danilo Medina Sanchez, would be reaching his aspiration to promote 400,000 new job opportunities. The combination of this sustained economic growth with high levels of job creation, together with low inflationary pressures, are key factors that would necessarily lead to poverty continuing to decline at a rate similar to that recorded in the last two years, when 534,139 people were lifted out of poverty, a reduction of 6 percentage points. Without a doubt, friends, this is good news. MONETARY POLICY AND FINANCIAL SECTOR This increase in production and employment has been achieved within a framework of price stability. As published in the national press, in the period January-September 2014, inflation was 2.53%, while annualized, measured from September 2013 to September 2014, stood at 2.83%, a rate much lower than the 5.13% registered in the same period of the previous year, placing us in second place among the countries with the lowest inflation in Latin America. excluding dollarized countries. To this end, monetary policy has acted in a timely manner, maintaining a neutral stance aimed at bringing inflation closer to the target range on the policy horizon and growing the economy around its potential. In that sense, the Central Bank has been prudent in providing the necessary liquidity to satisfy the demand for money of the different economic sectors of national life. Under this scenario, the monetary policy interest rate has remained at 6.25% since August 2013, while market interest rates have remained below their historical average. This condition, together with greater banking competition, boosted loans in national currency to the private sector of the financial system, which as of September 30, 2014 compared to the end of December 2013, grew by 11.0%, an additional RD 53,231.0 million, much higher than the increase of RD 42,281 million that was verified in the same period of the previous year. In annualized terms, the growth of these loans was 15.3% to September 2014, that is, Dominican households and companies, especially the manufacturing, commerce, MSMEs and housing acquisition sectors, received loans in the order of RD 71,002.0 million above what was received in September 2013, when the Central Bank had released around RD 20 billion of the resources of the Legal Reserve. This means, friends, that bank credit is flowing into the economy. As a country, for a decade, we have the strength of having a stable Financial System, with adequate indicators, which presents to September 2014, a liquidity ratio of 22.2%, an average return on equity of 18.5%, a delinquency of 1.96% and a solvency ratio of 17.7% to August 2014, much higher than the 10% required by the Monetary and Financial Law. Multiple banks, which represent more than 86% of the Financial System, exhibited at that same date, a delinquency of 1.69%, a return on equity of 21.5% and a solvency of 15.4%. EXTERNAL SECTOR In line with the behavior of the Dominican economy, the external sector exhibits a favorable performance. The current account deficit of the balance of payments was reduced by US221.9 million in January-September compared to the same period in 2013, driven by the 4.3% growth in total exports and the extraordinary increase in tourism receipts and remittances. Among the exports of goods, gold and silver stand out, which were US 322.7 million higher than those of January-September 2013, as well as cocoa, which for its quality could be considered part of our country brand, whose exports including those that left under the regime of special free zones, grew by 40.0%, amounting to US200.0 million. Other items to highlight are tobacco, goods purchased in port and sugar, which grew by 13.2%, 7.9% and 5.6% respectively. Free Zone exports totaled US3,877.5 million, growing 3.6% in the first nine months of the year. Regarding tourism, the country's main source of foreign exchange, in January-September 2014 revenues from this concept grew significantly by 11.5%, reaching US 4,285.3 million, thanks to the growth of 10% in the arrival of tourists in that period. It is important to note, by way of illustration, that only last September, the increase in tourist flow was an extraordinary 13.3%. These are truly encouraging data. Similar behavior experienced remittances, which grew by 10.8%, amounting to US 3,462.4 million, some US 336.4 million additional to the flow received in January-September 2013, a laudable support of our diaspora. It should be noted the favorable behavior of foreign direct investment, which reached US 1,807.4 million in January-September, an amount higher by US 298.6 million than the same period of 2013, that is, a growth of 20%. This increase, mainly in the trade and communications sectors, reaffirms that the Dominican Republic continues to be an attractive destination for foreign investment. As expected, dear friends, this performance of the external sector contributed to achieving international reserves equivalent to almost 3 months of imports, placing gross reserves at US4,353.4 million as of October 20, 2014 and US4,128.9 million net. This reserve position is equivalent to a coverage of 111% with respect to the monetary issue, that is, for each peso issued, the Central Bank has a support of the equivalent of 1.11 pesos in Net International Reserves, one of the highest ratios in the entire Dominican financial history and with a tendency to que.se increase towards the end of this year. In line with this panorama, the Dominican exchange market registers one of the lowest levels of accumulated depreciation in the region, this being only 2.6% as of October 20, 2014, well below Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Peru, Colombia and Costa Rica, among others, with depreciations between 3% and 23%. Institutional Achievements 2014 Allow me now to share some of the main institutional advances, of which you are the true protagonists, a clear example of that culture increasingly rooted in the Central Bank, of promoting the search for achievements by results. With regard to banking regulation, this year the Honorable Monetary Board heard the Draft Law on Reciprocal Guarantee Societies, sent to the Executive for consideration, as well as approved on August 14, the Microcredit Regulations, which will enable MSMEs to have greater access to credit and under better conditions. Two other important regulations were also published: the Financial Services User Protection Regulation and the Financial System Liquidity Risk Regulation. An initiative that benefits the Dominican population, especially the most remote rural areas, is the approval by the Honorable Monetary Board of the figure of the banking sub-agent, which promotes greater banking and financial inclusion. Economic Outlook Dear friends, I am convinced that the prospects for the Dominican Republic are very positive for the end of 2014. With regard to the decline in international oil prices, I think that if this situation continues, an opportunity could be opened for the country to implement a "hedging strategy through futures contracts", aimed at acquiring oil and other commodities at today's attractive prices. As you can see, the Dominican economy is on the right track. Final Thoughts I want to express to you, friends, that today more than ever the times that humanity lives demand an attitude of commitment and responsibility, to achieve the economic well-being and social inclusion of the neediest population, with quality jobs, more education and better health. From the Central Bank we will continue with determination to tread that journey of almost seven decades of existence, to fulfill the constitutional and legal mandate, to guarantee the control of inflation, the worst scourge against wage earners and the most dispossessed. Let me share with you the message that it is incumbent upon all of us, without exception, to contribute our work and best efforts, in order to build a more just and humane society. As His Holiness Pope Francis recently put it: "brotherhood among men and collaboration to build a more just society are not a dream or a fantasy, but the result of a concerted effort and the dignified work of all towards the common good." Let us embrace this great challenge wholeheartedly and with faith. L I conclude my words by telling you that the greatness of a society is determined by the way it faces its future. With the foundations of our economy and its potential, I urge you, friends all, to continue betting, with optimism and hope, on a better future for this beautiful land where we were born. May God bless you always. Thanks a lot.

It is no secret to anyone that since our previous appearance before ADOEXPO in 2014, different scenarios have emerged in a changing international economic landscape, still complex, uncertain and volatile. On the one hand, the continuation of the growth of the US economy stands out, which experienced in the second quarter of this year a year-on-year rate of 2.7% with a projection of the end of 2015 of 2.5% according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), also evidenced in a lower unemployment rate of 5.3%, which is already approaching its level of full employment of 5.25%. It is also propitious to highlight the definitive exit from the recession of the Eurozone. As expected, these events have been positively impacting our exports, tourism and remittances, while we have been favored by the significant reduction in international prices of several commodities, particularly oil, which has been registering figures truly unthinkable a year ago. On the other hand, I believe that there are aspects that deserve the attention of economic policymakers. Just by way of illustration we can cite the rising expectations in the Federal Reserve Bank's rate this year, which in a way has been internalized by the markets; Greece's fiscal and debt crisis, which created uncertainty in capital markets and, among other issues, recent measures by China, the world's second-largest economy. On August 11, China's central bank surprised markets by announcing a 1.9% devaluation of the yuan, rising to 2.7% from the start of the year to August 31. In addition, given the slowdown in its economy, the Chinese monetary authorities lowered their benchmark interest rates for the fifth consecutive time, accumulating a reduction of 140 basis points from October 2014 to date. After these expansionary monetary measures were taken, capital outflows occurred and the yuan depreciated at a greater rate than expected, causing interventions in the foreign exchange market equivalent to a reduction of US 106,000 million of its international reserves in the last weeks alone. The reaction in the international financial markets was immediate. Shares on major stock exchanges declined to their lowest levels since October 2014. Net exporters of primary goods were impacted, such as Russia, Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Peru and Colombia, among others, some of which, due to the sharp depreciation of their currencies, also intervened their exchange markets. Something similar happened in some Asian economies, such as South Korea, Singapore and Malaysia. I agree with the opinion of some government officials who have expressed themselves on the situation in China, in the sense that in the short term they do not foresee that it represents a threat to the Dominican Republic, although we must remain vigilant about the impact that could be generated for the world economy in the medium and long term, particularly in the 16/11/2022 19:15 The United States, our main trading partner. At the regional level, we are monitoring some events, such as double-digit inflation in Venezuela and Argentina, the tense situation with Haiti, our second largest trading partner, the problems of Mexico and other South American countries due to the drop in oil prices, as well as the delicate fiscal and debt situation of Puerto Rico. An element to consider for the Dominican Republic, especially for tourism in the medium term, is the reopening of relations between Cuba and the United States of America. Unlike much of Latin America, the Dominican Republic, as a net importer of commodities, reports significant foreign exchange savings due to the fall in the prices of crude oil and other primary goods, which together with the strong macroeconomic fundamentals have allowed to preserve the climate of stability and growth, maintaining the country as an attractive and safe destination for Foreign Direct Investment, successfully navigating the adverse international environment. These lines have shown resilience, successfully overcoming several external shocks. An example of this is how last year, our exports of goods grew by 5.3%, while those of Latin America on average registered a fall of 3.0%, according to ECLAC, with countries presenting significant decreases in their exports, such as 16/11/2022 19:15 such as Venezuela (-16.8%) Argentina (-11.9%), Panama (-10.6%), Peru (-7.8%) and Brazil (-7.0%), among others. However, we are aware that we have challenges and opportunities ahead of the export sector, in order to export new products with greater added value and to make further progress in diversifying markets for both export regimes. I am of the opinion that the right direction would be to maximize our comparative and competitive advantages, improving productivity, for which I wanted on this occasion to refer to a key issue in order to achieve these objectives: Innovation. Recently, when reading the book by journalist Andres Oppenheimer, "Create or Die", we were struck by his arguments about the importance for Latin America of promoting innovation, highlighting that today "the prosperity of countries depends less and less on their natural resources and increasingly on their educational systems, their scientists and their innovators". Hence the need to insist on strengthening education as a fundamental engine of socio-economic development and continue to promote new times. A laudable example in this regard has been the successful "surprise visits" of President Danilo Medina Sanchez, who has managed to promote agro-industrial products towards new market niches. I want to take advantage of this scenario, because of the importance of this auditorium in terms of job creation, to address an issue that has captured the attention of the President of the Dominican Republic, who has declared "the need to dediggify wages in the country to correct inequality ...", an approach that I fully share. The Central Bank has insisted that nominal wages in the country have grown on average less than inflation plus labor productivity. In this sense, the real average income of Dominican workers at the end of 2014 is practically the same as in 1991, despite productivity having increased 65.5% in those 23 years. On this point, it should be noted that despite the recent 14% increase in minimum wages in the private sector, there is still a significant gap due to the accumulated lag in wage adjustments. Improving income distribution is increasingly confirmed to be important for the sustainability of economic growth. In fact, recently the Managing Director of the IMF, Christine Lagarde, citing the results of a study by that organization, said that "we must raise the incomes of the poor and the middle class to reduce inequality and boost growth." To give you an idea, this study suggests that if the poorest 20% of the population increases their income by 1 percentage point as a proportion of GDP, the average annual growth of the economy would be expected to increase by 0.38%. In line with the above, I have repeatedly stated that a pending challenge in the country is to improve workers' wages, which allows to boost aggregate demand, through an increase in consumption, investment and production. In short, this would allow economic growth to spill over to the vast majority of the population, improving income distribution and contributing to poverty reduction. That is why in the future we see the Export Sector, not only as the main generator of foreign exchange and promotion of national production, but as a leading sector in the generation of quality jobs with a decent remuneration, as has happened in other countries. Although we already have the single window, the Export Bureau and through BANDEX, the Export Sector will have access to timely financing, we must recognize that we must continue to overcome the obstacles that I mentioned in my speech last year in terms of competitiveness, tax equity, logistics infrastructure, among others, maintaining clear and permanent rules of the game over time. Similarly, we must direct efforts to generate a greater export culture and strengthen export promotion strategies, assimilating successful experiences such as "PROCHILE", which already has offices in the United States of America and England to support Chilean products in these markets. text: p, DDiscurso delseptuagesimoprimeraniversariode lBCRDD r onunciado Li , pporelggobbernaddor cenciaddo Hector Valddez Albbizu 23 right octubbre right 81220 With great joy and deep emotion, on October 23 of each year, the Bancentraliana family commemorates a new anniversary of the Central Bank, founded in 1947 as part of the most transcendental monetary reform in our republican life, through which the Dominican peso was created as legal tender. Certainly, after the Bretton Woods agreements that gave rise in 1944 to a new global financial architecture, the monetarist experts, Robert Tri.n, Henri Wallich and Raul Prebisch, were in charge of drafting Law 1529 dated October 9, 1947 that gave birth to the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic as Issuing Entity and the Superintendency of Banks, laying the foundations for the development of national banking. I think, dear friends, that the celebration of these 71 years of institutional life is a good time to emphasize the importance of having a valuable human capital, made up of economists and professionals with doctorates and masters in economics, finance, law and other areas, carried out in prestigious centers of studies worldwide; But above all, we have a staff committed to excellence and ethical values, based on an efficient technological infrastructure and modern strategic planning tools. With great pride I want to emphasize on this occasion, that women occupy a preponderant place in the middle and high management of our institution, since 55% of all management positions are occupied by Bancentralianas, which distinguishes us at the national level in compliance with the policy that promotes gender equity. As I have reiterated on other occasions, it has been a privilege for the speaker to have the extraordinary and determined collaboration of the members of the Honorable Monetary Board, as well as a sta. and a staff willing to give their best at all times, in the arduous work of designing and executing monetary and financial policy in accordance with international standards, guaranteeing price stability, a mandate assigned to us by the Constitution of the Republic. I confess, my friends, that fulfilling this task has only been possible with the help of God, the sense of duty and commitment to the homeland and the support of the authorities of the country, headed by His Excellency the President of the Republic, Mr. Danilo Medina Sanchez, who has honored us once again, by placing his trust in us and in the entire team that accompanies me at the Central Bank. In the same way, the understanding and unconditional support of my beloved wife Fior, my dear son Hector Manuel, my beloved mother and my brothers, have been key in this titanic task, if you will, of To fulfil our responsibilities at the head of this institution. Allow me, now friends, to touch briefly on some relevant aspects of the international arena. of this dissertation, and refer to Just a few days ago, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), at its recent autumn meeting. held in Bali, Indonesia, updated its World Economic Outlook (WEO) report, revealing that it would grow 3.7% this year; while the economy of the United States of America, our main trading partner, would be growing by 2.9% in 2018, reaching unemployment rates at historic lows, considered "full employment". According to the IMF, the current international scenario presents various risks. Among others, the process of normalization of US monetary policy stands out, through the increase in US monetary policy rates. 16/11/2022 19:15 interest of the Federal Reserve; trade tensions between the world's major nations; geopolitical conflicts; technological crimes and cyberattacks and recent spikes in oil prices. Undoubtedly, this scenario has generated uncertainty in international financial markets, especially in some emerging economies with weak macroeconomic fundamentals. Currently, Latin America and the Caribbean faces several challenges due to the difficult situation that Venezuela, Nicaragua and Argentina are going through, which has led to a downward revision in the expected growth for the region, from 1.6% to 1.2% for 2018. Despite this adverse Latin American scenario, the IMF in its latest revision has increased to 6.4% the projections for the Dominican Republic at the end of 2018, whose economy would lead regional growth. Indeed, my friends, this year local monetary conditions have remained favourable, characterized by interest rates below their historical averages and high dynamism of private loans. The evolution of the main monetary indicators during the period January-September 2018 reflects that the economy continues to react positively to the expansionary measures implemented in the second half of 2017. As a result, there was a multiplier effect on the channelling of credit to the private sector and a rebound in domestic demand, particularly investment and private consumption. Considering the aforementioned external risk factors, and their possible impact on the future path of inflation, last July the Central Bank decided to move towards a less expansionary stance, by increasing the monetary policy rate from 5.25% to 5.50% annually. In the months since the aforementioned policy decision, the Dominican economy has evolved as expected. Monetary aggregates show rates consistent with nominal output growth; and private credit, in national and foreign currency, continues to expand in a healthy way, growing year-on-year by around 12% at the end of September, equivalent to a significant increase of RD 112,553 million. It is important to note that only during January-September 2018, private credit shows an increase of RD 70,364 million, a growth of 7.2%. The sectors that have benefited most from the expansion of financing to the private sector in this period have been: Consumption (RD 19,914 million), Acquisition of housing and Construction (RD 16,532 million), Commerce (RD 10,197 million) and Hotels and restaurants (RD 6,683 million), among others. I want at this time, following the tradition in each anniversary of the Central Bank, to share the scoops of the recent results of the Dominican economy, with you and with the friends of the press who accompany us in this auditorium and through social networks. I am pleased to announce to the country that, according to preliminary figures, the Gross Domestic Product in real terms registered a cumulative growth of 6.9% in January-September 2018. This robust performance reflects the momentum that the Dominican economy continues to show. In September of this year, the Monthly Indicator of Economic Activity (IMAE) shows a year-on-year increase of 8.6% compared to September 2017, a month in which the economy was slowed down as a result of storms Irma and Maria. It is important to highlight that all economic activities presented positive variations, being the ones with the highest incidence during January-September: Construction (10.9%), Free Zones (12.0%), Commerce (8.9%), Health (8.7%), Communications (8.0%), Financial Services (7.7%), Agriculture (6.9%), Transport and Storage (6.7%), Local Manufacturing (6.3%), Energy and Water (6.1%), Hotels, Bars and Restaurants (5.4%), among others. As I expressed in a recent dissertation before the Association of Industries of the Dominican Republic (AIRD), the performance of the manufacturing sector is consistent with the results of the Monthly Business Opinion Survey of the Manufacturing Sector published by the Central Bank, which presents a favorable opinion in more than 95% of the companies consulted, and also with the Monthly Index of Manufacturing Activity prepared by the AIRD. 16/11/2022 19:15 This revitalization of the Dominican economy in a context of low inflation, with this indicator standing at 1.52% in January-September, is also reflected in the behavior of the labor market. According to the latest figures available from the National Continuous Labor Force Survey, total jobs increased by an average of 150,000 additional employed in the last twelve months, accelerating the pace of job creation by about 30,000 compared to the 120,000 employed generated on average in the last four quarters. With these results, the annualized average of the open unemployment rate fell from 5.9% in the July-September 2017 quarter to 5.5% in the same period of 2018. A fact worth highlighting in this auditorium is that job creation reached the extraordinary figure of 734,544 additional employed in the six years from October 2012 to September 2018. It is fair to recognize that in order to achieve this rate of economic growth and job creation, as I have mentioned in several hearings, the contribution of the thriving private sector, which is mainly responsible for boosting economic growth in recent years, deserves to be highlighted. In fact, gross private capital formation and household consumption explain 86% of the growth in January-September of this year. Analyzing the performance of the External Sector, it should be noted that total exports of goods reached US8,271.6 million in January-September 2018, increasing by US795.0 million (10.6% growth). In that order, national exports amounted to US 3,576.8 million, grew 9.9%, some US 322.2 million additional to last year. Free zone exports reached about US4,694.8 million, for an increase of 11.2% in that period. On the other hand, in these first nine months of the year, compared to the same period 2017, tourism reported revenues of US 5,808.3 million, an increase of US 318.8 million. In the same way, US4,866.5 million were received for remittances, for a notable increase of 10.2%, while foreign direct investment amounted to US1,892.4 million and other income from services, US1,248.4 million. Based on the positive behavior of the external sector in January-September 2018, the country received foreign exchange earnings during that period for an amount amounting to US22,087.2 million, which represents an additional US1,597.0 million compared to 2017; It is estimated that such foreign exchange income would rise to US30,000.0 million at the end of 2018. This increase in the inflow of foreign currency facilitated the accumulation of significant levels of International Reserves, which rose to US7,329 million as of September 30, which represents a coverage of more than 4 months of imports, excluding free zones, in a context of relative exchange rate stability. At the same date, the accumulated depreciation was only -3.1%, lower than most countries in the Region. In addition to the economic outlook described, we have a stable, profitable and patrimonially strengthened financial system, according to figures published by the Superintendency of Banks, with low delinquency (1.85%) and a solvency ratio of 18.4% as of August 2018, above the 10% established in the Monetary and Financial Law and the recommendations of Basel III. At the end of September, multiple banks, which represent 86.5% of the financial system, reported a return on equity (ROE) of 22.69% and the return on their assets (ROA) reached 2.36%. In another vein, I consider it pertinent to mention that the Monetary Board ordered the creation of a Committee on Macroprudential Policies and Financial Stability, composed of officials of the Central Bank and the Superintendency of Banks, whose objective is to examine and safeguard a potential systemic risk, preparing the First Financial Stability Report, aligning the country with the international trend in this area. It should be noted that with regard to the banking field and our modern Payment System, we are working on two issues of great relevance today: In the regulation that would apply to financial innovations based on digital technology, or "fintechs" as they are known; and in the Cyber and Information Security Regulations, in line with the government's National Cybersecurity Strategy. The Central Bank also created the Department of Operational Security, 16/11/2022 19:15 Specialized in handling all cybersecurity issues. Entering the last part of this traditional speech, I want to refer to the prospects of the Dominican economy. Going forward, the Central Bank expects private sector financing to remain dynamic for the rest of the year, in a context of strong macroeconomic fundamentals and effective coordination between monetary and fiscal policies. In this vein, it is foreseen that economic activity will register a growth of around 6.5% at the end of 2018, converging to its potential growth for next year. Inflation by the end of the year is projected to be close to 3%, gradually returning to the central value of the target of 4%1% in 2019. As for the current account deficit, it is estimated that it would close this year at around -1% of GDP, largely explained by the increase in the oil bill, which already in January-September 2018 had increased by US 778.5 million, equivalent to 38.1% compared to the same period of the previous year. Lower inflationary pressures have given the Central Bank room to pause the normalization process towards a more neutral monetary policy stance. Rest assured that we are prepared to react in a timely manner to possible risks arising from the international and domestic environment, which may generate deviations in meeting the inflation target and maintaining macroeconomic stability. In particular, we are monitoring the upward trend in oil prices and, in particular, the impact that a greater differential between the domestic interest rate and that of the United States of America may have, as the Federal Reserve's normalization process continues, through further adjustments in its monetary policy rate. This good performance and outlook for economic activity have been accompanied by an adequate implementation of fiscal policy, which has continued the process of consolidation of public finances. During this year, tax revenues are in line with budget estimates, while public spending has moderated, which has allowed the deficit of the Non-Financial Public Sector to stand at only -0.5% of GDP as of August. Looking at the dynamism shown by tax revenues during the period January-September 2018, with an expansion of 12.5% in year-on-year terms, it can be expected that the fiscal deficit would end up around -2.2% of GDP, according to the General State Budget of this year. Arriving at the final message, I want to address a topic that should motivate us to reflect as policy makers. The threats to the global economy from climate change are not trivial and pose a challenge to long-term growth. During the aforementioned annual meeting of the IMF in Bali, Indonesia, the governors of the Bank of France and the Bank of England, affirmed that, considering the pernicious effects of global warming on economies, central banks have a role to play in the fight against climate change, through the design of regulatory frameworks that encourage banks to finance activities that favor the environment. Likewise, according to the economist recently awarded with the Nobel Prize, William Nordhaus, "it is necessary to make adjustments to the productive systems so that it is possible to achieve a path of economic growth that coexists with the sustainability of the environment". In this sense, the Central Bank is part of the National Council for Climate Change and Clean Development Mechanism and we have on the agenda the formulation of policies and measures that will involve the national financial system in support of environmental solutions. In that direction, we are proceeding with the gradual transformation of our facilities to operate with the use of renewable energy, and the Central Bank Volunteer has joined the enormous efforts made by the Government, in terms of reforestation to safeguard our watersheds. It is indisputable, my friends, that we have challenges ahead of us that can only be achieved on the basis of expanding and strengthening strategic public-private partnerships. To promote more inclusive economic growth, banishing inequality, inequality and poverty, we need to continue improving education and access to health; generate quality jobs, develop the potential of our Stock Market, increase our competitiveness and facilitate the entrepreneurship of young people and MSMEs, among other initiatives. Recently, Paul Romer, also a Nobel Prize laureate in economics, pointed out that the best way to boost the 16/11/2022 19:15 Sustained economic growth is through technological innovation, based on the generation of new ideas, research and more qualified human capital. With this motivating force to take on the challenge of uniting wills for the sake of a better nation, as I always conclude my words urging you to enthusiastically bet with faith and optimism on the future, for a better future for all Dominicans. May God bless you. Thanks a lot. 16/11/2022 19:15

Cabe destacar que en lo concerniente al <87>mbito bancario y a nuestro moderno Sistema de Pagos, estamos trabajando en dos temas de gran relevancia en la actualidad: En la regulaci<97>n que aplicar<92>a a las innovaciones <de>nancieras basadas en tecnolog<92>a digital, o <d2><de>ntechs<d3> como se les conoce; y en el Reglamento de Seguridad Cibern<8e>tica y de la Informaci<97>n, de acuerdo con la Estrategia Nacional de Ciberseguridad del gobierno. Asimismo, el Banco Central cre<97> el Departamento de Seguridad Operativa, 16/11/2022 19:15 especializado en manejar todos los temas de ciberseguridad. Entrando a la <9c>ltima parte de este tradicional discurso, quiero referirme a las perspectivas de la econom<92>a dominicana. Hacia adelante, el Banco Central espera que el <de>nanciamiento al sector privado se mantenga din<87>mico durante el resto del a<96>o, en un contexto de fundamentos macroecon<97>micos fuertes y una efectiva coordinaci<97>n entre las pol<92>ticas monetaria y <de>scal. En ese tenor se avizora que la actividad econ<97>mica registre un crecimiento en torno a 6.5% al <de>nalizar 2018, convergiendo a su crecimiento potencial para el pr<97>ximo a<96>o. La in<df>aci<97>n para <de>n del a<96>o se proyecta cercana al 3%, retornando en forma gradual al valor central de la meta de 4%<b1>1% en 2019. En cuanto al d<8e><de>cit de cuenta corriente se estima que el mismo cerrar<92>a este a<96>o en torno al -1% del PIB, explicado en gran medida por el incremento de la factura petrolera, que ya en enero-septiembre 2018 hab<92>a aumentado en US$778.5 millones, equivalente a un 38.1% respecto a igual per<92>odo del a<96>o anterior. Las menores presiones in<df>acionarias han dado espacio al Banco Central para hacer una pausa en el proceso de normalizaci<97>n, hacia una postura de pol<92>tica monetaria m<87>s neutral. Tengan la certeza de que estamos preparados para reaccionar de manera oportuna ante eventuales riesgos que se deriven del entorno internacional y dom<8e>stico, que puedan generar desv<92>os en el cumplimiento de la meta de in<df>aci<97>n y el mantenimiento de la estabilidad macroecon<97>mica. Particularmente, estamos dando seguimiento a la tendencia al alza de los precios del petr<97>leo y, de manera especial, al impacto que pueda tener un mayor diferencial entre la tasa de inter<8e>s dom<8e>stica y la de Estados Unidos de Am<8e>rica, en la medida que contin<9c>e el proceso de normalizaci<97>n de la Reserva Federal, a trav<8e>s de nuevos ajustes en su tasa de pol<92>tica monetaria. Este buen desempe<96>o y perspectivas de la actividad econ<97>mica han estado acompa<96>adas de una implementaci<97>n adecuada de la pol<92>tica <de>scal, que ha continuado el proceso de consolidaci<97>n de las <de>nanzas p<9c>blicas. Durante el presente a<96>o, los ingresos <de>scales se encuentran en l<92>nea con las estimaciones presupuestarias, mientras que el gasto p<9c>blico se ha moderado, lo que ha permitido que el d<8e><de>cit del Sector P<9c>blico No Financiero se ubique en tan s<97>lo -0.5% del PIB al mes de agosto. Al observar el dinamismo que muestran los ingresos <de>scales durante el per<92>odo enero-septiembre de 2018, con una expansi<97>n de 12.5% en t<8e>rminos interanuales, se puede prever que el d<8e><de>cit <de>scal terminar<92>a en torno a -2.2% del PIB, seg<9c>n el Presupuesto General del Estado del presente a<96>o. Arribando ya al mensaje <de>nal, quiero abordar un tema que nos debe motivar a re<df>exiones como hacedores de pol<92>tica. Las amenazas a la econom<92>a mundial que se derivan del cambio clim<87>tico no son triviales y representan un reto para el crecimiento de largo plazo. Durante la citada reuni<97>n anual del FMI en Bali, Indonesia, los gobernadores del Banco de Francia y del Banco de Inglaterra, a<de>rmaron que, considerando los efectos perniciosos del calentamiento global sobre las econom<92>as, los bancos centrales tienen un rol que jugar en la lucha contra el cambio clim<87>tico, a trav<8e>s del dise<96>o de marcos regulatorios que incentiven a la banca a <de>nanciar actividades que favorezcan al medio ambiente. Asimismo, de acuerdo al economista reci<8e>n galardonado con el Premio Nobel, William Nordhaus, <d2>es necesario realizar ajustes a los sistemas productivos para que sea posible alcanzar una senda de crecimiento econ<97>mico que coexista con la sostenibilidad del medio ambiente<d3>. En este sentido el Banco Central forma parte del Consejo Nacional para el Cambio Clim<87>tico y Mecanismo de Desarrollo Limpio y tenemos en agenda la formulaci<97>n de pol<92>ticas y medidas que involucrar<87>n al sistema <de>nanciero nacional en apoyo a soluciones medioambientales. En esa direcci<97>n, estamos procediendo con la transformaci<97>n gradual de nuestras instalaciones para operar con el uso de energ<92>a renovable, y el Voluntariado del Banco Central se ha sumado a los ingentes esfuerzos que realiza el Gobierno, en materia de reforestaci<97>n para salvaguardar nuestras cuencas hidrogr<87><de>cas. Es indiscutible mis amigos, que tenemos por delante retos y desaf<92>os que s<97>lo pueden alcanzarse sobre la base de ampliar y fortalecer las alianzas estrat<8e>gicas p<9c>blicas-privadas. Para promover un crecimiento econ<97>mico m<87>s inclusivo, que destierre la inequidad, la desigualdad y la pobreza, necesitamos continuar mejorando la educaci<97>n y el acceso a la salud; generar empleos de calidad, desarrollar las potencialidades de nuestro Mercado de Valores, elevar nuestra competitividad y facilitar el emprendimiento de j<97>venes y de MIPYMES, entre otras iniciativas. Recientemente, el tambi<8e>n galardonado con el Premio Nobel de econom<92>a, Paul Romer, se<96>al<97> que la mejor forma para impulsar el 16/11/2022 19:15 crecimiento econ<97>mico sostenido es a trav<8e>s de la innovaci<97>n tecnol<97>gica, sustentada en la generaci<97>n de nuevas ideas, en la investigaci<97>n y en un capital humano m<87>s capacitado. Con esta fuerza motivadora para asumir el desaf<92>o de unir voluntades en aras de una mejor naci<97>n, como siempre concluyo mis palabras exhort<87>ndolos a que de manera entusiasta apostemos con fe y optimismo al futuro, por un mejor porvenir para todos los dominicanos. Title: Speech on the Seventy-Second Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: - 1.1.1.1.1 Li , DDiscurso delgobernador ct en e , rValdez Albizu Seventy-second anniversary 91 ddelBanco CentralddelaDominican Republic 23dde octubbredde 20 It is a true honor for me to address once again the Monetary Board, the staff of the bank and special guests, on the occasion of the celebration of the seventy-second anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, an institution created on this day in 1947, as the issuing entity of the national currency and executor of monetary policies, exchange and financial. After a long history of 72 years of institutional life, today we can say with certainty that we have a modern, transparent and highly credible central bank, committed to macroeconomic stability and sustained growth. These achievements have earned him numerous recognitions that have cemented his prestige, both in the national and international economic scenario, which should be a source of deep pride for the entire Bancentraliana family and the country. I must express to you with all humility, the great satisfaction I feel for the path traveled by the institution in these 22 years that I have had the opportunity to exercise the position of governor. In particular, I would like to express my gratitude to His Excellency the President of the Republic, Mr. Danilo Medina Sanchez, for his trust and for the unconditional support he has always given to the central bank, which has allowed it to carry out its functions with autonomy and independence, complying with the provisions of the Constitution of the Republic and the Monetary and Financial Law. Undoubtedly, the support received from the honorable members of the Monetary Board has been decisive in order to meet the objective of price stability and the proper functioning and security of the financial and payment systems. Likewise, we feel fortunate to have a team of officials and employees, with high academic training, with a high ethical and professional level, committed to excellence and the institutional values that identify us. I confess my dear friends personally that it is the constant guide of God, who can do everything, and the unconditional support and understanding of my beloved wife Fior, my dear son Hector Manuel, my beloved mother and my brothers, which impels me every day to fulfill my tasks with the enthusiasm and passion of always, sacrificing precious family time. Allow me, as is customary in each appearance on the occasion of the anniversary, to present to you an overview of the international panorama and the main results of the Dominican economy in the period January  September, as well as the prospects for the end of the year. I have just returned from the 2019 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings, held in Washington, DC. In these meetings, the challenge faced by economies, both the most advanced and emerging, in the face of a complex, convulsive international economic panorama with a high level of uncertainty was widely discussed. In particular, trade disputes between the United States and China, the imminent departure of the United Kingdom from the European Union (Brexit) and geopolitical tensions in several regions of the world, have caused a slowdown in international trade and a slowdown in global growth. As the new Managing Director of the IMF, Kristalina Georgieva, expressed in the plenary session of the aforementioned event, "a slowdown is observed in almost 90.0% of the world, projecting a growth of 3.0% in the world economy for 2019, the lowest rate since the beginning of the decade". In its forecasts for industrialized economies, the IMF estimates a growth of 2.4% for the United States of America in 2019, which means a slowdown compared to the 2.9% reached in 2018, product of a moderation in consumption and investment as a result of the trade war with China and the disappearance of the fiscal impulse from the tax reform of the Trump Administration. Likewise, the Eurozone would grow just 1.2% this year, as a result of a 16/11/2022 19:16 weak external demand and lower production of the industrial sector in countries such as Germany, Italy, among others. Regarding emerging economies, the IMF expects growth of 3.9% for 2019, a slowdown from the 4.5% reached in 2018. This reduction in growth is explained by less dynamism in large economies, mainly China and India, which after having achieved average growth above 7.0% between 2013 and 2018, would register expansions of around 6.1% this year. For Latin America and the Caribbean, the projections are less encouraging, with growth estimated at 0.2% in 2019 due to weakness in the region's two largest economies, Brazil and Mexico, which would grow less than 1.0%, and recessions in countries such as Venezuela, Argentina, Ecuador and Nicaragua. In this context, to counteract the negative impact of international uncertainty and the slowdown in countries' domestic growth, most of the world's central banks have initiated monetary easing processes, through reductions in their monetary policy interest rates and liquidity provision programs. For example, the Federal Reserve of the United States (FED) has been providing greater liquidity to the financial system, through repurchase agreements (repos) and the purchase of short-term Treasuries for about US 60,000 million per month. Likewise, the European Central Bank is implementing a liquidity provision program for the channeling of credit to the private sector, while it has resumed the purchase of sovereign debt assets, this time for an amount of 20,000 million euros per month. In Latin America, in addition to policy interest rate cuts in most countries, the central banks of Brazil, Chile, and Costa Rica have adopted liquidity programs to boost lending to the private sector. I am of the opinion that, in the times we live in, central banks must go beyond the traditional measures contained in textbooks and orthodoxy historically promoted by international bodies. In this new reality, the monetary policymaker must find alternative ways to provide liquidity to the economy, without jeopardizing its inflation target and stability. That is why, at the global level, along with interest rate reductions, unconventional monetary policy measures have been implemented. In the particular case of the Dominican Republic, faced with a complex international environment and the moderation of domestic economic activity during the first months of the year, the monetary policy rate was reduced by 100 basis points (from 5.50% in May to 4.50% today), while unconventional monetary easing measures were approved. particularly the release of resources from the legal reserve for more than RD 34 billion, to be channeled by financial intermediation entities to the productive sectors. These measures have managed to boost private credit in national currency, which has increased by RD 55,586.8 million since June to date. Of this amount, RD 25,197.6 million equivalent to 73.3% of the total released, correspond to legal reserve resources, while RD 30,389.2 million come from funds available for loans from financial intermediation entities. In year-on-year terms, credit to the private sector in national currency has grown by around 11.0% to date. Let me inform you at this time, dear friends, that preliminary figures confirm that monetary easing measures have had a positive effect on the Dominican economy. In that sense, I am pleased to announce to the country that in September real economic activity registered a year-on-year growth of 5.1%, after having reached 4.8% in August. Thus, during the first nine months of the year, the Gross Domestic Product registered a year-on-year growth of 4.8%, the highest in Latin America and the Caribbean. As Dominicans, we should be proud to maintain our position as the region's leading economy, despite the adverse environment we face. In this behavior, the activities with the highest incidence during the first nine months of the year were: Financial Services (8.8%), Construction (8.5%), Energy and Water (7.9%), Other Services Activities (6.9%), Transport (5.2%), Real Estate Activities (5.0%) and Agriculture (4.2%). As for the activity Hotels, Bars and Restaurants it should be noted that despite the 16/11/2022 19:16 As a result of a negative media campaign in international media about the Dominican Republic, it registered a positive year-on-year growth of 1.0% in January-September 2019. I think it is important to recognize that nothing structural has changed in tourism and that the country maintains its attractiveness as one of the main destinations in Latin America. For this reason, it is expected that in the short term tourism will recover the dynamism of recent years. In fact, the effects of the international media campaign on tourism have begun to subside, a process that should be accelerated after the Federal Bureau of Investigation of the United States (FBI) confirmed the version of the Dominican authorities that the deaths that originated the dissemination of negative information corresponded to natural causes. An important aspect to note is that the positive reaction of the economy to monetary measures has occurred in a context of price stability. Indeed, accumulated inflation as of September reached 2.38% and year-on-year inflation stood at 2.02%, remaining below the lower limit of the target range of 4.0% 1.0%, established in the Monetary Program. We cannot fail to mention that price stability has been maintained despite the fact that the drought that has affected the country caused higher food inflation, which was partially offset by the year-on-year fall in prices in the transport and housing sectors. As for the labor market, the latest figures available from the Continuous National Labor Force Survey reflect on average some 156,500 net new employed between April-June 2018 and April-June 2019, so in the seven years from October 2012 to June 2019 831,725 additional jobs have been accumulated. A point to highlight in the labor market figures is that the global participation rate, that is, the number of people of working age who are employed, stood at 65.2% in April-June 2019, a historical maximum for this indicator. In this same sense, the annualized average of the open unemployment rate, that is, that which includes people aged 15 and over, who are actively looking for work, stood at 5.9%, below the average of the countries of Latin America and the Caribbean, according to the latest figures available from the International Labor Organization (ILO). Beyond its effects on the labour market, economic growth has also contributed to improving other social indicators such as poverty and inequality. As stated in other forums, monetary poverty fell from 39.7% in 2012 to 22.8% at the end of 2018, this means that approximately one and a half million Dominicans managed to overcome the poverty line in six years. Within this behavior of general poverty, it is important to note that the proportion of extreme poverty or indigence fell from 9.9% to 2.9% during that same period, about six hundred and fifty thousand fewer indigents, which represents an extraordinary achievement. Likewise, a gradual decrease in inequality has been observed, measured by the Gini coefficient, which went from 0.487 in 2012 to 0.439 last year, indicating that the Dominican economy is among the four countries with the lowest level of inequality in the region, a fact that was highlighted by the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) in its recent publication Social Panorama of Latin America 2018 edition. With regard to the external accounts, we are pleased to share with you that, according to preliminary figures, the current account deficit for the January-September period was only US 587.6 million. It is important to note that foreign direct investment amounted to about US 2,040 million, an amount that would finance almost four times that deficit. Within the current account, total exports grew 2.9% year-on-year, reaching US 8,429.9 million as of September. Likewise, national exports, which represent 44.1% of total exports, increased 6.1% in January  September, highlighting mineral sales, which achieved a growth of 13.2%, mainly due to gold exports due to better international prices. As for tourism, the country received about 5 million visitors in January-September 2019, which meant revenues of US 5,767.2 million in the period, a slight decrease of 0.8% compared to the same period of the previous year. The lower performance of tourism was largely offset by remittances, which grew 8.8% year-on-year, some US 426.6 million additional to the 16/11/2022 19:16 registered as of September last year. As of October 18, international reserves amounted to US 7,668.6 million, equivalent to 4.2 months of imports of goods and services, excluding free zones. An indisputable achievement is that the country has strengthened its international reserve position without jeopardizing the relative stability of the exchange rate. In this sense, this year, despite the effects on the foreign exchange market of the adverse international scenario and the domestic environment characterized by the uncertainty of the electoral process, the accumulated depreciation remained below the Latin American average, reaching 4.9%. I am aware that recent movements in the foreign exchange market have generated apprehension in some sectors of society. Those who know me know that I have a non-negotiable commitment to exchange rate stability and that these situations that have arisen, as a result of political uncertainty, as I pointed out earlier, will be confronted and resolved in a forceful manner. In support of economic activity, we have a financial system that stands out for its liquidity, solvency and profitability, as well as the low level of risk of its loan portfolio. According to the Superintendency of Banks, as of August 2019, the solvency ratio was 18.15%, higher than the minimum ratio of 10.0% legally required. Likewise, as of September 2019, the profits of financial intermediaries reached RD 26,691.0 million, for a return on average equity (ROE) of 19.8% and on assets (ROA) of 2.4%. The delinquency rate stood at 1.69%, with provisions above 100%. With regard to multiple banks, which represent 86.8% of the net assets of the financial system, the return on equity amounted to 22.4%. Likewise, the delinquency of its loan portfolio was 1.63%, with a coverage of 174.2% on non-performing loans. Within the framework of the regulation of the financial system, the Monetary Board approved the amendment of the Exchange Regulations, incorporating the provisions on the Electronic Currency Trading Platform, administered by the Central Bank, as well as the establishment of new limits on the Net Position in Foreign Currency, with the purpose of contributing to preserving financial and exchange stability. In this regard, we are pleased to inform you that, since last Monday, October 21, 2019, multiple banks are transacting their operations within the Electronic Currency Platform, starting the first stage of the process of modernization of the exchange market in an electronic environment, of greater efficiency and transparency. Dear friends, allow me to refer to some issues that are currently the subject of discussion in central banks. Specifically, I want to highlight the role of these institutions in the regulation of financial technology companies, FINTECH, and in the implementation of computer security or cybersecurity mechanisms. In the Dominican Republic, with the assistance of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), we are developing the FINTECH regulations to provide legal certainty to the services offered by these companies, which constitute a more agile mechanism for financial inclusion. Regarding the strengthening of cybersecurity, the Central Bank is installing a Cyber Security Incident Response Center (CSIRT), which will be interconnected with the banking system with the aim of mitigating and strengthening the capacity to react to incidents that could affect financial institutions and other participants of the Payment System. Another issue that continues in the debate in international organizations, addressed again at the IMF meeting, is the call to central banks to a more proactive role in contributing solutions for the identification and mitigation of the impacts of climate change, given the risks they could present to the financial systems and productive activities of the countries. On this subject, the Dominican Government began in 2017 a broad reforestation plan, aimed at planting trees in the middle and upper watersheds of the southern region of the country. This plan, led by the presidency and the ministries of Agriculture and Environment, has as its main goal to intervene an area of 726,000 tasks. So far, almost 65.0% of the 16/11/2022 19:16 plan, having planted some 468,500 tasks of fruit and timber trees. Before concluding my statement, I would like to refer to the prospects for the Dominican economy. I think that despite the difficult environment that we have had to face this year, we will be able to achieve the goals we have set for ourselves. Taking into account the lagged effects of the reduction in the monetary policy rate and the resources of the legal reserve outstanding to be disbursed, which would leave the economy more quickly after the provision that eliminates the sectorization of these funds, aggregate demand is expected to continue to react positively, projecting growth close to the potential of 5.0% by the end of the year. That growth would be accompanied by inflation around 3.5%, within the target range of 4% 1%. Likewise, the gradual recovery of tourism, the dynamism of exports and remittances, would allow the current account of the balance of payments to close the year with a deficit of around 1.6% of GDP, well below its historical average. Foreign direct investment is also expected to exceed US 2,500.0 million in 2019. Dear friends, the Dominican Republic has undoubtedly demonstrated once again its resilience in difficult situations. It is indisputable that monetary policy has played a leading role in this process. As the IMF Managing Director mentioned in her speech quoted above, "the slowdown in growth requires monetary policy to continue to provide support. But it alone is not enough." In that regard, I must point out that we have succeeded in strengthening policy coordination with the Ministry of Finance. In the case of the recapitalization of the Central Bank, we have signed a memorandum of understanding that has already been approved by the Monetary Board, an organization that will know next week the draft modification of the recapitalization law that will later be sent to Congress via the Executive Branch. This major structural reform will contribute to a better ordering of monetary policy and public finances, as well as to debt sustainability and economic growth. It is important to emphasize that the sustained economic growth and the strengthening of macroeconomic fundamentals that the Dominican Republic has presented in recent years constitute the main basis for the development of private sector projects and the attraction of foreign investment. In addition, it is important to continue advancing in improving the competitiveness of the productive sectors, with the aim of increasing productivity and growth. We must also encourage public-private partnerships (PPPs) in order to increase strategic investments for long-term economic development. I would like to take this opportunity to urge all Dominicans to zealously care for the economic and social stability we exhibit and to join forces to continue building a better country, with equal opportunities and higher incomes for the most vulnerable population. As noted by French economist Thomas Piketty, author of the internationally bestselling book Capital in the Twenty-First Century, "it is important to recognize that innovation and growth alone are not enough to moderate wealth inequality." It is for this reason that we must promote policies that, in addition to contributing to growth, allow reduce inequality in income distribution and improve purchasing power at the base of Social pyramid. In all of us is the key to success. Definitely, this is a nation blessed by God, protected by the Virgin of Altagracia. Let us continue to bet optimistically on the future of our nation. Thanks a lot. 16/11/2022 19:16
