En sus pron<97>sticos para las econom<92>as industrializadas, el FMI estima un crecimiento de 2.4 % para Estados Unidos de Am<8e>rica en 2019, lo que signi<de>ca una desaceleraci<97>n con respecto al 2.9% alcanzado en 2018, producto de una moderaci<97>n en el consumo y la inversi<97>n como consecuencia de la guerra comercial con China y de la desaparici<97>n del impulso <de>scal proveniente de la reforma impositiva de la Administraci<97>n Trump. Asimismo, la Zona Euro crecer<92>a apenas 1.2 % en este a<96>o, como resultado de una 16/11/2022 19:16 demanda externa d<8e>bil y de una menor producci<97>n del sector industrial en pa<92>ses como Alemania, Italia, entre otros. En lo referente a las econom<92>as emergentes, el FMI espera un crecimiento de 3.9 % para 2019, una desaceleraci<97>n con respecto al 4.5 % alcanzado en 2018. Esta reducci<97>n del crecimiento est<87> explicada por un menor dinamismo en las econom<92>as grandes, principalmente China e India, que luego de haber alcanzado crecimientos promedio superiores a 7.0 % entre 2013 y 2018, registrar<92>an expansiones en torno a 6.1 % en el presente a<96>o. Para Am<8e>rica Latina y el Caribe, las proyecciones son menos alentadoras, estim<87>ndose un crecimiento de 0.2 % en 2019 por la debilidad en las dos econom<92>as de mayor tama<96>o de la regi<97>n, Brasil y M<8e>xico, que crecer<92>an menos de 1.0 %, y por recesiones en pa<92>ses como Venezuela, Argentina, Ecuador y Nicaragua. En este contexto, para contrarrestar el impacto negativo de la incertidumbre internacional y la desaceleraci<97>n del crecimiento dom<8e>stico de los pa<92>ses, la mayor<92>a de los bancos centrales del mundo han iniciado procesos de <df>exibilizaci<97>n monetaria, a trav<8e>s de reducciones en sus tasas de inter<8e>s de pol<92>tica monetaria y de programas de provisi<97>n de liquidez. Por ejemplo, la Reserva Federal de los Estados Unidos (FED) ha estado proporcionando mayor liquidez al sistema <de>nanciero, a trav<8e>s de acuerdos de recompra (repos) y de la compra de bonos del tesoro de corto plazo por unos US$ 60,000 millones mensuales. Asimismo, el Banco Central Europeo est<87> aplicando un programa de provisi<97>n de liquidez para la canalizaci<97>n de cr<8e>dito al sector privado, a la vez que ha retomado la compra de activos de deuda soberana, en esta ocasi<97>n por un monto de <db> 20,000 millones de euros mensuales. En Am<8e>rica Latina, en adici<97>n a las reducciones de tasas de inter<8e>s de pol<92>tica en la mayor<92>a de los pa<92>ses, los bancos centrales de Brasil, Chile y Costa Rica han adoptado programas de provisi<97>n de liquidez para dinamizar los pr<8e>stamos al sector privado. Soy de opini<97>n que, en los tiempos que vivimos, los bancos centrales deben ir m<87>s all<87> de las medidas tradicionales que contienen los libros de texto y la ortodoxia promovida hist<97>ricamente por los organismos internacionales. En esta nueva realidad, el hacedor de pol<92>tica monetaria debe encontrar formas alternativas de proveer liquidez a la econom<92>a, sin poner en riesgo su objetivo de in<df>aci<97>n y la estabilidad. Es por eso que, a nivel global, junto a las reducciones de tasas de inter<8e>s, se vienen implementando medidas de pol<92>tica monetaria no convencionales. En el caso particular de la Rep<9c>blica Dominicana, ante un entorno internacional complejo y frente a la moderaci<97>n de la actividad econ<97>mica dom<8e>stica durante los primeros meses del a<96>o, se redujo la tasa de pol<92>tica monetaria en 100 puntos b<87>sicos (de 5.50 % en mayo a 4.50 % en la actualidad), a la vez que se aprobaron medidas no convencionales de <df>exibilizaci<97>n monetaria, particularmente la liberaci<97>n de recursos del encaje legal por m<87>s de RD$ 34 mil millones, para ser canalizados por las entidades de intermediaci<97>n <de>nanciera a los sectores productivos. Estas medidas han logrado dinamizar el cr<8e>dito privado en moneda nacional, el cual se ha incrementado en RD$ 55,586.8 millones desde junio a la fecha. De este monto, RD$ 25,197.6 millones equivalentes al 73.3 % del total liberado, corresponden a recursos del encaje legal, mientras RD$ 30,389.2 millones proceden de fondos disponibles para pr<8e>stamos de las entidades de intermediaci<97>n <de>nanciera. En t<8e>rminos interanuales, el cr<8e>dito al sector privado en moneda nacional ha crecido en torno al 11.0 % a la fecha. Perm<92>tanme informarles en este momento, estimados amigos y amigas, que cifras preliminares con<de>rman que las medidas de <df>exibilizaci<97>n monetaria han tenido un efecto positivo en la econom<92>a dominicana. En ese sentido, me complace anunciar al pa<92>s que en el mes de septiembre la actividad econ<97>mica real registr<97> un crecimiento interanual de 5.1%, luego de haber alcanzado un 4.8% en el mes de agosto. De esta forma, durante los primeros nueve meses del a<96>o, el Producto Interno Bruto registr<97> un crecimiento interanual de 4.8% el m<87>s alto de Am<8e>rica Latina y el Caribe. Como dominicanos, debemos sentirnos orgullosos de mantener nuestra posici<97>n como econom<92>a l<92>der de la regi<97>n, a pesar del entorno adverso que enfrentamos. En este comportamiento, las actividades de mayor incidencia durante los primeros nueve meses del a<96>o fueron: Servicios Financieros (8.8 %), Construcci<97>n (8.5 %), Energ<92>a y Agua (7.9 %), Otras Actividades de Servicios (6.9 %), Transporte (5.2 %), Actividades Inmobiliarias (5.0 %) y Agropecuaria (4.2 %). En cuanto a la actividad Hoteles, Bares y Restaurantes es preciso destacar que no obstante las 16/11/2022 19:16 di<de>cultades por las que ha atravesado el turismo, como resultado de una campa<96>a medi<87>tica negativa en medios internacionales sobre Rep<9c>blica Dominicana, la misma registr<97> un crecimiento interanual positivo de 1.0% en enero-septiembre de 2019. Pienso que es importante reconocer que nada estructural ha cambiado en el turismo y que el pa<92>s mantiene su atractivo como uno de los principales destinos de Am<8e>rica Latina. Por esta raz<97>n, es de esperarse que en el corto plazo el turismo recupere el dinamismo de los <9c>ltimos a<96>os. De hecho, los efectos de la campa<96>a medi<87>tica internacional sobre el turismo han comenzado a ceder, proceso que deber<87> acelerarse luego de que el Bur<97> Federal de Investigaciones de los Estados Unidos (FBI) con<de>rmara la versi<97>n de las autoridades dominicanas de que los decesos que originaron la difusi<97>n de informaci<97>n negativa correspondieron a causas naturales. Un aspecto importante a destacar es que la reacci<97>n positiva de la econom<92>a a las medidas monetarias se ha dado en un contexto de estabilidad de precios. En efecto, la in<df>aci<97>n acumulada al mes de septiembre alcanz<97> 2.38 % y la in<df>aci<97>n interanual se situ<97> en 2.02 %, manteni<8e>ndose por debajo del l<92>mite inferior del rango meta de 4.0 % <b1> 1.0 %, establecido en el Programa Monetario. No podemos dejar de mencionar que la estabilidad de precios se ha mantenido a pesar de que la sequ<92>a que ha afectado al pa<92>s provoc<97> una mayor in<df>aci<97>n de alimentos, la cual fue compensada parcialmente por la ca<92>da interanual de precios en los sectores de transporte y viviendas. En cuanto al mercado laboral, las <9c>ltimas cifras disponibles de la Encuesta Nacional Continua de Fuerza de Trabajo re<df>ejan en promedio unos 156,500 nuevos ocupados netos entre abril-junio 2018 y abril-junio 2019, por lo que en los siete a<96>os transcurridos desde octubre de 2012 a junio 2019 se han acumulado 831,725 empleos adicionales. Un punto a destacar en las cifras del mercado laboral es que, la tasa global de participaci<97>n, es decir, la cantidad de personas en edad de trabajar que se encuentra ocupada, se ubic<97> en 65.2% en abril-junio de 2019, un m<87>ximo hist<97>rico para este indicador. En este mismo sentido, el promedio anualizado de la tasa de desocupaci<97>n abierta, es decir, aquella que incluye a las personas de 15 a<96>os de edad y m<87>s, que se encuentran buscando activamente trabajo, se ubic<97> en 5.9%, por debajo del promedio de los pa<92>ses de Am<8e>rica Latina y el Caribe, seg<9c>n las <9c>ltimas cifras disponibles de la Organizaci<97>n Internacional del Trabajo (OIT). M<87>s all<87> de sus efectos en el mercado laboral, el crecimiento econ<97>mico tambi<8e>n ha contribuido a mejorar otros indicadores sociales como la pobreza y la desigualdad. Como se ha a<de>rmado en otros foros, la pobreza monetaria baj<97> de 39.7 % en el a<96>o 2012 a 22.8 % al cierre de 2018, esto signi<de>ca que aproximadamente un mill<97>n y medio de dominicanos lograron superar el umbral de la pobreza en seis a<96>os. Dentro de este comportamiento de la pobreza general, resulta importante destacar que la proporci<97>n de pobreza extrema o indigencia descendi<97> de 9.9 % a 2.9% durante ese mismo per<92>odo, unos seiscientos cincuenta mil indigentes menos, lo que representa un logro extraordinario. Asimismo, se ha observado una disminuci<97>n gradual de la desigualdad, medida por el coe<de>ciente de Gini, el cual pas<97> de 0.487 en 2012 a 0.439 el pasado a<96>o, indicando que la econom<92>a dominicana se encuentra entre los cuatro pa<92>ses de menor nivel de desigualdad en la regi<97>n, hecho que fue destacado por la Comisi<97>n Econ<97>mica para Am<8e>rica Latina y el Caribe (CEPAL) en su reciente publicaci<97>n Panorama Social de Am<8e>rica Latina edici<97>n 2018. En lo referente a las cuentas externas, nos complace compartir con ustedes que, de acuerdo a cifras preliminares, el d<8e><de>cit de cuenta corriente para el per<92>odo enero-septiembre fue de apenas US$ 587.6 millones. Es importante destacar que la inversi<97>n extranjera directa ascendi<97> a unos US$ 2,040 millones, monto que permitir<92>a <de>nanciar casi cuatro veces dicho d<8e><de>cit. Dentro de la cuenta corriente, las exportaciones totales crecieron 2.9 % interanual, alcanzando US$ 8,429.9 millones al mes de septiembre. Asimismo, las exportaciones nacionales, que representan un 44.1 % de las exportaciones totales, aumentaron 6.1 % en enero <d0> septiembre, destac<87>ndose las ventas de minerales, que lograron un crecimiento de 13.2 %, principalmente por las exportaciones de oro debido a los mejores precios internacionales. En cuanto al turismo, el pa<92>s recibi<97> cerca de 5 millones de visitantes en enero-septiembre de 2019, lo que signi<de>c<97> ingresos por US$ 5,767.2 millones en el per<92>odo, una ligera disminuci<97>n de 0.8 % con respecto a igual periodo del a<96>o anterior. El menor desempe<96>o del turismo fue compensando en gran medida por las remesas, las cuales crecieron 8.8 % interanual, unos US$ 426.6 millones adicionales a los 16/11/2022 19:16 registrados a septiembre del pasado a<96>o. Al 18 de octubre, las reservas internacionales ascendieron a US$ 7,668.6 millones, equivalentes a 4.2 meses de importaciones de bienes y servicios, excluyendo las zonas francas. Un logro indiscutible es que el pa<92>s ha fortalecido su posici<97>n de reservas internacionales sin poner en riesgo la estabilidad relativa del tipo de cambio. En ese sentido, en el presente a<96>o, a pesar de los efectos que sobre el mercado cambiario han tenido el escenario internacional adverso y el entorno dom<8e>stico caracterizado por la incertidumbre propia del proceso electoral, la depreciaci<97>n acumulada se mantuvo por debajo del promedio de Am<8e>rica Latina, alcanzando 4.9 %. Estoy consciente de que los movimientos recientes en el mercado cambiario han generado aprensi<97>n en algunos sectores de la sociedad. Los que me conocen saben que tengo un compromiso innegociable con la estabilidad cambiaria y que estas situaciones que se han presentado, producto de la incertidumbre pol<92>tica como se<96>al<8e> anteriormente, ser<87>n enfrentadas y resueltas de manera contundente. En apoyo a la actividad econ<97>mica, contamos con un sistema <de>nanciero que se destaca por su liquidez, solvencia y rentabilidad, as<92> como el bajo nivel de riesgo de su cartera de cr<8e>ditos. Seg<9c>n la Superintendencia de Bancos, a agosto 2019, el coe<de>ciente de solvencia fue de 18.15 %, superior al coe<de>ciente m<92>nimo de 10.0 % requerido legalmente. Asimismo, a septiembre 2019, las utilidades de los intermediarios <de>nancieros alcanzaron RD$ 26,691.0 millones, para una rentabilidad sobre el patrimonio promedio (ROE) de 19.8 % y sobre los activos (ROA) de 2.4%. El <92>ndice de morosidad se situ<97> en 1.69 %, con provisiones superiores al 100 por ciento. En lo referente a los bancos m<9c>ltiples, que representan el 86.8 % de los activos netos del sistema <de>nanciero, la rentabilidad del patrimonio ascendi<97> a 22.4 %. Asimismo, la morosidad de su cartera de cr<8e>ditos fue de 1.63%, con una cobertura de 174.2 % sobre cartera vencida. En el marco de la regulaci<97>n del sistema <de>nanciero, la Junta Monetaria aprob<97> la modi<de>caci<97>n del Reglamento Cambiario, incorporando las disposiciones sobre la Plataforma Electr<97>nica de Negociaci<97>n de Divisas, administrada por el Banco Central, as<92> como el establecimiento de nuevos l<92>mites a la Posici<97>n Neta en Moneda Extranjera, con el prop<97>sito de contribuir a preservar la estabilidad <de>nanciera y cambiaria. Sobre este particular, nos complace informarles que, desde el pasado lunes 21 de octubre de 2019, los bancos m<9c>ltiples se encuentran transando sus operaciones dentro de la Plataforma Electr<97>nica de Divisas, dando inicio a la primera etapa del proceso de modernizaci<97>n del mercado cambiario en un ambiente electr<97>nico, de mayor e<de>ciencia y transparencia. Apreciados amigos, perm<92>tanme referirme a algunos temas que en la coyuntura actual son objeto de discusi<97>n en los bancos centrales. Espec<92><de>camente, quiero destacar el rol de estas instituciones en la regulaci<97>n de las empresas de tecnolog<92>a <de>nanciera, FINTECH, y en la implementaci<97>n de mecanismos de seguridad inform<87>tica o ciberseguridad. En la Rep<9c>blica Dominicana, con la asistencia del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID), estamos elaborando la normativa de las FINTECH para conferir seguridad jur<92>dica a los servicios ofrecidos por estas empresas, que constituyen un mecanismo m<87>s <87>gil de inclusi<97>n <de>nanciera. En lo relativo al fortalecimiento de la ciberseguridad, en el Banco Central se est<87> instalando un Centro de Respuesta a Incidentes de Seguridad Cibern<8e>tica (CSIRT), el cual estar<87> interconectado con el sistema bancario con el objetivo de mitigar y fortalecer la capacidad de reacci<97>n ante incidentes que pudieran afectar las entidades <de>nancieras y dem<87>s participantes del Sistema de Pagos. Otro tema que contin<9c>a en el debate en los organismos internacionales, abordado nueva vez en la reuni<97>n del FMI, es el llamado a los bancos centrales a un rol m<87>s proactivo en la contribuci<97>n de soluciones para la identi<de>caci<97>n y atenuaci<97>n de los impactos del cambio clim<87>tico, dado los riesgos que podr<92>an presentar a los sistemas <de>nancieros y a las actividades productivas de los pa<92>ses. Sobre este tema, el Gobierno Dominicano inici<97> en el a<96>o 2017 un amplio plan de reforestaci<97>n, orientado a sembrar de <87>rboles las cuencas hidrogr<87><de>cas media y alta de la regi<97>n sur del pa<92>s. Dicho plan, liderado por la presidencia y los ministerios de Agricultura y Medio Ambiente, tiene como meta principal intervenir un <87>rea de 726,000 tareas. Hasta el momento se ha ejecutado casi un 65.0 % del 16/11/2022 19:16 plan, habiendo sembrado unas 468,500 tareas de <87>rboles frutales y maderables. Antes de concluir mi intervenci<97>n, quisiera referirme a las perspectivas de la econom<92>a dominicana. Pienso, que a pesar del entorno dif<92>cil que nos ha tocado enfrentar en el presente a<96>o, lograremos alcanzar las metas que nos hemos trazado. Tomando en consideraci<97>n los efectos rezagados de la reducci<97>n de la tasa de pol<92>tica monetaria y los recursos del encaje legal pendientes por desembolsar, los cuales saldr<92>an m<87>s r<87>pidamente a la econom<92>a tras la disposici<97>n que elimina la sectorizaci<97>n de estos fondos, se espera que la demanda agregada continu<8e> reaccionando positivamente, proyect<87>ndose un crecimiento cercano al potencial de 5.0 % para el cierre del a<96>o. Ese crecimiento vendr<92>a acompa<96>ado de una in<df>aci<97>n en torno a 3.5 %, dentro del rango meta de 4% <b1> 1%. Asimismo, la recuperaci<97>n gradual del turismo, el dinamismo de las exportaciones y de las remesas, permitir<92>an que la cuenta corriente de la balanza de pagos cierre el a<96>o con un d<8e><de>cit alrededor de 1.6 % del PIB, muy por debajo de su promedio hist<97>rico. Se espera de igual forma que la inversi<97>n extranjera directa supere los US$ 2,500.0 millones en 2019. Estimados amigos, la Rep<9c>blica Dominicana sin duda alguna ha demostrado una vez m<87>s su capacidad de resiliencia ante situaciones dif<92>ciles. Es indiscutible que en este proceso la pol<92>tica monetaria ha jugado un rol de primer orden. Como mencion<97> la Directora-Gerente del FMI en su discurso citado anteriormente, <d2>la desaceleraci<97>n del crecimiento requiere que la pol<92>tica monetaria siga brindando apoyo. Pero, por s<92> sola no basta.<d3> En ese sentido, debo se<96>alar que hemos logrado fortalecer la coordinaci<97>n de pol<92>ticas con el Ministerio de Hacienda. En el caso de la recapitalizaci<97>n del Banco Central, hemos <de>rmado un memor<87>ndum de entendimiento que ya fue aprobado por la Junta Monetaria, organismo que conocer<87> en la pr<97>xima semana el proyecto de modi<de>caci<97>n de la ley de recapitalizaci<97>n que posteriormente ser<87> remitido al Congreso v<92>a el Poder Ejecutivo. Esta importante reforma estructural contribuir<87> a un mejor ordenamiento de la pol<92>tica monetaria y las <de>nanzas p<9c>blicas, as<92> como a la sostenibilidad de la deuda y al crecimiento econ<97>mico. Es importante destacar que el crecimiento econ<97>mico sostenido y el fortalecimiento de los fundamentos macroecon<97>micos que ha presentado la Rep<9c>blica Dominicana en los <9c>ltimos a<96>os constituyen la base principal para el desarrollo de los proyectos del sector privado y la atracci<97>n de inversi<97>n extranjera. En adici<97>n, es importante continuar avanzando en la mejor<92>a de la competitividad de los sectores productivos, con el objetivo de incrementar la productividad y el crecimiento. Asimismo, debemos fomentar las alianzas p<9c>blico-privadas (APP) con el <de>n de aumentar inversiones estrat<8e>gicas para el desarrollo econ<97>mico de largo plazo. Quisiera aprovechar la oportunidad para exhortar a todos los dominicanos y dominicanas, a cuidar con celo la estabilidad econ<97>mica y social que exhibimos y a aunar esfuerzos para continuar construyendo un mejor pa<92>s, con igualdad de oportunidades y mayores ingresos para la poblaci<97>n m<87>s vulnerable. Como se<96>al<97> el economista franc<8e>s Thomas Piketty, autor del libro, <8e>xito de ventas internacional, El Capital en el Siglo XXI, <d2>es importante reconocer que la innovaci<97>n y el crecimiento por s<92> mismos no son su<de>cientes para moderar la desigualdad de las riquezas<d3>. Es por esta raz<97>n que debemos promover pol<92>ticas que adem<87>s de contribuir al crecimiento, permitan reducir la desigualdad en la distribuci<97>n del ingreso y mejorar el poder adquisitivo en la base de la pir<87>mide social. En todos nosotros est<87> la clave del <8e>xito. De<de>nitivamente, esta es una naci<97>n bendecida por Dios, protegida por la Virgen de la Altagracia. Sigamos apostando con optimismo al futuro de nuestra naci<97>n. Muchas gracias. 16/11/2022 19:16

Title: Speech at the 2019 Grand Investor Gala
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: - 1.1.1.1.1 Li , DDiscurso delgobernador ct enlaGr , orValdez Albizu9102 an GaladelInversionista On behalf of the Central Bank, and on my own behalf, I would like to thank engineer Marius De Leon, executive director of the Export and Investment Center of the Dominican Republic, for his kind invitation to share with you the central words of this significant event in which special recognition is given to foreign investors. For those who speak to you, it is a great honor to address this distinguished audience composed of a representation of important foreign investors, local businessmen and officials from different areas of the public sector. In this intervention, we will refer to the valuable contributions generated by foreign direct investment for the development of a small and open economy, such as the Dominican Republic, as it constitutes one of the most important sources of financing for projects in the different economic sectors. In addition, foreign direct investment generates other important benefits for the productive activities of the economy such as the transfer of knowledge and new technologies and the adoption of international best practices, contributing, not only to the generation of foreign exchange and direct and indirect jobs, but also to the increase of productivity, innovation and better human capital. The foreign direct investment received by the main economic sectors of the country, such as Tourism, Telecommunications, Free Trade Zones, Mining and Commerce, just to mention some of the sectors, confirms the confidence that many of the companies represented here have placed in the growth and macroeconomic stability, legal security and climate of social peace of the Dominican Republic. Moreover, in an era like the present, characterized by a complicated international environment, convulsive and with great uncertainty for investment and the development of productive activities. In this challenging international environment, foreign direct investment in the Dominican Republic has averaged 2.5 billion over the past 10 years, totaling some 27 billion. This amount of investment, contrary to what was reported by the press last week, is higher than that received by the economies of Central America, except Panama, a country that is considered an international financial center, regional leader in offshore banking, and that has the Panama Canal, a majestic work that divides two oceans, and that required a public and private investment of about US 6,000 million for its expansion. I do not intend to make comparisons with the Central American countries in terms of gross domestic product, since ours is almost double the average GDP of these countries. For example, if we compare the average flows of foreign direct investment for the last 5 years, the Dominican Republic is above the others, given that Nicaragua reached US 704 million, Guatemala US 1,055 million, Honduras US 1,065 million and Costa Rica US 2,450 million. Similarly, our country surpasses other Latin American countries such as Uruguay, a recipient of Argentine funds due to its proximity and political security, which attracted an average investment for the same period of US2,216.8 million; and even exceeds other larger countries, such as Ecuador, which received foreign direct investment flows of US978 million in those years. I must emphasize that this flow of investment received in our country is so important that since 2014 it has financed the current account deficit of the Dominican Republic. Of this total, 70% is concentrated in the tourism, trade and real estate sectors, with the main countries of origin being the United States, Canada, Brazil, Spain and Mexico. Moreover, it is important to note that we currently have investment records from a total of 92 countries that have bet on the advantages offered by this nation. In this way, the Dominican Republic has managed to position itself as one of the most dynamic economies in the world, with an average growth of 6.2% in the period 2013-2018, the highest in Latin America during that period. It is important to note that this economic expansion has been accompanied by a climate of low inflation, exchange rate stability and job creation, elements that 16/11/2022 19:16 They are very relevant for international investors. Distinguished friends, I believe it is prudent and timely to reflect briefly on how the Dominican Republic has consistently achieved this outstanding performance. I am convinced that the answer lies in two fundamental pillars: the strengthening of the macroeconomic fundamentals of our country, through the implementation of effective economic policies, both fiscal and monetary, which have contributed to the maintenance of stability, and the execution of a broad process of reforms for the encouragement and promotion of foreign direct investment. in particular with the liberalization of the investment regime and the granting of national treatment to foreign investors with the enactment of Law 16-95, which implies that foreign investments are subjected to neutral or equivalent treatment, compared to domestic investments. With regard to structural reforms, we must highlight the strengthening over the past three decades of the legal and institutional framework that provides protection and clear rules of the game to investors who decide to bet on national development. Among the advances in legal matters we can mention the Law on the Promotion of Free Zones, the Law on the Securities Market, the Law on Intellectual Property, the Law on the Promotion of Tourism Development, the Law on Unfair Trade Practices and Safeguard Measures, the Law on Competitiveness and Industrial Innovation, the Law on the Defense of Competition and the Law on the Promotion of Cinematographic Activity. Likewise, we can highlight other laws that are in the process of approval and that also affect the investment climate, such as the Law of Public-Private Partnerships, the Law of Territorial Planning, the Law of National Mining, among others. No less important is the port and land transit infrastructure that the country has, and the advances exhibited in terms of competitiveness that made us improve 5 of the 10 indicators evaluated by the World Bank in its "Doing Business 2020" ranking, especially in the aspects of business opening, property registration and contract compliance. All of the above, framed in an environment where social peace reigns and the political stability that characterizes us, has consistently favored, since the end of 2014, the country-risk indicator (EMBI) is below the Latin American average, strengthening the favorable perception of international investors in the Dominican economy. However, I do not fail to recognize that, as has been noted by Her Excellency the Ambassador of the United States of America, Robin Bernstein, there is a way to go, and that there are still certain obstacles and aspects to improve, such as the reduction of bureaucracy, institutional strengthening, transparency and the streamlining of procedures for the creation of new companies and acquisition of real estate. which is related to building and land use permits, so that we can attract more and more foreign direct investment. We must therefore ponder and thank the concern and suggestions expressed by the distinguished ambassador of our main trading partner, and continue to strengthen the investment climate in the Dominican Republic. On the side at hand, allow me to mention that the institution that I am honoured to lead has maintained a proactive monetary policy that has been reflected in sustained economic growth with price stability, maintaining adequate coordination with fiscal policy, in order to promote certainty in economic agents and a favorable climate for investment. Likewise, to keep pace with the times in terms of the use of technologies in activities of a financial nature, the Central Bank is in the process of installing a Cyber Security Incident Response Center (CSIRT), with the aim of mitigating and strengthening the reaction capacity to incidents that could affect the entities of the financial system and other participants of the national Payment System. Likewise, it put into operation an Electronic Currency Trading Platform, through which multiple banks are transacting their foreign exchange operations under a system of greater efficiency, fluidity and transparency for the foreign exchange market. Likewise, the Central Bank contemplates in its current Institutional Strategic Plan the evaluation of regulations for financial technology companies (FINTECH), with the support of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), to confer security and legal certainty to the transactions carried out through these figures, for which a regulation is being prepared. I think, dear friends, that the implementation of coordinated public policies, together with good macroeconomic performance and the appropriate legal framework, have allowed foreign direct investment to grow and diversify among the different sectors of the Dominican economy, promoting a 16/11/2022 19:16 demand for increasingly technical and specialized labor, which has favored increasing productivity in our economy. To mention some examples, the transformation that the free zone sector has evidenced, from an eminently maquila export model, to a broad diversification of industrial manufacturing and services, developing manufacturing industries of jewelry, medical equipment and parts of advanced computer systems, among others, is highlighted. Likewise, the mining activity has led to the development and innovation of practices and technical knowledge in this area, which we are convinced augur greater results in the future. The tourism sector has been the largest beneficiary of foreign direct investment in recent years, embarking on the development of projects for greater diversity in the offer of services, from the most demanding tastes, to adventure ecotourism in different geographical areas of the country. To mention an example, only in the area that covers from Puerto Plata to Samana, we have records of 12 foreign capital projects in the last three years, with a total investment of more than US 223 million. And at the national level, some 33 projects are currently being executed for a total value of US885 million. Of these projects, 30 are new hotel complexes that, together with the expansions of existing ones, are estimated to add some 13 thousand rooms to the national offer in the coming years. Another sector that should be mentioned is real estate, which has recently gained an important share in total foreign direct investment, and for this year it is estimated a flow of around US 29 million among some 15 projects that we have identified. On the other hand, in the energy sector, there is an increasing commitment to clean sources that come from the sun and wind, and only for this year an investment flow of about US 117 million is estimated distributed among some 7 projects of this type. Similarly, the free zone, mining and financial sectors continue to provide significant flows to sustain external accounts. Distinguished personalities, investors present and friends all, I cannot finish this dissertation without referring to the panorama we glimpse. Today, we face an international environment with high levels of uncertainty, associated with the trade disputes between the United States and China, the lack of agreement for Brexit and the escalation of socio-political tensions in several regions of the world, including our Latin America. In this context, the IMF projects that the world economy would grow 3.0% this year, its lowest level in a decade. Despite these adverse conditions, in the domestic context, preliminary information from the monthly index of economic activity (IMAE) indicates that domestic demand continues to react favorably after the implementation of monetary easing measures. Indeed, the economy expanded 5.2% year-on-year in October, after having reached 5.1% in September. Thus, the average growth during the January-October period was 4.8%. This dynamism registered by economic activity in recent months would contribute to the economic growth of the Dominican Republic being around its potential of 5.0% at the end of the year, maintaining leadership in the Latin American and Caribbean region that according to the IMF would barely grow 0.2%. In addition, price stability would be maintained, with inflation closing between 3.5% and 4%, within the target range of 4% 1% of the Central Bank's Monetary Program. As for the external sector, the current account deficit of the balance of payments is projected to be around 1.6% of GDP, well below its historical average, thanks to the dynamism of remittances and exports, as well as the gradual recovery of tourism. It is important to note that foreign direct investment will exceed US 2,600 million during this year 2019, which would be equivalent to a coverage of more than twice the current account deficit. In summary, the fundamentals of the Dominican economy will continue to strengthen, so that the country can continue to grow steadily and maintain its leadership at the regional level. As we have mentioned, this commitment rests on the united commitment of all sectors, without ever looking away from our export vocation, which is undoubtedly the bet that as a country we have defended for many years and continue to defend, with a firm conviction that it is our key to economic development and prosperity for all of us who continue to trust in this island that by the grace of God has it. "9102-4102o Ma" and duct "2102y7002o Enel Io ambt Merca On behalf of the authorities of the Central Bank and myself, I am pleased to welcome you warmly on the occasion of the launch of the new "Quarterly Labour Market Bulletin" associated with the National Continuous Labour Force Survey (ENCFT). Taking advantage of the fact that 22 quarters have already been accumulated, that is, five and a half years of observations associated with the new continuous survey, this afternoon an "Diagnosis of the Labor Market 2014-2019" will be additionally presented, based on the analysis of the evolution of the main indicators of the labor market in the Dominican Republic. As you all know, the Central Bank has a long tradition of conducting household surveys compiling statistics that allow analyzing the situation of individuals in the labor market, their income and living conditions. After two decades of data collection under the scheme of cross-sectional surveys, that is, carried out twice a year in the months of April and October with independent samples that did not allow the monitoring of the same dwelling over time, the Central Bank adopted the modality of continuous survey for its labor survey. In this sense, the staff is in the field conducting interviews during 48 of the 52 weeks of the year, which constitutes an improvement in terms of design, allowing to obtain representative results on a quarterly basis and to perform panel analysis with greater analytical richness than the previous traditional survey. It should be noted, friends present, that the sample size of the continuous survey is 8,480 homes selected each quarter, which translates into some 6,625 effective quarterly interviews, accumulating a total of 26,500 questionnaires satisfactorily completed by Dominican households throughout the national territory. In this sense, the survey is representative for statistical inference purposes in the four large geographical regions of the country, this is the Greater Santo Domingo, the North or Cibao region and the East and South regions, being the sample of the continuous survey superior by more than 65% in terms of effective interviews compared to the previous traditional survey. For the implementation of the new labor survey, the Department of National Accounts and Economic Statistics had the technical support of the International Labour Organization (ILO) and the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC). An aspect of great relevance to note is that the questionnaire of the new survey incorporated all the changes in the definitions of the main indicators of the labor force and the guidelines for the estimation of informality emanating from the Nineteenth International Conference of Labour Statisticians of 2013, a conference that the ILO organizes every 5 years with the presence of the entities responsible for labor surveys throughout the world. The compliance of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic with the aforementioned guidelines of the ILO, being the pioneer country together with Brazil in the region in implementing them, motivated this international organization to invite this institution to hold the Vice-Presidency of the Twentieth International Conference of Labour Statisticians that took place at the ILO headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland in October 2018, leading 7 of the 14 plenary sessions from which new statistical resolutions emerged that will be implemented in the coming years, keeping the country at the forefront in the field of labour statistics at the international level. The most relevant changes include the monitoring of 4 indicators of underutilization of the labor force, the first of them being the open unemployment rate, that is, of people over 15 years of age who are unemployed and are actively looking for work. The other three additional indicators that allow us to study the people who are somehow being 16/11/2022 19:16 1 sur 3 Firefox about:blank underutilized in the labor market, such as those who would like to work longer hours, as well as the unemployed who would be willing to work even if they are not looking for a job in the market or those who are looking for work but are not available to work immediately. Likewise, with regard to the measurement of informality, the modern criterion of identification of formal and informal workers is incorporated, based on access or not to social security benefits via occupation, instead of using the criterion of the early eighties recommended by ECLAC, which considered informal people working in establishments with less than five people and which also focused the analysis on strictly urban environment, excluding rural informality. To accompany the quarterly dissemination of the labor market indicators that are released through the website of this institution, the Department of National Accounts and Economic Statistics has designed a descriptive bulletin that will accompany henceforth every three months the results of the different variables of the Dominican labor market. The first edition of the "Quarterly Bulletin of the Labour Market" that is being made official this afternoon includes an analysis of the behaviour of employment and indicators of underutilization, as well as the dynamics of transition between the different conditions of the labour market (occupation, unemployment and inactivity), informality in the labour market and the evolution of the income of the employed. among other relevant aspects. The bulletin has two sections, one that presents a year-on-year analysis, that is, comparing the results of each quarter with the same quarter of the previous year and another with an annual perspective with the averages of the last four quarters, which allows to isolate in both cases any effect of a seasonal nature of the data. As I told you at the beginning of these words, the launch of this new bulletin is accompanied today by a diagnostic analysis of the Dominican labor market for the period 2014-2019, where you can see the evolution of the main indicators of the labor market in the last five years. In addition to the analysis of the labor market, today a document that is an integral part of the statistical sequence of the National Accounts is being made available to the general public, it is the "Input-Output Matrix", which is presented both for the year 2007, current reference of the national accounts and for the year 2012, following the usual practice of updating this type of tools every five years. The next output input matrix will be broader and will be disclosed within the framework of the new national accounts referenced to the year 2018, for which work is currently being done. The input-output matrix is an instrument of great relevance for economic analysis since they are ideal for studying the effects on national productive activity of changes induced by economic policies in demand levels or by exogenous changes that impact the production and consumption decisions of economic agents. Matrices make it possible to analyse the reaction of domestic production in a particular sector or in the economy as a whole due to changes in final demand for specific products or economic activities. This analysis is carried out through coefficients that illustrate the various intersectoral transactions to satisfy their own intermediate demand or final use, starting from the model originally created by Professor Leontief of Harvard University and later of New York University, and for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1973. In general, matrices are very useful for a wide variety of studies, always illustrating the interrelationships between the various economic activities, highlighting the reaction of the economy to shocks in aggregate demand or supply. Tonight we will have two presentations, the first where the evolution of the main indicators of the Dominican labor market will be appreciated will be in charge of Dr. Ramon Gonzalez Hernandez, Deputy Manager of National Accounts and Economic Statistics and the second on the most relevant aspects of the input-output matrix will be made by Elina Rosario, director of the Department of National Accounts and Economic Statistics. 16/11/2022 19:16 2 sur 3 Firefox about:blank Once again, dear colleagues and friends, I am pleased to present these documents, as they reflect the continuous effort and commitment of this Central Bank with the dissemination of timely and quality economic information, and which I am sure will be appreciated by researchers, analysts and economic agents in general. To all of you, thank you very much for your assistance and my desire that you get the most out of these documents that we make available to all, to contribute to the strengthening and improvement of the design and formulation of economic and socio-labor policies in the country. Title: Speech on the Seventy-Third Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: - DDiscurso delgober Nador T en e , or Valdez Albizu The seventy-third anniversary of the Central Zone of the Dominican Republic Today is a special day for all Bancentralians, as we commemorate the seventy-third anniversary of the creation of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic as the issuing entity of the Dominican peso and executor of monetary, exchange and financial policies. By fulfilling every day its constitutional and legal mandate to preserve price stability and ensure the proper functioning of the financial and payment system, the Central Bank demonstrates its commitment to the development of the nation, as do all of us who are part of this great family. Personally, I wish to express my gratitude to God, for allowing me to continue in health at the head of this prestigious institution, in which I have put heart and soul for most of my adult life, in the incessant search for stability and Dominican economic growth. Allow me also to express my gratitude to His Excellency the President of the Republic, Luis Abinader, for the great distinction and confidence he has given me, in such complex and difficult times for the Dominican economy and the world, by confirming me for a new period as Governor of the Central Bank; responsibility that I assume with the same determination and dedication with which I have held the position for more than two decades. In the same way, I would especially like to thank my wife Fior and my son Hector Manuel, my beloved mother and my brothers, for their unconditional love and advice, for accompanying me, understanding me and always supporting me in the fulfillment of my responsibilities towards the country, despite the high family and personal sacrifice that they demand. Certainly, the work done by the Central Bank, under the leadership of the honorable members of the Monetary Board, is the result of the joint work of its officials and employees; those who work tirelessly long hours, inspired by a mystique of excellence that allows us to achieve institutional objectives, in line with the best interests of society. As is tradition, and in compliance with the Central Bank's policy of transparency and accountability, I will present the main indicators on the performance of the economy for the current year and the outlook for next year. On this occasion, I cannot deny that I am moved by the devastating effects that the health crisis has had on humanity and in particular, on our country, in terms of health, production, employment, tourism, education, culture, in short, practically in all sectors and activities. The reality is that much of the world has entered into recession and global policymakers have been challenged to design and implement new strategies to ease the burden on those segments of the population most affected by the pandemic. This great challenge has been firmly assumed, determined to put our economies back on track on the path of progress and prosperity, for as the great Albert Einstein said: "It is in crises that initiative, discoveries and great strategies are born." International environment, monetary policy and inflation After a sharp contraction in economic activity in the second quarter of this year, a large part of the world's economies began a process of gradual reopening, creating the conditions for a moderate recovery of the productive sectors. The impact of this decision was reflected in the latest World Economic Outlook Report of the International Monetary Fund (WEO) that moderated its projection of the decline of the world economy for 2020, from 4.9% in June to 4.4% in October. In the case of the United States of America, our main trading and financial partner, the The IMF's economic outlook indicates that output would fall 4.3% in real terms, a Important correction of 8.0% initially planned. 16/11/2022 19:16 On the other hand, the Eurozone, where a large number of countries are experiencing a second wave of the pandemic, would be contracting by 8.3% in 2020. With regard to Latin America, an estimated reduction of 8.1% influenced by larger countries such as Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Peru, which together have registered more than 9 million infections. In this challenging situation, most of the world's central banks have assumed markedly expansionary positions, and in this process the Dominican Republic has not been the exception. In a timely manner and since the beginning of the crisis, the Central Bank designed and implemented the most comprehensive monetary stimulus plan in the entire Central American and Caribbean region. In this way, it has focused its efforts on providing liquidity to the financial system, in order to guarantee the flow of credit to the productive sectors, under conditions of more favorable terms and interest rates, particularly for micro, small and medium enterprises, trying to preserve employment and protect the income of the most vulnerable households during the health crisis. Indeed, since March of this year the Central Bank has reduced the monetary policy interest rate by 150 basis points, from 4.50% to 3.00% per year, its lowest historical level; at the same time it decided to narrow the interest rate corridor, decreasing the rate of the permanent liquidity expansion facility (1-day Repos) from 6.00% to 3.50% per year, while the rate of remunerated deposits (Overnight) was reduced from 3.00% to 2.50% per year. Likewise, some RD190 billion (more than 4% of GDP) was made available to financial intermediation entities, of which RD60 billion correspond to repos up to one year that function as a revolving credit line for the financial system; and RD130 billion come from the release of legal reserve requirements, windows for financing strategic sectors and the rapid liquidity facility. The latter allows the restructuring of credits for debtors who have been affected by the temporary closure of activities, with lower interest rates and longer terms. To date, of the RD130 billion available, some RD123 billion (95% of the total) have been disbursed to more than 50,000 beneficiaries. In addition to these monetary and financial measures to combat the economic effects of COVID-19, the Central Bank proactively managed with the International Monetary Fund the disbursement of some US650 million through Rapid Financing, an instrument that this multilateral organization made available to countries in the current situation. This amount, equivalent to 100% of the country's quota, has been used to strengthen international reserves and to support the Government's public policies budget. I must inform you that these measures have been extremely successful in easing monetary conditions. It should be noted that since the first decisions were made, there has been a decrease of more than 300 basis points in the weighted average of the active interest rate of multiple banks, which went from 13.28% in March to 9.95% in September, as well as net loans to the private sector in national currency show a year-on-year growth of 10.4%, one of the highest in Latin America. Given that recently different media have reviewed the rise in prices of products of the basic basket, I want to be emphatic that these are transitory pressures in some foods of high weighting in it, which are related to the lagged impact of environmental factors such as drought and the passage of tropical storms Isaias and Laura, that affected productivity and supply in the market of several items. Indeed, accumulated inflation during the first nine months of the year was 3.74%, while annualized inflation to September was around the upper limit of the target range of 4.0% 1.0% and is expected to remain on average within that range over the monetary policy horizon. Real sector I am convinced my friends that the timely implementation of these monetary measures, together with a fiscal policy aimed at expanding the social protection network to the most vulnerable sectors of the population, which were extended by the government until the end of the year, have contributed significantly to the effects of the pandemic on the economy. employment and household income are less severe. In this order, there has been a sustained trend towards the recovery of economic activity. 16/11/2022 19:16 in recent months. I take this opportunity to report that the preliminary figures available reflect that the monthly indicator of economic activity (IMAE) registered a year-on-year variation of -5.6% in September, a substantial improvement of 24.2 percentage points compared to the -29.8% observed when the economy bottomed out in April; That is, the contraction of the economy in September was 5 times less than that registered in April. With this result, the accumulated variation of the gross domestic product (GDP) in January-September stood at -8.1%. It is important to note that, excluding the hotels, bars and restaurants sector, undoubtedly the sector most affected by the pandemic, the rest of the economic activities on average exhibit a significant recovery, going from -12.6% in April-June to -3.0% in July-September. Among the activities that registered a positive behavior during January-September 2020 are: health (12.4%); financial services (9.2%); Real estate activities (4.2%) and agriculture (3.8%) communications (2.1%); public administration (2.1%) and energy and water (1.1%). The agricultural sector has remained in positive territory thanks to central government support policies aimed at preserving the supply chain and ensuring the country's food security. In addition, it is expected that this sector will continue to strengthen with the creation of a financing program for RD 5 billion at zero rate for producers through the Agricultural Bank, for new crops. In the construction sector, after a forced pause due to the confinement, the private sector has resumed the gradual execution of investment projects, while the public sector announces various infrastructure works and conditioning of land roads. In this sense, it is expected that construction will be decisive for the consolidation of the recovery, as it has been historically, given its multiplier effect and its great capacity to drag the rest of the productive activities. On the other hand, given the challenges that persist in tourism, the government has implemented the Responsible Tourism Recovery Plan that seeks to establish the Dominican Republic as a safe destination and promote the Country Brand, combining health and safety protocols with incentives for companies in the sector and financing and pricing strategies to promote domestic tourism. In accordance with the above, His Excellency the President of the Republic, Luis Abinader, has visited several provinces of the national territory, promoting the initiation or continuation of tourism investment projects. Among the initiatives announced by the president are the boost that will be given to the development of the hotel offer in Bahia de las aguilas, while the tourist poles of the East and North zones continue their expansion process. Likewise, the road infrastructure in Samana will be improved and the Amber Highway will be built, which will connect Santiago and Puerto Plata much more expeditiously. In addition, the Government will remodel more than 30,000 homes throughout the country through the "Dominican Republic is Rebuilt" program and will proceed to modernize the port of Manzanillo that will be the center of logistics operations in the northern region. These measures will contribute significantly to economic recovery and job creation. External sector With regard to the external sector, preliminary balance of payments figures show the country's great capacity to face unfavorable international environments with determination, such as the one that has arisen as a result of the spread of the coronavirus. This position of resilience is observed in the current account deficit that reached US1,014.7 million in January-September, a much better result than initially projected for a country that for several months was forced to completely close the economic activity that generates the most foreign exchange, tourism; whose revenues compared to the same period of 2019 went from US 5,759.5 million to US 1,992.9 million. This decrease has been offset by the interventions of the Central Bank in the foreign exchange market through its electronic platform, managing to make up for the transitory mismatch generated by the closure of the foreign exchange generating sectors, for more than US 5,000 million. It should be noted that even under these adverse conditions, foreign direct investment (FDI) continues to flow to the country, to the point of reaching US2,066.4 million in January-September, an amount that 16/11/2022 19:16 It makes it possible to finance more than twice the current account deficit of the same period. This result represents a growth in foreign direct investment of 4.0% compared to 2019, driven mainly by the communications and mining sectors. On the export side, it is important to note that if the month of September is taken exclusively, total exports grew 4.5% year-on-year, driven mainly by the recovery of the free zone sector, whose exports increased 9.8%, as well as by exports from the agricultural sector that grew 15.0% in the aforementioned month. However, in January-September there was a year-on-year reduction of 9.0%, reaching about US 7,535.6 million. It should be noted that the effects of the health crisis on the goods and services export sector have been partially cushioned by a better-than-expected performance in remittances. In September alone, the flow of remittances to the country increased for the fifth consecutive month, reaching some US777.4 million, a year-on-year growth of 37.1%. In the first nine months of the year, remittances amounted to US5,849.8 million, an additional US556.9 million (10.5%) to those registered in the same period last year. This result is mainly due to the reduction of the unemployment rate in the United States from 14.7% in April to 7.9% in September, where more than 80% of these flows come from, as well as the financial assistance provided by the US Government to the unemployed in that country, which has benefited the Dominican diaspora. On the import side, a recovery is beginning to be observed, particularly in non-oil imports which, after registering a variation of -21.9% year-on-year in August, fell 7.4% during the month of September. In the case of imports from free zones, the performance was even better, exhibiting in September a growth of 12.0% for the first time after the reopening of the economy. This, my friends, is good news that indicates that the economy is on the right track. It should be noted that the active participation of the Central Bank in the foreign exchange market at times of greatest uncertainty in the first months of confinement, added to the dynamism of remittances and the recent improvement in exports, have been key to maintaining the relative stability of the exchange rate. Another factor that has contributed in this direction has been the successful placement of sovereign bonds in international markets for US 3,800 million, which has allowed to increase International Reserves to above US 10,500 million, 13.0% of GDP higher than the metric recommended by the IMF, at the end of September. Institutional scope On the other hand, in the institutional sphere, despite the impact of the state of emergency on the projects that were underway last March, we have been able to successfully conclude the implementation of the Cybersecurity Incident Response Center that allows us to respond quickly and efficiently to any possible cyber attack on the financial and payment system. contributing greatly to reducing the systemic risk of such attacks. Closing prospects for 2020 and 2021 Dear friends, as the recovery of the productive sectors is consolidated, driven by the Central Bank's easing measures and in coordination with the Government's fiscal policy, the Dominican economy is expected to continue improving steadily. De estos recursos, RD$20 mil millones ser<87>n para nuevos pr<8e>stamos y los RD$20 mil millones restantes para re<de>nanciamientos y reestructuraciones de pr<8e>stamos a tasas de inter<8e>s m<87>s bajas y plazos m<87>s favorables. Pero no es menos cierto que el trabajo coordinado, la capacidad y la determinaci<97>n con la que hemos actuado como naci<97>n, nos ha permitido resguardar la salud de las personas al tiempo de aliviar la carga de las empresas y los hogares, protegiendo a los sectores m<87>s vulnerables de la sociedad. Si bien hoy enfrentamos el gran reto de continuar con el proceso de recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica ya iniciado y retomar la senda de crecimiento en un entorno internacional todav<92>a incierto, estoy convencido de que bajo el liderazgo del excelent<92>simo se<96>or presidente de la Rep<9c>blica, Luis Abinader, y mediante las alianzas de un sector p<9c>blico comprometido con el desarrollo econ<97>mico y de un sector privado innovador, motor principal de la econom<92>a, lograremos ganar la batalla y garantizar la estabilidad macroecon<97>mica y social que caracteriza a nuestra Rep<9c>blica Dominicana. De esta manera, como dijo Kristalina Georgieva, Directora Gerente del FMI en las reuniones de oto<96>o celebradas recientemente: <d2>Podemos hacer algo mejor que reconstruir el mundo previo a la pandemia, podemos construir un mundo que sea m<87>s resiliente, sostenible e inclusivo.<d3> Concluyo haciendo un llamado al pa<92>s para que mantengamos una actitud positiva de mucha fe en el porvenir, y con los ojos puestos en nuestro creador, trillemos el camino hacia un mejor futuro. Title: Speech at Fintech Market RD 2021

text: Firefox Hec , scu so de DDi r lgobernador torVal bzu i in F , dez Ali ntech Mar 1202 ketRDD about:blank Remarks by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Hector Valdez Albizu.  Mr. Miguel Angel Adames, President of ADOFINTECH  Mrs. Virginia Velazquez, Executive Director of ADOFINTECH  Distinguished Exhibitors and Panelists  Ladies and gentlemen: It gives me great pleasure to deliver these opening remarks and to greet them cordially, on behalf of the authorities of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic and on my own behalf. In turn, I would like to thank the Dominican Association of Fintech Companies, ADOFINTECH, for the invitation they made to us to inaugurate this important event, so timely for the Dominican Republic and other countries represented in it, particularly in the current context. As everyone knows, the banking business has undergone substantial transformations in the last decade, driven by technological development and changes in the needs of financial users, which have motivated the transition of financial work from physical spaces to digital environments. At the same time, technological advancement has come hand in hand with the emergence of companies that offer fully digital and innovative financial services and products, known as FINTECHs or financial technology companies. In the case of the Dominican Republic, perhaps few have noticed the role of the Central Bank in that process. However, observing the historical development of the "Fintech" concept and studying the evolution of the last decades of the Dominican financial system, it is appropriate to highlight the important impulse given by the Central Bank to the transformation and modernization of payment systems, and thereby creating the conditions and tracing the way for banking and non-banking entities to offer financial products and services based on financial technologies. The modernization of the Payment and Securities Settlement System, with the implementation of a real-time gross settlement system (RTGS) in 2008, constitutes a before and after in the way of making transfers of funds in the country, giving way to modern and efficient services, such as Instant Payments, that allow bank customers to make immediate transfers and payments from banks' web and mobile platforms. For all this, we can conclude that the first entity that introduced a major change in the financial system driven by the advancement of technology, was the Central Bank, long before the term FINTECH was coined. The positive externalities that these advances produced, at the time, were and continue to be substantial. They have made possible the development, even, of other innovations, promoting in the Dominican Republic a nascent ecosystem that combines technology, finance and innovation. In this, the Central Bank recommended the association of financial technology companies, under a joint project and identity that would enable a greater impact on the financial work of our society, which eventually led to the creation of the Dominican Association of Fintech Companies (ADOFINTECH). The foregoing seeks to convey to you the message that, in terms of innovation in the financial system to promote economic development and inclusion, the Central Bank has been and will be a promoter and active institution in these initiatives, within a framework that seeks the security of the personal information of users of the financial system and the necessary safeguards to guarantee financial integrity and stability. As you can see, dear young entrepreneurs, we have understood perfectly for years what you do and your projects, even before the term "FINTECH" was officially coined, 16/11/2022 19:16 1 sur 3 Firefox about:blank And we are convinced of the great contribution they can make to the Dominican financial ecosystem and the world. Friends, digital transformation has accelerated exponentially. So that you can get an idea, in the case of the Dominican Republic, Internet Banking users, which in 2014 totaled 1.4 million, as of May of this year, reaches a community of 5.0 million digital users. In a similar order, by 2018 some 20 financial technology companies were verified, while by 2021, more than 40 of these entities already operate in the local market, providing services in various segments, such as digital payments, personal and business finance management, alternative financing, financial assets and capital markets. among others. All this would not have been possible without a regulation promoted by the Central Bank, which seeks a balance between promoting this innovation in the provision of financial services, including the emergence of new players in the ecosystem, and the preservation of financial stability and user protection. In that vein, we have already issued advanced regulations that include payments fintechs, while possible regulations for other types of fintech companies are being evaluated. Central banks have opened spaces and forums for collaboration and learning both within our institutions and with the entities of the system, in which guidelines and policies related to issues such as open banking, cybersecurity, the Cloud, Artificial Intelligence, and more recently, discussions on the benefits of distributed technologies are analyzed and recommended. Digital money from central banks, cryptocurrencies and many other novelties that are already part of our daily work. That is why I am pleased to announce that, as I announced a few months ago, we are already working hand in hand with the Inter-American Development Bank for the creation of the Financial Innovation Hub of the Dominican Republic, which will allow private initiatives in this area to be analyzed, tested and evaluated in a controlled environment. prior to its formal approval and commissioning process. These Innovation Hubs already exist in countries such as the United Kingdom, Israel, Chile and Mexico, to mention just a few, and have proven to be a very useful platform for the exchange of information and experiences, which serves both the regulator and the regulated to promote together innovative ventures that benefit the population, and support equitable access to financial services. In the case of our HUB, and this is a historic milestone, the four superintendencies are participating: Banks, Securities Market, Pensions and Insurance, together with the Central Bank, since many innovations need cross-regulation or have applications that go beyond the scope of action of a regulator. These five institutions, working as a team, will promote with greater force the development of new products and services that are proposed by FINTECHs and entities in each sector. We hope, before the end of 2021, to put into operation this Innovation Hub, which will surely be well used by all of you. I cannot fail to refer in this important forum to central bank-issued digital currencies (CBDCs), which are obligations of central banks, originated and transferred by digital means, and which are supported by these issuing entities. In this respect, like other central banks, we are exhausting a preliminary phase of analysis and exploring the nature, monetary impact and functionality of these schemes. I am pleased to inform you that we are making arrangements to participate in an international Sandbox, together with other central banks, which will allow us to know in practice, in simulated environments, the behavior and conditions of these currencies. In addition to the above, we have observed in practice and empirical evidence, that contrary to other paradigms that make the traditional financial system and the market of FINTECH companies compete, there are important benefits that we can obtain from the synergy between both worlds, the most relevant being financial inclusion. In this sense, the Central Bank, as part of its financial inclusion strategy, has promoted the provision of financial services in traditionally unserved areas, through the figure of banking sub-agents. This progress has been complemented by financial education strategies, which have been implemented throughout the country since 2013. 16/11/2022 19:16 2 sur 3 Firefox about:blank If the regulated financial sector and FINTECHS work together, with the support of monetary authorities, great things can be achieved in terms of inclusion. Therefore, we have evaluated the possibility of establishing, by regulation, incentives that promote a greater adoption of innovative and inclusive processes in the financial system, based on principles of collaboration and complementarity, which allow placing the financial system as a whole on the path of a deeper, transformative and beneficial innovation for the country. These issues to which I have referred: the regulation that promotes innovation, the Financial Innovation Hub, central bank digital money, instant payments, banking subagents and others that I have not dealt with, but no less important such as cybersecurity and cross-border payment systems, contribute to directing the Dominican financial system towards digitalization. Of course, other components are required such as a national digital identity system, rules to facilitate interoperability between mobile applications and a greater use of digital certificates in commercial procedures, which are being contemplated in the draft of the Digital Agenda of the Presidency of the Republic. Finally, in the face of the challenge caused by the pandemic, we have seen that our financial and payment system has demonstrated the capacity for reinvention and innovation, with the help of companies like you. From the Central Bank we wish to reiterate once again our commitment to this progress and modernization, with that impulse towards a financial and payment system as digital as possible, and with the financial inclusion of the sectors traditionally not served. But always, in a framework of economic and financial stability for all, to contribute to achieving "a fairer, more sustainable and inclusive economy, which leaves no one behind." Thanks a lot. 16/11/2022 19:16 3 of 3

Title: Speech on the Seventy-fourth Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: DDirde rr t Hec , scu so lgobe nado en e , or Valdez Albizu The seventy-fourth anniversary of the Central Zone of the Dominican Republic On the occasion of the 74 years of life of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, an organization created in 1947 as the only issuing institution in the country and the main depository of its monetary and financial sovereignty, as is customary on each anniversary of our institution, I appear before you, Bancentraliana family, with feelings of deep emotion and pride, to present the recent evolution of the Dominican economy and its prospects, highlighting the achievements made in the struggle to overcome the economic and health effects caused by the pandemic. It is a great honor and source of infinite gratitude for me to lead a central bank recognized, locally and internationally, as an institution of high credibility, committed to the stability and development of the country. For the fulfillment of its mission, the central bank has an exceptional human capital that, supported by a cutting-edge technological infrastructure, performs day by day a tenacious work with high quality standards and attached to non-negotiable ethical principles. Allow me to take this opportunity to reiterate my deepest gratitude to His Excellency the President of the Republic, Luis Abinader, who honored me with his confidence to continue leading the conduct of the country's monetary, exchange and financial policies in one of the most difficult moments in the entire Dominican economic history. I greatly appreciate the President's unconditional support for our central bank at this time of great challenges. Similarly, in this arduous task of facing the impact of the coronavirus on our economy, the support of the honorable members of the Monetary Board has been essential, as well as all the officials and employees of the central bank who, as I said earlier, demonstrate responsibility and excellence in the performance of their duties. I want at this moment, in a very special way, to express that the years of intense work at the head of this institution have been possible thanks to the solidarity and love received from my family. I thank God for giving me a companion like my beloved wife Fior, who has always been present without regard to the precious time that my labors take away from family dynamics, helping me to maintain an unshakable faith in the Almighty even in the most difficult circumstances. I also thank my dear children Hector Manuel and Begona, my beloved mother and my siblings, who have always given me their understanding and support in the most pressing situations of my personal and work life. Friends, I would like to begin my words with some reflections on the international environment, explaining the great challenge that the spread of COVID-19 has meant for central banks and governments of countries. INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENT After eighteen months of joint efforts between the public and private sectors, the world economy has entered a phase of frank recovery, especially in those countries where vaccination plans have allowed the reopening of the main economic activities. In its most recent Global Economic Prospects (WEO) report, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects year-on-year growth of the world economy of 5.9% for 2021, a remarkable recovery after having contracted 3.1% in 2020. A large part of this growth is explained by the performance of industrialized economies. In that vein, the United States of America, our main trading partner, would grow 6.0% in 2021, as a result of an efficient vaccination program and the application of extensive monetary and fiscal stimuli. Meanwhile, euro zone countries have restored growth as they have eased containment policies. According to the IMF, this bloc of countries would reach a growth of 5.0% in 2021, recovering a large part of last year's -6.3%. 16/11/2022 19:16 The most dynamic emerging economies have also been in the process of recovery. Along these lines, the IMF projects growth of 6.3% for Latin America, supported by the reactivation of private consumption and better terms of trade for the largest economies in the region. A point to note in the IMF report is that the Dominican Republic would be, once again, among the fastest growing economies forecasting a real GDP expansion of 9.5% during 2021. Despite this dynamism, significant risks remain in the global environment associated with the spread of new variants of the virus, higher commodity prices and barriers in global trade supply chains. These elements have slightly moderated growth forecasts, while inflation has increased, in both developed and emerging economies. Good news is that experts from international organizations agree that the increase in inflation caused by distortions in global supply is transitory and will moderate as productive activity is freed from the "bottlenecks" generated by the coronavirus crisis. Personally, I can tell you that last week I participated in several virtual meetings with central bank governors, organized by the IMF and the Center for Monetary Studies of Latin America (CEMLA), and I was able to see first-hand that there is a consensus among central bankers on the temporary nature of inflationary pressures coming from the global environment. MONETARY AND FINANCIAL POLICY At the national level, the economic recovery has been faster than expected, largely due to the monetary stimulus plan launched by the central bank since the beginning of the pandemic. That plan cut the policy rate by 150 basis points to a record low of 3.0 percent a year, while tightening the rate corridor, reducing the overnight to 2.5 percent. Likewise, liquidity facilities were granted to financial institutions for RD 215 billion (5.0% of GDP), who in turn placed some 92,000 loans to companies and households at low rates, in most cases around 8.0%. Las actividades econ<97>micas que lideraron el desempe<96>o en t<8e>rminos de valor agregado en el periodo enero-septiembre fueron: Hoteles, bares y restaurantes (31.8 %); construcci<97>n (30.0 %); manufactura de zonas francas (24.2 %); transporte y almacenamiento (13.7 %); manufactura local (11.5 %); comercio (11.1 %); y explotaci<97>n de minas y canteras (6.9 %). Como ha venido ocurriendo en meses anteriores, la construcci<97>n volvi<97> a ser la actividad de mayor incidencia en el crecimiento, representando casi un 80% de la formaci<97>n bruta de capital <de>jo. En otro orden, la manufactura local ha sido determinante en la trayectoria de recuperaci<97>n, tanto por su 16/11/2022 19:16 importante participaci<97>n en el PIB como por ser uno de los principales generadores de empleos formales en el pa<92>s. En cuanto a la manufactura de zonas francas, la actividad recuper<97> el 100% de los empleos suspendidos a ra<92>z del con<de>namiento, creciendo 24.2% interanual en enero-septiembre 2021. El sector comercio tambi<8e>n se bene<de>ci<97> de un incremento en la demanda, como resultado de la <df>exibilizaci<97>n del con<de>namiento orientado a mitigar la propagaci<97>n del coronavirus. Asimismo, las facilidades crediticias del banco central a trav<8e>s de los intermediarios <de>nancieros impulsaron la producci<97>n y distribuci<97>n de bienes agropecuarios y manufacturados, contribuyendo al crecimiento del comercio. Un resultado sorprendente es que el turismo se ha recuperado m<87>s r<87>pido de lo previsto, recibiendo m<87>s de 3.3 millones de visitantes no residentes en enero-septiembre. Solo en septiembre, los pasajeros no residentes que ingresaron al pa<92>s se incrementaron en 12.9% con respecto a los visitantes recibidos en igual mes de 2019. MERCADO LABORAL Ahora me referir<8e> a la evoluci<97>n reciente del mercado laboral dominicano, bas<87>ndome en los resultados preliminares de la Encuesta Nacional Continua de Fuerza de Trabajo (ENCFT). Este instrumento estad<92>stico es reconocido internacionalmente como el m<87>s efectivo para dar seguimiento al mercado laboral, ya que los indicadores relevantes se obtienen de las directrices de la Organizaci<97>n Internacional del Trabajo (OIT) e incluyen tanto empleos formales p<9c>blicos y privados, como empleos informales. De acuerdo a esta encuesta, la ocupaci<97>n total alcanz<97> 4,598,409 en julio-septiembre 2021, lo cual implica que en t<8e>rminos netos represent<97> un 97.5 % de la ocupaci<97>n total de octubre-diciembre 2019, es decir, de la pre-pandemia. En t<8e>rminos interanuales, la ocupaci<97>n total aument<97> en 302,958 para un crecimiento de 7.05 % con respecto a julio-septiembre de 2020. La tendencia hacia la regularizaci<97>n del mercado laboral tambi<8e>n se observa en los registros administrativos de la Tesorer<92>a de la Seguridad Social (TSS). Dichos registros muestran que, en el caso de los asalariados formales del sector privado, la ocupaci<97>n se ha recuperado pr<87>cticamente en su totalidad con respecto a febrero de 2020. Resulta oportuno puntualizar que la cantidad de ocupados de la TSS siempre ser<87> menor a la ocupaci<97>n total que arroje la Encuesta Nacional Continua de Fuerza de Trabajo, ya que esta <9c>ltima incluye el empleo informal, adem<87>s de los asalariados formales inscritos en la TSS.
