text: BCRD offers entertainment to the secretaries of the institution The return of this social meeting after the covid-19 pandemic was a source of joy for all participants, who enjoyed a lunch organized at the BCRD Employees Club Santo Domingo. Title: BCRD puts four new works into circulation within the framework of the 24th Santo Domingo International Book Fair
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: BCRD puts into circulation four new works within the framework of the 24th International Book Fair of Santo Domingo Valdez Albizu described the book as a prudent advisor to men and women of power, and a kind voice for those dominated by oppressors Santo Domingo. Dominican Republic. - The Central Bank of the Dominican Republic (BCRD), through its Cultural Department, put into circulation four new works from its institutional collection for a total of 234 published titles, within the framework of the twenty-fourth Santo Domingo International Book Fair 2022. Governor Hector Valdez Albizu said at the presentation ceremony that "the book has been, for centuries and in the most diverse forms, a companion of inestimable value, both personal and collective." Valdez Albizu also pointed to the book as "a prudent advisor to men and women of power, as well as a kind voice for those who suffer under the domination of their oppressors." He also called the book an ingenious teacher for creators in the sciences and arts, being a source of wisdom for all eternity. The four new works are as follows:  Culture at the Central Bank 2020-2022, by Hector Valdez Albizu, which collects the speeches given by him at the cultural activities held at the institution during the pandemic period, with the opening of numismatic and philatelic exhibitions, the release of new books and compact discs, and awards in the economics and art and literature competitions.  Temporary exhibitions at the Numismatic and Philatelic Museum 2021-2022, a volume that brings together the material from the last three exhibitions held at the BCRD museum, with banknotes and coins commemorative events on the exploitation of the Pueblo Viejo Gold Mine, inaugurated in 1975; sports in Dominican numismatics, which served to once again exalt the passion of Dominicans for all kinds of sports and their outstanding performance on any stage, inside and outside the country; and the coins, banknotes and commemorative stamps of the religious culture of the Dominican Republic, on the occasion of commemorating this year the centenary of the canonical coronation of the Virgin of Altagracia.  Se cortan chazo, a book of short stories by the Dominican writer of Cuban origin Jose M. Fernandez Pequeno, literary critic and essayist, who comes to nourish the list of writers in the catalog of the collection, author of twenty works, twice winner of the Ibero-American Contest of Stories of Casa de Teatro, and twice winner of the Annual Literature Awards in the Dominican Republic.  Laurels and Birds, by the Puerto Plata architect, painter, poet and narrator Aida Yolanda Diaz Fernandez, founding member of the group Encuentro con la Poesia de Santiago de los Caballeros, who brings in this book a set of varied stories and texts whose main characteristic is the novelty and freshness of themes rooted in personal experiences of her region and a literary treatment that, According to experts in this field, it constitutes a new look at local narrative. Valdez Albizu congratulated the authors Aida Yolanda Diaz Fernandez and Jose M. Fernandez Pequeno, and thanked the team of the Cultural Department of the BCRD for keeping the institutional editorial program active. During the event, the deputy manager/director of the Cultural Department of the BCRD, the writer Jose Alcantara Almanzar, to present the works put into circulation, while Aida Yolanda Diaz Fernandez expressed gratitude on behalf of the authors. Present at the activity, accompanying Governor Valdez Albizu, were Clarissa de la Rocha de Torres, deputy governor; Ervin Novas Bello, manager; the member of the honorable Monetary Board, Jose Manuel Mallen; the comptroller, Jose Manuel Taveras Lay; and the assistant managers Joel Tejeda Compres, Roberto Pelliccione, Fabiola Herrera and Ramon Rosario. Participation in the International Book Fair Also as part of its active cultural work, the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic participates this year with a stand at the XXIV Santo Domingo International Book Fair 2022, which takes place in the colonial city. At this stand, located in the Ozama Fortress, visitors will be able to purchase many of the 234 works published by the BCRD on art, literature, economics and social sciences. Those interested can consult the titles of the collection on the CRD website April 28, 2022

Tambin calific al libro de ingenioso maestro para los creadores en ciencias y artes, siendo una fuente de sabidura para toda la eternidad. Las cuatro nuevas obras son las siguientes:  La cultura en el Banco Central 2020-2022, obra de Hctor Valdez Albizu, que recoge los discursos pronunciados por l en las actividades culturales celebradas en la institucin durante el perodo de la pandemia, con la apertura de exposiciones numismticas y filatlicas, la salida de nuevos libros y discos compactos, y las premiaciones en los concursos de economa y de arte y literatura.  Exposiciones temporales en el Museo Numismtico y Filatlico 2021-2022, volumen que rene el material de las ltimas tres exposiciones realizadas en el museo del BCRD, con los billetes y monedas conmemorativos sobre la explotacin de la Mina de Oro de Pueblo Viejo, inaugurada en 1975; los deportes en la numismtica dominicana, que sirvi para exaltar nuevamente la pasin de los dominicanos por todo tipo de deportes y su actuacin sobresaliente en cualquier escenario, dentro y fuera del pas; y las monedas, billetes y sellos conmemorativos de la cultura religiosa de la Repblica Dominicana, con motivo de conmemorarse este ao el centenario de la coronacin cannica de la Virgen de la Altagracia.  Se cortan chazo, un libro de cuentos del escritor dominicano de origen cubano Jos M. Fernndez Pequeo, crtico literario y ensayista, quien viene a nutrir la lista de escritores del catlogo de la coleccin, autor de una veintena de obras, dos veces ganador del Concurso Iberoamericano de Cuentos de Casa de Teatro, y dos veces ganador de los Premios Anuales de Literatura en Repblica Dominicana.  Laureles y pjaros, de la arquitecta, pintora, poeta y narradora puertoplatea Ada Yolanda Daz Fernndez, miembro fundadora del grupo Encuentro con la Poesa de Santiago de los Caballeros, quien trae en este libro un conjunto de relatos y textos variados cuya principal caracterstica es la novedad y la frescura de unos temas enraizados en vivencias personales de su regin y un tratamiento literario que, segn los entendidos en esta materia, constituye una nueva mirada en la narrativa local. Valdez Albizu felicit a los autores Ada Yolanda Daz Fernndez y Jos M. Fernndez Pequeo, y agradeci al equipo del departamento Cultural del BCRD por mantener activo el programa editorial institucional. Durante el acto, el subgerente/director del departamento Cultural del BCRD, el escritor Jos Alcntara Almnzar, para presentar las obras puestas en circulacin, en tanto que Ada Yolanda Daz Fernndez expres el agradecimiento en nombre de los autores. En la actividad estuvieron presentes, acompaando al gobernador Valdez Albizu, Clarissa de la Rocha de Torres, vicegobernadora; Ervin Novas Bello, gerente; el miembro de la honorable Junta Monetaria, Jos Manuel Malln; el contralor, Jos Manuel Taveras Lay; y los subgerentes Joel Tejeda Comprs, Roberto Pelliccione, Fabiola Herrera y Ramn Rosario. Participacin en la Feria Internacional del Libro Tambin como parte de su activa labor cultural, el Banco Central de la Repblica Dominicana participa este ao con un estand en la XXIV Feria Internacional del Libro Santo Domingo 2022, que se lleva a cabo en la ciudad colonial. En dicho estand, ubicado en la Fortaleza Ozama, los visitantes podrn adquirir muchas de las 234 obras editadas por el BCRD sobre arte, literatura, economa y ciencias sociales. Title: Speech by Governor Hctor Valdez Albizu on the seventy-fifth (LXXV) anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Speech by the governor, Hector Valdez Albizu, on the seventy-fifth (LXXV) anniversary of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic On this memorable date we celebrate the 75th anniversary of the creation of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic as the issuing entity of the national currency and responsible for price stability and the regulation of the financial system, as well as executor of the monetary, exchange and financial policies of the nation, complying with the mandate of the Constitution of the Republic. A very special occasion that fills us with great satisfaction as we are participants in its extraordinary career, which has made this institution worthy of national and international recognition for its high quality standards in the performance of its functions. As we commemorate the seventy-fifth anniversary of the Central Bank, it is also an opportunity to thank Almighty and Merciful God for the forgers of this institution who are no longer with us today, as well as for the lives of those present here and the blessings with which he has filled us. Likewise, our thanks to His Excellency the President of the Republic, Luis Abinader, who for the second time has placed his trust in our work, by ratifying the person who speaks to you as governor in one of the most difficult moments for the Dominican and world economy, respecting the autonomy of the Central Bank and its total independence for the design of monetary policies. exchange and financial institutions. I am honored to be holding this position for 24 years, that is, practically a third of the institutional life of the Central Bank. Our most sincere thanks also go to the honorable members of the Monetary Board, who have played a crucial role in the strengthening and continuous improvement of the policies that frame the actions of the Central Bank. In particular, I would like to highlight the support provided for the measures adopted in the management of the crises we have faced over the past two years. Friends, we certainly have many reasons to be proud of the successes we have achieved and for which we have been the object of recent recognitions, highlighting the one granted by the Senate of the Republic to me for the great contributions in favor of the economic development of the nation and the investiture as Doctor Honoris Causa in Economic and Business Sciences by the APEC University. which constitutes the highest distinction in the academic field that an economics professional can obtain to exalt life achievements and contributions to the well-being of society, distinctions that I have received with joy and of course with the greatest humility. I speak to you in the plural, because the successes and achievements achieved would not have been possible without the dedication to work and the highest adherence to the standards of excellence and other institutional values of the staff of this Central Bank, both of the officials who accompany me on a daily basis, and of all the technical and administrative staff. including the simplest collaborator, whose work is essential for the efficient performance of the institution. Allow me now, my friends, in compliance with the Central Bank's commitment to communication, transparency and accountability, to share with you some reflections on the conduct of monetary policy, as well as the scoops on the behavior of the economy in the January-September 2022 period and the outlook for the end of the year. As you all know, the international environment has been impacted since 2020 by significant successive shocks, such as the COVID-19 pandemic and its aftermath; namely, disruptions in supply chains, increased external prices of raw materials (commodities), including oil, and increased container transportation costs. And more recently, aggravated by the uncertainty associated with the Russia-Ukraine war conflict. These two phenomena have constituted a kind of perfect storm, as I have figuratively expressed on more than one occasion. Monetary policy, growth and inflation Initially, the policies implemented to face the pandemic and its aftermath prevented a collapse of the economy that would have been much greater than the -6.7% drop in real gross domestic product (GDP) in 2020. As you may recall, in this scenario, the Central Bank acted proactively with the support of the Monetary Board, reducing the monetary policy rate (MPR) to its historic low of 3.00%, channeling to companies and households, through financial intermediation entities, resources amounting to more than RD215,000 million (around 5.0% of GDP) for new loans and refinancing that were granted for an average term of three years and at an interest rate of no more than 8.0% per annum. At the same time, the Government provided direct support to both formal and informal workers and households through the various social programmes that were put in place. As a result of the right mix of monetary and fiscal policies, the economy was able to recover faster than expected, demonstrating its resilience and the momentum of the private sector, whose average contribution accounts for approximately 85 percent of the economy's growth. In this regard, at the end of 2021, a year-on-year expansion of real GDP of 12.3% was reached according to the behavior of the value added of the different economic activities that make up this indicator. Likewise, if the production volume index of 2021 is compared with that of 2019, it shows a real growth of 4.7%, all of which we explain in detail to the country with a great sense of responsibility. Once this remarkable performance of the Dominican economy was achieved, which turned out to be better than that of most countries in the region, and in the face of the rise in global inflationary pressures of magnitudes not observed in some advanced economies in the last 40 years, the Central Bank began a gradual process of monetary tightening at the end of 2021. with the purpose of avoiding an overheating of the economy and a potential outflow of capital, anticipating the increases in interest rates that would begin to be verified later in 2022 in the largest economies. In this sense, the Central Bank's monetary policy rate has been increased by 525 basis points, from 3.0% in November 2021 to 8.25% currently. In addition, the surplus liquidity of the financial system has been reduced through open market operations and the gradual return of the resources that had been granted during the pandemic. These restrictive measures to moderate inflation could deserve criticism from some. However, it is worth noting the prominent economist Ben Bernanke, former chairman of the Federal Reserve and one of the recent laureates of the 2022 Nobel Prize in Economics, in his book 'The Courage to Act', I quote: 'Making politically unpopular decisions for the long-term benefit of the country is the reason why the Federal Reserve exists as a politically independent central bank. It was created precisely for this purpose: to do what must be done, what others cannot or do not want to do'. Currently, we can say that the expansionary stance of monetary policy has been reversed. In fact, the increases made in the MPR, together with the reduction in inflation expectations, have caused the real interbank interest rate to be approximately one percentage point above its estimated neutral level. Similarly, market interest rates have increased while a slowdown in the pace of expansion of monetary aggregates has been observed, which has contributed to a soft landing in the performance of the Dominican economy. Indeed, the circulating medium (MI) has moderated its year-on-year growth from a maximum of 33% in 2021 to expand by around 10% at the end of September 2022. However, credit to the private sector in national currency continues to grow above 14% year-on-year in September, reflecting the boost in domestic demand and the healthy dynamism of the productive sectors. It should be noted that the fight of monetary policy against inflation has materialized in coordination with the fiscal policy of the Government of President Luis Abinader, mainly with the implementation of fuel subsidies and electricity rates, as well as initiatives to lower production costs in agriculture. The effectiveness of these measures has been reflected in the downward trajectory recorded by year-on-year inflation in recent months, standing at 8.63% in September for a reduction of 100 basis points compared to the maximum of 9.64% reached in April of this year. This recent behavior is a sign that inflation is on the path to converging to the target range of 4% 1% during the first half of 2023. Indeed, inflation registered 0.29% in September 2022, after 0.21% in August, variations that reflect a significant moderation compared to the previous 26 months in which monthly inflation averaged 0.78%. I would also like to highlight that, when analyzing the data of 18 Latin American economies, it is evident that the year-on-year inflation rate of the Dominican Republic is lower than that of eleven countries in the region. This means that only six countries report year-on-year inflation below that of the Dominican Republic, of which three are from dollarized economies (Panama, Ecuador and El Salvador). I have no doubt that the economic policy decisions taken in the Dominican Republic, both monetary and fiscal, have been timely and prudent in the context of the events and circumstances described above. In fact, the prominent economist and professor at Columbia University, Xavier Sala-i-Martin, recently described in an appearance in the country that the measures adopted by the Central Bank were correct and timely, in the context of the fight against inflation. Preliminary results of the economy January-September 2022 Regarding the preliminary results of the economy corresponding to the end of September 2022, I am pleased to share with you the scoop that the monthly indicator of economic activity (IMAE) registered a year-on-year variation of 4.8% in the month of September, for a cumulative growth of the real Gross Domestic Product of 5.4% in January-September 2022 compared to the same period of the previous year. When analyzing in detail the sectoral behavior of GDP in January-September 2022, the notable incidence of services as a whole stands out, which constitute approximately 60.0% of the total economy and present a cumulative year-on-year variation of 7.2%. Among the activities that make it up, it is worth highlighting hotels, bars and restaurants (28.9%), health (11.7%), other service activities (9.1%), public administration (7.8%), transport and storage (7.0%), commerce (6.6%) and financial services (5.7%). Regarding industries, free zone activity grew 6.6%, local manufacturing 4.3% and construction 2.2%; while agriculture grew 3.8% in January-September 2022. The activity of hotels, bars and restaurants has been the one with the greatest impact on GDP performance in the first nine months of 2022, explaining approximately a third of its total expansion in the aforementioned period, exhibiting a relative variation of 28.9% in terms of real value added. This year has been extraordinary for the tourism sector in the Dominican Republic, exceeding expectations of recovery after the challenge posed by the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war for international tourism. Indeed, there have been unprecedented flows in the arrival of non-resident passengers, accumulating 5.3 million visitors in nine months, according to data announced by the Minister of Tourism, David Collado, that is, 6.5% and 6.9% more non-resident visitors than in 2018 and 2019, respectively. This reveals that, despite the adversities that the tourism industry has faced worldwide in the face of the current international situation, the Dominican Republic remains the leading destination in terms of tourist arrivals in the insular Caribbean region and Central America. These are, without a doubt, achievements worthy of highlighting given the boost that tourism represents for national productive activity and the generation of foreign exchange. On the other hand, the increase in the volumes of local production of goods and tradable imports continue to have a positive impact on the performance of trade and transport activities, which exhibit year-on-year rates of 6.6% and 7.0%, respectively in January-September 2022. The result of these sectors is in turn associated with the verified increase in storage and distribution logistics support services. In addition, the manufacture of free zones has been a key activity for economic recovery, boosting the national production chain and the expansion of exports. Particularly in terms of real value added, it registered a year-on-year growth of 6.6% this year, in line with the 11.7% increase in exports from this sector. With regard to local manufacturing, there is a cumulative variation of 4.3%, mainly explained by the increase in production volumes in the industries of manufacture of base metals, non-metallic mineral products, manufacture of alcoholic beverages, non-alcoholic beverages and tobacco derivatives, other food products and chemical substances and products. As for agriculture, this economic activity accumulated a year-on-year increase of 3.8% at the end of the first nine months of 2022. It has been impacted by the high costs of imported raw materials, so the measures implemented by the Government such as the temporary subsidy for the import at zero rate of some inputs required in the production process, as well as the credit facilities for small and medium-sized agricultural producers, have contributed to its positive performance. With regard to the labor market, the main indicators continue to show a recovery trajectory. In this sense, according to the results of the Continuous National Labor Force Survey (ENCFT) corresponding to the third quarter of 2022, the open unemployment rate, which includes unemployed people who are actively looking for work, has experienced a reduction of 3.2 percentage points, from 8.0% registered in January-March 2021 to 4.8% in July-September 2022. With regard to fiscal policy, the higher collections in relation to what was initially estimated by the General Directorate of Internal Taxes and the General Directorate of Customs, which have been doing an excellent job, stand out. This improvement in tax revenues has provided the necessary space to apply subsidies aimed at mitigating the impact of higher commodity prices on national production and households; as well as for assistance to the provinces affected by the recent passage of Hurricane Fiona, which has been estimated by the Government to require an investment in repairs of more than RD20,000 million. On the other hand, the indicators of the external sector maintained a favorable evolution during the January-September 2022 period. According to preliminary figures, during the first nine months of this year, total exports amounted to US10,543.3 million, growing by 14.2% year-on-year. Within exports, those corresponding to the free zone sector continue to show record figures so far this year, approaching about US6,000 million, for an increase of 11.7% compared to 2021. The potential for expansion of free zones is evident in the high demand for new companies to settle in the country, which supports the continuous flow of investments into this sector. It is also important to highlight the positive development of other foreign exchange-generating activities, such as tourism, a sector that has recovered faster than expected with an arrival of 5.3 million non-resident visitors, registering revenues of US6,341.9 million in January-September, and exhibiting an increase of 65.7% compared to the same period in 2021. Similarly, remittances reached US7,309.4 million in the first nine months of 2022, reflecting the solidarity of the Dominican diaspora. Likewise, in this period, flows of around US2,870.4 million were received for foreign direct investment, increasing by 19.1% compared to the same period in 2021, which reiterates the confidence of international investors in the stability of the Dominican economy with clear and transparent rules, a climate of social peace, in addition to the commendable work that the country's Investment Promotion Cabinet has been doing. These higher foreign exchange earnings have favored the relative stability of the exchange rate, reflected in a cumulative appreciation of the local currency of 7% at the end of September, being the second largest after Uruguay, which has registered 7.1%. In addition, they have contributed to the strengthening of international reserves to close to US14,000 million, equivalent to 12.3% of GDP and 5.7 months of imports, exceeding the metrics recommended by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Regarding the performance of the consolidated financial system, at the end of September 2022, the indicators demonstrate its equity strength, supported by adequate levels of solvency, profitability and low levels of non-performing loans. In that order, the solvency position reached 16.0% as of July 2022, according to the most recent information published by the Superintendency of Banks, which shows compliance with the minimum requirement of 10%, required by current legal provisions. As for the return on equity (ROE) indicator, this was 22.7% and on average assets (ROA) of 2.6%. It should be noted that the NPL ratio stood at just 1.0%. In the case of multiple banks, which represent 88.4% of the national financial system by asset levels, it presented a solvency of 14.6%, return on equity of 25.3%, on assets 2.6% and a delinquency ratio of 0.9%. Institutional achievements In the institutional sphere, I am very pleased to emphasize that this institution in the course of its 75 years of existence has always remained at the forefront of the latest technological advances. In this regard, I would like to briefly share with you three initiatives of significant value to the Central Bank. The first is our cybersecurity center, which in its second year of operations continues to contribute to supporting the mitigation of the effects and propagation of possible cybersecurity events in the financial and payment system, which in turn could become a systemic or reputational risk. This center is a great achievement for which we have received local and international recognition. In the same vein, as you well know, last June we published the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion, incorporating technology to build a payment ecosystem that all citizens can access, supported by an intensive use of digital media complemented by personalized financial education. Finally, this year we inaugurated the Financial Innovation Hub, with the support of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) and with the assistance of the Superintendencies of Banks, the Stock Market, Insurance and Pensions. This Hub will allow private initiatives in this area to be promoted, promoting their feasibility and sustainability. Friends present, my words would be incomplete if I did not mention the contributions of our institution to art and culture in its different manifestations. In this sense, we have one of the best equipped specialized libraries in the country and spaces aimed at promoting cultural and academic activities. Also noteworthy is the collection of publications published by the Central Bank, which has contributed to society more than 250 works in its different series: art and literature; social and economic sciences; numismatics and philatelics; music by Dominican composers; and various award-winning works. In addition, in the social field, we have a volunteer staff made up of our own staff dedicated to contributing to solutions to problems that affect the most vulnerable sectors of the population. Perspectives and final thoughts Dear friends, taking into consideration the momentum that economic activity has maintained during the first nine months of the year, the Central Bank's forecasting system indicates that real GDP growth would be in the range of 5.0%-5.5% for the year 2022, that is, around the potential pace of the economy. Likewise, international organizations such as the IMF and the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) maintain a positive outlook for the Dominican economy, projecting an expansion of more than 5.0% for the country in 2022. With respect to nominal GDP, it is expected to reach about US112,000 million by the end of 2022, which, together with the prudent management of public finances by the Ministry of Finance and the exchange rate stability observed during this year, have been determining elements for the consolidated public sector debt as a proportion of GDP to be below 60% at the end of the year. reducing with respect to the levels recorded in recent years. It should also be noted that the efficient management of liabilities by the Ministry has contributed to reducing debt service and improving its sustainability over time. Regarding the evolution of domestic prices, in line with liquidity conditions in an active monetary policy scenario and the maintenance of fuel and electricity subsidies for the remainder of the year, inflation is expected to end 2022 at around 7.0% and it would continue to fall in year-on-year terms in the following months to converge to the target range of 4.0% 1.0% in the first half of 2023. As I stated during my participation in the recently concluded 2022 Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank in Washington, DC, central banks must remain focused on controlling inflation, since, without price stability, the benefits of growth are at risk of being eliminated, generating a negative social impact, especially for the most vulnerable population. Likewise, forecasts for the external sector suggest that foreign direct investment flows would reach US3,800 million by the end of 2022. Similarly, it is forecast that this year would close with total exports of more than US14,000 million, an all-time high; remittances close to US10,000 million and tourism revenues above US8,500 million. All this, added to the income from other services, estimated at about US3,000, would lead to ending the year with foreign exchange revenues of more than US39,300 million, a record figure. A relevant aspect to highlight is that the country's strong macroeconomic fundamentals are highlighted by economists, investors, and financial analysts when making their forecasts for next year's 2023 performance. As an example, the Bank of America, within the framework of the aforementioned annual meetings of the IMF and the World Bank in Washington, reiterated in its report 'Outlook for emerging economies' that the Dominican Republic will be one of the fastest growing economies in the region for 2023, in the face of the challenging international situation. Similarly, Moises Naim, former executive director of the World Bank, recently indicated in our country that the 'Dominican Republic is among the countries that will not have a recession' and that it is in 'good conditions to come out successfully' in the adverse scenario that is projected for next year. Finally, dear Bancentralian family, these last few years have been among the most difficult for humanity, but they have undoubtedly served to accumulate invaluable experience in terms of coordinated crisis management and that can be a very valuable input for the future to work with the same zeal and comprehensively face the challenges that lie ahead as a nation. Supported by the resilience that the Dominican economy has shown in challenging times, as a faithful standard-bearer of optimism, I feel confident that through a joint effort between the public and private sectors, where the former has shown the application of timely measures to solve the moments of greatest calamity in the economic sectors and the most vulnerable population, and the second has been able to adapt to the reality of the times, keeping the machinery of production and job creation on, we will continue on the path of stability and economic growth. For our part, rest assured that the Central Bank will continue to carry out its work as an issuing entity, to ensure price stability and guarantee the regulation of the financial and payment system to fully comply with our anniversary motto of working for "a stability that is felt". May God bless you all, today, tomorrow, and forever! Thanks a lot. Friday, October 21, 2022
text_original: Discurso del gobernador, Hctor Valdez Albizu, en el septuagsimo quinto (LXXV) aniversario del Banco Central de la Repblica Dominicana En esta memorable fecha celebramos los 75 aos de la creacin del Banco Central de la Repblica Dominicana como el ente emisor de la moneda nacional y responsable de la estabilidad de precios y la regulacin del sistema financiero, as como ejecutor de las polticas monetaria, cambiara y financiera de la nacin, cumpliendo con el mandato de la Constitucin de la Repblica. Ocasin muy especial que nos llena de una gran satisfaccin al ser partcipes de su extraordinaria trayectoria, que ha hecho a esta institucin merecedora del reconocimiento nacional e internacional por sus altos estndares de calidad en el desempeo de sus funciones. Al tiempo que conmemoramos el septuagsimo quinto aniversario del Banco Central, tambin se hace propicia la oportunidad para dar gracias a Dios todopoderoso y misericordioso por los forjadores de esta institucin que hoy ya no estn con nosotros, as como por la vida de los aqu presentes y las bendiciones con las que nos ha colmado. Igualmente, nuestro agradecimiento al excelentsimo seor presidente de la Repblica, Luis Abinader, quien por segunda ocasin ha depositado su confianza en nuestro trabajo, al ratificar a quien les habla como gobernador en uno de los momentos ms difciles para la economa dominicana y mundial, respetando la autonoma del Banco Central y su total independencia para el diseo de polticas monetarias, cambiaras y financieras. Me honra estar desempeando este cargo por 24 aos, es decir, prcticamente una tercera parte de la vida institucional del Banco Central. Nuestro ms sincero agradecimiento tambin a los honorables miembros de la Junta Monetaria, quienes han jugado un rol crucial en el fortalecimiento y mejora continua de las polticas que enmarcan el accionar del Banco Central. Especialmente, quiero destacar el apoyo brindado ante las medidas adoptadas durante el manejo de las crisis que hemos enfrentado en el periodo de los ltimos dos aos. Amigos y amigas, ciertamente tenemos muchas razones para sentirnos orgullosos de los xitos alcanzados y por los cuales hemos sido objeto de reconocimientos recientes, destacndose el otorgado por el Senado de la Repblica a mi persona por los grandes aportes a favor del desarrollo econmico de la nacin y la investidura como Doctor Honoris Causa en Ciencias Econmicas y Empresariales por la Universidad APEC, la cual constituye la ms alta distincin en el mbito acadmico que un profesional de la economa puede obtener para exaltar los logros de vida y contribuciones al bienestar de la sociedad, distinciones que he recibido con regocijo y por supuesto con la mayor humildad. Les hablo en plural, porque los xitos y logros alcanzados no hubiesen sido posibles sin la entrega al trabajo y el ms alto apego a los estndares de excelencia y dems valores institucionales del personal de este Banco Central, tanto de los funcionarios que me acompaan en el da a da, como de todo el personal tcnico y administrativo, incluyendo al ms sencillo colaborador, cuyas labores resultan esenciales para el eficiente desempeo de la institucin. Permtanme ahora, mis amigos, en cumplimiento con el compromiso de comunicacin, transparencia y rendicin de cuentas del Banco Central, compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones sobre la conduccin de la poltica monetaria, as como las primicias sobre el comportamiento de la economa en el perodo enero-septiembre 2022 y las perspectivas para el cierre de ao. Como es del conocimiento de todos ustedes, el entorno internacional ha estado impactado desde el 2020 por significativos choques sucesivos, como la pandemia del COVID-19 y sus secuelas; a saber, disrupciones en las cadenas de suministros, aumento de los precios externos de las materias primas (commodities), incluyendo el petrleo y el incremento en los costos de transporte de los contenedores. Y ms recientemente, agravado por la incertidumbre asociada al conflicto blico Rusia- Ucrania. Estos dos fenmenos se han constituido en una especie de tormenta perfecta, como figurativamente he expresado en ms de una ocasin. Poltica monetaria, crecimiento e inflacin Inicialmente, las polticas implementadas para enfrentar la pandemia y sus secuelas evitaron un colapso de la economa que hubiese sido mucho mayor a la cada de -6.7 % del producto interno bruto (PIB) real en 2020. Como recordarn, ante este escenario, el Banco Central actu de forma proactiva con el apoyo de la Junta Monetaria, reduciendo la tasa de poltica monetaria (TPM) a su mnimo histrico de 3.00 %, canalizando a las empresas y los hogares, a travs de las entidades de intermediacin financiera, recursos ascendentes a ms de RD$215,000 millones (en torno a 5.0 % del PIB) para nuevos prstamos y refinanciamientos que fueron otorgados a un plazo promedio de tres aos y a una tasa de inters no mayor al 8.0 % anual. De manera simultnea, el Gobierno brind apoyo directo a los trabajadores tanto formales como informales y a los hogares mediante los diferentes programas sociales que se pusieron en marcha. Como resultado de la acertada combinacin de polticas monetaria y fiscal, la economa pudo recuperarse ms rpido de lo previsto demostrando su capacidad de resiliencia y el impulso que representa el sector privado, cuya contribucin promedio explica aproximadamente el 85 % del crecimiento de la economa. En este tenor, al cierre de 2021 se alcanz una expansin interanual del PIB real de 12.3 % de acuerdo al comportamiento del valor agregado de las diferentes actividades econmicas que componen este indicador. Asimismo, si se compara el ndice de volumen de produccin de 2021 con el de 2019, arroja un crecimiento real de 4.7 %, todo lo cual explicamos de manera detallada al pas con gran sentido de responsabilidad. Una vez logrado este notable desempeo de la economa dominicana, que result ser mejor al de la mayora de los pases de la regin, y ante el alza de las presiones inflacionarias globales de magnitudes no observadas en algunas economas avanzadas en los ltimos 40 aos, el Banco Central inici un proceso gradual de restriccin monetaria a finales del ao 2021, con el propsito de evitar un sobrecalentamiento de la economa y una potencial salida de capitales, anticipndose a los incrementos en las tasas de inters que comenzaran a verificarse posteriormente en 2022 en las economas ms grandes. En ese sentido, se ha incrementado la tasa de poltica monetaria del Banco Central en 525 puntos bsicos, pasando de 3.0 % en noviembre de 2021 a 8.25 % en la actualidad. Adicionalmente, se ha reducido el excedente de liquidez del sistema financiero a travs de operaciones de mercado abierto y del retorno gradual de los recursos que haban sido otorgados durante la pandemia. Estas medidas de corte restrictivo para moderar la inflacin, pudieran merecer las crticas de algunos. No obstante, vale la pena resear al destacado economista Ben Bernanke, expresidente de la Reserva Federal y uno de los recin laureados con el Premio Nobel de Economa 2022, en su libro El Coraje de Actuar, cito: Tomar decisiones polticamente impopulares para el beneficio a largo plazo del pas es la razn por la cual la Reserva Federal existe como un banco central polticamente independiente. Fue creado precisamente con este propsito: hacer lo que se debe hacer, lo que otros no pueden o no quieren hacer. Actualmente, podemos afirmar que la postura expansiva de la poltica monetaria se ha revertido. En efecto, los incrementos realizados en la TPM, junto a la reduccin de las expectativas de inflacin, han provocado que la tasa de inters real interbancaria se encuentre aproximadamente un punto porcentual por encima de su nivel neutral estimado. De igual modo, las tasas de inters del mercado han aumentado a la vez que se ha observado una desaceleracin del ritmo de expansin de los agregados monetarios, lo que ha contribuido a un aterrizaje suave del desempeo de la economa dominicana. En efecto, el medio circulante (MI) ha moderado su crecimiento interanual de un mximo de 33 % en 2021 a expandirse en torno a 10 % al cierre de septiembre de 2022. No obstante, el crdito al sector privado en moneda nacional se mantiene creciendo por encima del 14 % interanual a septiembre, reflejando el impulso de la demanda interna y el sano dinamismo de los sectores productivos. Cabe sealar que la lucha de la poltica monetaria contra la inflacin se ha materializado en coordinacin con la poltica fiscal del Gobierno del presidente Luis Abinader, principalmente con la implementacin de subsidios a los combustibles y a la tarifa elctrica, as como a las iniciativas para bajar los costos de produccin en la agropecuaria. La efectividad de estas medidas se ha reflejado en la trayectoria descendente registrada por la inflacin interanual en los ltimos meses, al ubicarse en 8.63 % en septiembre para una reduccin de 100 puntos bsicos con respecto al mximo de 9.64 % alcanzado en el mes de abril del presente ao. Este comportamiento reciente es una seal de que se transita por el camino de lograr la convergencia de la inflacin al rango meta de 4 %  1 % durante el primer semestre de 2023. En efecto, la inflacin registr 0.29 % en el mes de septiembre de 2022, luego del 0.21 % del mes de agosto, variaciones que reflejan una importante moderacin con respecto a los 26 meses anteriores en los que la inflacin mensual promedi 0.78 %. Quisiera destacar adems que, al analizar los datos de 18 economas de Amrica Latina, se evidencia que la tasa de inflacin interanual de la Repblica Dominicana es inferior a la de once pases de la regin. Esto quiere decir que slo seis pases reportan una inflacin interanual por debajo de la dominicana, de los cuales tres son de economas dolarizadas (Panam, Ecuador y El Salvador). No me cabe la menor duda de que las decisiones de polticas econmicas tomadas en la Repblica Dominicana, tanto monetarias como fiscales, han sido oportunas y prudentes en el marco de los acontecimientos y circunstancias antes descritos. En efecto, el destacado economista y profesor de la Universidad de Columbia, Xavier Sala-i-Martin, calific recientemente en una comparecencia en el pas que las medidas adoptadas por el Banco Central fueron correctas y oportunas, en el contexto de la lucha contra la inflacin. Resultados preliminares de la economa enero-septiembre 2022 En cuanto a los resultados preliminares de la economa correspondientes al cierre del mes de septiembre de 2022, me complace compartirles la primicia de que el indicador mensual de actividad econmica (IMAE) registr una variacin interanual de 4.8 % en el mes de septiembre, para un crecimiento acumulado del Producto Interno Bruto real de 5.4 % en enero-septiembre de 2022 con respecto a igual periodo del ao anterior. Al analizar en detalle el comportamiento sectorial del PIB en enero-septiembre de 2022, se destaca la notable incidencia de los servicios en su conjunto, que constituyen aproximadamente el 60.0 % del total de la economa y presentan una variacin interanual acumulada de 7.2 %. Entre las actividades que lo componen, vale resaltar hoteles, bares y restaurantes (28.9 %), salud (11.7 %), otras actividades de servicios (9.1 %), administracin pblica (7.8 %), transporte y almacenamiento (7.0 %), comercio (6.6 %) y servicios financieros (5.7 %). Respecto a las industrias, la actividad de zonas francas creci 6.6 %, manufactura local 4.3 % y construccin 2.2 %; mientras la agropecuaria, creci 3.8 % en enero-septiembre 2022. La actividad hoteles, bares y restaurantes ha sido la de mayor incidencia en el desempeo del PIB en los primeros nueve meses del ao 2022, explicando aproximadamente la tercera parte de la expansin total del mismo en el referido perodo, al exhibir una variacin relativa de 28.9 % en trminos de valor agregado real. El presente ao ha sido extraordinario para el sector turstico en la Repblica Dominicana, superndose las expectativas de recuperacin tras el reto que ha significado la pandemia del COVID-19 y el conflicto blico Rusia-Ucrania para el turismo internacional. En efecto, se han registrado flujos sin precedentes en la llegada de pasajeros no residentes, acumulando 5.3 millones de visitantes en nueve meses, de acuerdo a los datos anunciados por el ministro de Turismo, David Collado, es decir, 6.5 % y 6.9 % ms visitantes no residentes que en 2018 y 2019, respectivamente. Lo anterior revela que, a pesar de las adversidades que ha enfrentado la industria turstica a nivel mundial ante la actual coyuntura internacional, la Repblica Dominicana se mantiene como el destino lder en trminos de llegada de turistas en la regin del Caribe Insular y Centroamrica. Estos son, sin duda alguna, logros dignos de resaltar dado el impulso que representa el turismo para la actividad productiva nacional y la generacin de divisas. Por otro lado, el incremento en los volmenes de produccin local de bienes y de las importaciones comercializables continan incidiendo positivamente en el desempeo de las actividades de comercio y transporte, las cuales exhiben tasas interanuales de 6.6 % y 7.0 %, respectivamente en enero-septiembre de 2022. El resultado de estos sectores est asociado a su vez al incremento verificado en los servicios de apoyo logstico de almacenamiento y distribucin. Adicionalmente, la manufactura de zonas francas ha sido una actividad clave para la recuperacin econmica, impulsando el encadenamiento productivo nacional y la expansin de las exportaciones. Particularmente en trminos de valor agregado real, el mismo registr un crecimiento interanual de 6.6 % en el presente ao, cnsono con el incremento de 11.7 % en las exportaciones de este sector. En lo que respecta a la manufactura local, se observa una variacin acumulada de 4.3 % explicada principalmente por el aumento en los volmenes de produccin de las industrias de fabricacin de metales comunes, de productos minerales no metlicos, elaboracin de bebidas alcohlicas, no alcohlicas y derivados del tabaco, de otros productos alimenticios y de sustancias y productos qumicos. En cuanto a la agropecuaria, esta actividad econmica acumul un incremento interanual de 3.8 % al cierre de los primeros nueve meses de 2022. La misma ha sido impactada por los altos costos de las materias primas importadas, por lo que las medidas implementadas por el Gobierno como el subsidio temporal para la importacin a tasa cero de algunos insumos requeridos en el proceso productivo, as como las facilidades de crdito a pequeos y medianos productores agropecuarios, han contribuido a su desempeo positivo. En lo que respecta al mercado laboral, los principales indicadores continan evidenciando una trayectoria de recuperacin. En este sentido, conforme los resultados de la Encuesta Nacional Continua de Fuerza de Trabajo (ENCFT) correspondientes al tercer trimestre de 2022, la tasa de desocupacin abierta, que comprende a los desocupados que estn buscando activamente trabajo, ha experimentado una reduccin de 3.2 puntos porcentuales, desde el 8.0 % registrado en enero-marzo de 2021 a 4.8 % en julio-septiembre de 2022. En lo referente a la poltica fiscal, se destacan las mayores recaudaciones con relacin a lo estimado inicialmente por la Direccin General de Impuestos Internos y la Direccin General de Aduanas, que han estado realizando una excelente labor. Esta mejora en los ingresos fiscales ha otorgado el espacio necesario para aplicar subsidios orientados a mitigar el impacto de los mayores precios de las materias primas sobre la produccin nacional y los hogares; as como para la asistencia a las provincias afectadas por el reciente paso del huracn Fiona, la cual ha sido estimada por el Gobierno que requerir una inversin en reparaciones de ms de RD$20,000 millones. En otro orden, los indicadores del sector externo mantuvieron una evolucin favorable durante el perodo enero-septiembre de 2022. De acuerdo con cifras preliminares, durante los primeros nueve meses de este ao las exportaciones totales ascendieron a US$10,543.3 millones, creciendo un 14.2 % de manera interanual. Dentro de las exportaciones, las correspondientes al sector de zonas francas siguen mostrando cifras rcord en lo que va de ao, acercndose a unos US$6,000 millones, para un aumento de 11.7 % con respecto al 2021. El potencial de expansin de zonas francas resulta evidente en la alta demanda de nuevas empresas para radicarse en el pas, lo que sustenta el continuo flujo de inversiones hacia este sector. Es importante destacar tambin el desarrollo positivo de las dems actividades generadoras de divisas, como el turismo, sector que se ha recuperado ms rpido de lo esperado con una llegada de 5.3 millones de visitantes no residentes, registrando ingresos por US$6,341.9 millones en enero-septiembre, y exhibiendo un incremento de 65.7 % con respecto a igual periodo de 2021. De igual forma, las remesas alcanzaron US$7,309.4 millones en los primeros nueve meses de 2022, reflejando la solidaridad de la dispora dominicana. Asimismo, en este perodo se recibieron flujos del orden de los US$2,870.4 millones por concepto de inversin extranjera directa, aumentando en 19.1 % respecto al mismo perodo de 2021, lo que reitera la confianza de los inversionistas internacionales en la estabilidad de la economa dominicana con reglas claras y transparentes, un clima de paz social, adems del encomiable trabajo que ha venido realizando el Gabinete de Promocin de Inversiones del pas. Estos mayores ingresos de divisas han favorecido la estabilidad relativa del tipo de cambio, reflejada en una apreciacin acumulada de la moneda local de 7 % al cierre de septiembre, siendo la segunda de mayor magnitud despus de Uruguay que ha registrado un 7.1 %. En adicin, han contribuido al fortalecimiento de las reservas internacionales hasta ubicarse cercanas a US$14,000 millones, equivalentes a 12.3 % del PIB y 5.7 meses de importaciones, superando las mtricas recomendadas por el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI). Respecto al comportamiento del sistema financiero consolidado, al cierre de septiembre de 2022, los indicadores demuestran su fortaleza patrimonial, sustentada en adecuados niveles de solvencia, rentabilidad y bajos niveles de morosidad. En ese orden, la posicin de solvencia alcanz 16.0 % a julio de 2022, de acuerdo a la ms reciente informacin publicada por la Superintendencia de Bancos, lo que evidencia el cumplimiento con holgura del requerimiento mnimo de 10%, exigido por las disposiciones legales vigentes. En cuanto al indicador de rentabilidad sobre el patrimonio (ROE), ste fue de 22.7 % y sobre activos promedio (ROA) de 2.6 %. Cabe destacar que el coeficiente de morosidad se situ en apenas un 1.0%. En el caso de la banca mltiple, la cual representa el 88.4 % del sistema financiero nacional por sus niveles de activos, present una solvencia de 14.6 %, rentabilidad sobre el patrimonio de 25.3 %, sobre sus activos 2.6 % y un coeficiente de morosidad de 0.9 %. Logros institucionales En el mbito institucional, me complace sobremanera enfatizar que esta institucin en el transcurso de sus 75 aos de existencia siempre se ha mantenido a la vanguardia de los ltimos avances tecnolgicos. En ese sentido me permito compartir brevemente con ustedes, tres iniciativas de significativo valor para el Banco Central. La primera, es nuestro centro de ciberseguridad, que en su segundo ao de operaciones sigue contribuyendo a apoyar en la mitigacin de los efectos y la propagacin de posibles eventos de ciberseguridad en el sistema financiero y de pagos, que a su vez pudiesen devenir en un riesgo sistmico o reputacional. Este centro es un gran logro por el que hemos recibido el reconocimiento local e internacional. En ese mismo orden, como bien saben, en junio pasado publicamos la Estrategia Nacional de Inclusin Financiera, incorporando la tecnologa para construir un ecosistema de pagos al que todos los ciudadanos puedan acceder, apoyada en un uso intensivo de medios digitales complementado con educacin financiera personalizada. Finalmente, este ao inauguramos el Hub de Innovacin Financiera, con el respaldo del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) y con el concurso de las superintendencias de Bancos, del Mercado de Valores, de Seguros y de Pensiones. Este Hub permitir potenciar las iniciativas privadas en esta materia, fomentando su factibilidad y sostenibilidad. Amigos presentes, mis palabras estaran incompletas si no menciono los aportes de nuestra institucin al arte y la cultura en sus distintas manifestaciones. En ese sentido, contamos con una de las bibliotecas especializadas mejor equipadas del pas y con espacios orientados a la promocin de actividades culturales y acadmicas. Asimismo, se destaca la coleccin de publicaciones editadas por el Banco Central, que ha aportado a la sociedad ms de 250 obras en sus distintas series: arte y literatura; ciencias sociales y econmicas; numismtica y filatlica; msica de compositores dominicanos; y diversas obras premiadas. Adems, en lo social, contamos con un voluntariado formado por el propio personal dedicado a contribuir con soluciones a problemas que afectan a los sectores ms vulnerables de la poblacin. Perspectivas y reflexiones finales Amigos todos, tomando en consideracin el impulso que ha mantenido la actividad econmica durante los primeros nueve meses del ao, el sistema de pronsticos del Banco Central indica que el crecimiento PIB real se ubicara en el rango de 5.0 %-5.5 % para el ao 2022, es decir, en torno al ritmo potencial de la economa. Igualmente, organismos internacionales como el FMI y la Comisin Econmica para Amrica Latina y el Caribe (CEPAL) mantienen una perspectiva positiva para la economa dominicana, proyectando una expansin superior a 5.0 % para el pas en 2022. Con respecto al PIB nominal, se espera que el mismo alcance unos US$112,000 millones al cierre de 2022, lo cual, junto al manejo prudente de las finanzas pblicas por el Ministerio de Hacienda y la estabilidad cambiara observada durante el presente ao, han sido elementos determinantes para que la deuda del sector pblico consolidado como proporcin del PIB se ubique por debajo de 60 % al finalizar el ao, reducindose respecto a los niveles registrados en aos recientes. Cabe destacar, adems, que el manejo eficiente de pasivos por dicho ministerio ha contribuido a reducir el servicio de la deuda y mejorar su sostenibilidad en el tiempo. En cuanto a la evolucin de los precios internos, cnsono con las condiciones de liquidez en un escenario activo de poltica monetaria y el mantenimiento de los subsidios a los combustibles y la energa elctrica en lo que resta del ao, se espera que la inflacin termine el 2022 en torno a 7.0 % y la misma continuara reducindose en trminos interanuales en los meses sucesivos para converger al rango meta de 4.0 % 1.0 % en la primera mitad de 2023. Como afirm durante mi participacin en las recin finalizadas Reuniones Anuales de 2022 del FMI y el Banco Mundial en Washington, DC, los bancos centrales deben permanecer enfocados en controlar la inflacin, ya que, sin estabilidad de precios, los beneficios del crecimiento estn en riesgo de ser eliminados, generando un impacto social negativo, sobre todo para la poblacin ms vulnerable. Asimismo, las previsiones para el sector externo apuntan a que los flujos de inversin extranjera directa alcanzaran los US$3,800 millones al cierre de 2022. De igual forma, se pronostica que este ao cerrara con exportaciones totales superiores a los US$14,000 millones, un mximo histrico; remesas cercanas a los US$10,000 millones e ingresos por turismo por encima de US$8,500 millones. Todo esto, sumado a los ingresos por otros servicios, estimados en unos US$3,000 conllevara a finalizar el ao con ingresos de divisas superiores a los US$39,300 millones, una cifra rcord. Un aspecto relevante a resaltar es que los fuertes fundamentos macroeconmicos del pas son destacados por los economistas, inversionistas y analistas financieros a la hora de realizar sus pronsticos para el desempeo del prximo ao 2023. A manera de ejemplo, el Bank of America, en el marco de las referidas reuniones anuales del FMI y el Banco Mundial en Washington, reiter en su informe Perspectivas para las economas emergentes que la Repblica Dominicana ser de las economas de mayor crecimiento de la regin para 2023, ante la desafiante coyuntura internacional. De igual forma, Moiss Nam, exdirector ejecutivo del Banco Mundial, indic recientemente en nuestro pas que la Repblica Dominicana est entre los pases que no tendrn recesin y que se encuentra en buenas condiciones para salir airoso en el escenario adverso que se proyecta para el ao entrante. Finalmente, estimada familia bancentraliana, estos ltimos aos han sido de los ms difciles para la humanidad, pero indudablemente han servido para acumular una experiencia invaluable en lo que respecta al manejo coordinado de crisis y que puede ser un insumo muy valioso de cara al futuro para trabajar con el mismo ahnco y afrontar integralmente los retos que como nacin tenemos por delante. Apoyado en la resiliencia que la economa dominicana ha demostrado en los momentos desafiantes, como fiel abanderado del optimismo, me siento confiado de que a travs de un esfuerzo mancomunado entre el sector pblico y privado, donde el primero ha puesto de manifiesto la aplicacin de medidas oportunas para solventar los momentos de mayor calamidad en los sectores econmicos y de la poblacin ms vulnerable, y el segundo ha sabido adaptarse a la realidad de los tiempos, manteniendo encendida la maquinaria de produccin y generacin de empleos, continuaremos el camino de la estabilidad y el crecimiento econmico. De nuestra parte, tengan la certeza de que el Banco Central continuar realizando su labor como ente emisor, de velar por la estabilidad de precios y garantizar la regulacin del sistema financiero y de pagos para cumplir con cabalidad nuestro lema aniversario de trabajar por una estabilidad que se siente. Que Dios los bendiga a todos, hoy, maana y siempre! Muchas gracias. Viernes 21 de octubre, 2022

Title: BCRD concludes its first diploma course on cybersecurity
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: BCRD concludes its first diploma course on cybersecurity Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. The governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic (BCRD), Hector Valdez Albizu, delivered the closing speech of the first Diploma on Cybersecurity offered by the institution, whose purpose has been to promote a culture of information security and data protection, as well as to share knowledge on this topic of such importance for the business and personal environment. Valdez Albizu said that "in the digital era we are living in, and due to the proliferation of the use of technology in all areas of human endeavor, it is essential to know what cybersecurity is and how to protect ourselves in this new environment, which is managed through computers and cell phones." He also stressed that "it is essential in our society to be up to date on technological innovation, cybercrime, the hidden network, digital identity, data protection and digital assets, as a basis for constantly creating and innovating a legal framework that responds to all threats that may arise." He recalled that the Monetary Board authorized the creation of the Sectoral Center for Response to Cyber Security Incidents (SPRICS), an investment of the Central Bank with the highest technological level, which came into operation in 2020. On the same, he pointed out that "this center is the nodal point that contributes greatly to the participants of the Dominican financial system being able to prevent and protect themselves from cyberattacks, since, among other activities, it recommends immediate actions in the face of events that could affect them." The training was aimed at journalists, communicators and directors of communication departments for 48 hours, distributed over six Saturdays, in the BCRD auditorium, being integrated and coordinated by the Central Classroom program for economic and financial education. The course, organized by BCRD, was coordinated with the participation of institutions linked to the issues of security, data protection and management and prevention of cybercrime in the Dominican Republic, members of the National Cybersecurity Council (CNSC). The National Police (PN), the Dominican Institute of Telecommunications (Indotel), the Ministry of Defense (MIDE), the Superintendence of Banks (SB) and the Government Office of Information and Communication Technology (OGTIC) participated. Among the main speakers were, for the BCRD: the deputy manager of Systems and Technological Innovation, Fabiola Herrera; the directors of Systems and Technology, Payment Systems, and Cyber and Information Security, Sabrina Diaz, angel Gonzalez and Ruddy Simons, respectively; Cesar Novo, responsible for the management of SPRICS; and Emiko Hidaka, Cybersecurity consultant. On behalf of the collaborating institutions, Cesar Moline, Indotel and CNCS participated; Piero Alvigini, MIDE and CNCS; magistrate Esther Agelan; James Pichardo of the SB; Carlos Leonardo of the CNCS; and Armando Manzueta of the OGTIC. Among the topics discussed during the training were: Payment systems; Cybersecurity: concepts, definition, history and trends; Technology innovation: systems, artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, internet of things (IoT), and ML; Cybersecurity Vs Cybercrime - Regulation and national and international legislative frameworks; and Money: past, present and future. Also, Digital Assets; Cybercrimes: Child protection, violence against women and human trafficking Online; Data: handling, protection, access; Darkweb: the hidden network; Trends in cybersecurity and cybercrime threats; Cybersecurity: On social networks; Role of the press in communication in the face of crises and cyber events; Digital Identity in the Face of Cybersecurity - Future in the Dominican Republic. Likewise, Cybersecurity: Protection recommendations in the personal and family environment; Cybersecurity: Recommendations for the protection of journalists' professional activity in the digital age; a wrap-up panel on cybersecurity and cybercrime journalism in the Dominican Republic; and a cyberattack simulation with a "RANSOMWARE" with the corresponding crisis communication management. November 1, 2022
text_original: BCRD concluye su primer diplomado sobre ciberseguridad Santo Domingo, Repblica Dominicana. El gobernador del Banco Central de la Repblica Dominicana (BCRD), Hctor Valdez Albizu, pronunci el discurso de clausura del primer Diplomado sobre Ciberseguridad ofrecido por la institucin, cuyo fin ha sido promover una cultura de seguridad de la informacin y proteccin de datos, as como compartir conocimientos sobre este tema de tanta importancia para el entorno empresarial y personal. Valdez Albizu expres que en la era digital que estamos viviendo, y debido a la proliferacin de uso de la tecnologa en todas las reas del quehacer humano, es indispensable saber qu es la ciberseguridad y cmo protegernos en este nuevo entorno, que se maneja a travs de los computadores y los telfonos celulares. Asimismo, destac que se hace imprescindible en nuestra sociedad estar al da en la innovacin tecnolgica, el ciberdelito, la red oculta, la identidad digital, la proteccin de los datos y los activos digitales, como base para crear e innovar constantemente un marco legal que responda a todas las amenazas que se puedan presentar. Record que la Junta Monetaria autoriz la creacin del Centro Sectorial de Respuesta a Incidentes de Seguridad Ciberntica (SPRICS), una inversin del Banco Central con el ms alto nivel tecnolgico, el cual entr en operacin en el ao 2020. Sobre el mismo, seal que este centro es el punto nodal que contribuye en gran medida a que los participantes del sistema financiero dominicano puedan prevenir y protegerse de los ciberataques, pues, entre otras actividades, recomienda acciones inmediatas frente a eventos que pudiesen afectarles. La capacitacin estuvo dirigida a periodistas, comunicadores y directores de departamentos de comunicacin durante 48 horas, distribuidas en seis sbados, en el auditorio del BCRD, estando integrada y coordinada por el programa Aula Central para la educacin econmica y financiera. El diplomado, organizado por BCRD, se coordin con la participacin de las instituciones vinculadas a los temas de seguridad, proteccin y gestin de datos y prevencin de ciberdelitos en la Repblica Dominicana, miembros del Consejo Nacional de Ciberseguridad (CNSC). Participaron la Polica Nacional (PN), el Instituto Dominicano de Telecomunicaciones (Indotel), el Ministerio de Defensa (MIDE), la Superintendencia de Bancos (SB) y la Oficina Gubernamental de Tecnologa de Informacin y Comunicacin (OGTIC). Entre los principales expositores, se encontraban, por el BCRD: la subgerente de Sistemas e Innovacin Tecnolgica, Fabiola Herrera; los directores de Sistemas y Tecnologa, Sistemas de Pagos, y Seguridad Ciberntica y de la Informacin, Sabrina Daz, ngel Gonzlez y Ruddy Simons, respectivamente; Csar Novo, responsable de la gestin del SPRICS; y Emiko Hidaka, consultor de Ciberseguridad. Por las instituciones colaboradoras, participaron Csar Molin, Indotel y CNCS; Piero Alvigini, el MIDE y CNCS; la magistrada Esther Ageln; James Pichardo de la SB; Carlos Leonardo del CNCS; y Armando Manzueta de la OGTIC. Entre los temas que se trataron durante la capacitacin destacaron: Sistemas de pago; Ciberseguridad: conceptos, definicin, historia y tendencias; Innovacin tecnolgica: sistemas, inteligencia artificial (IA), computacin en la nube, internet de las cosas (loT) y ML; Ciberseguridad Vs ciberdelito - Regulacin y marcos legislativos nacionales e internacionales; y El dinero: pasado, presente y futuro. Tambin, Activos digitales; Ciberdelitos: La proteccin infantil, violencia contra la mujer y trata de personas Online; Datos: manejo, proteccin, acceso; Darkweb: la red oculta; Tendencias en las amenazas de ciberseguridad y ciberdelito; Ciberseguridad: En redes sociales; Rol de la prensa en la comunicacin ante crisis y eventos cibernticos; La identidad digital ante la Ciberseguridad - Futuro en Repblica Dominicana. Igualmente, Ciberseguridad: Recomendaciones de proteccin en el entorno personal y familiar; Ciberseguridad: Recomendaciones para la proteccin en la actividad profesional del periodista en la era digital; un panel de recapitulacin sobre el periodismo en materia de ciberseguridad y ciberdelito de la Repblica Dominicana; y un simulacro de ciberataque con un RANSOMWARE con el correspondiente manejo de comunicacin de crisis. 1 de noviembre de 2022

Title: Remarks by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Hctor Valdez Albizu, at the Latin American Congress on Financial Technology and Innovation, organized by the Latin American Federation of Banks (FELABAN)
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Hector Valdez Albizu, at the Latin American Congress on Financial Technology and Innovation, organized by the Latin American Federation of Banks (FELABAN)  Mr. Giorgio Trettenero, Secretary General of FELABAN;  Mr. Marco Antonio Rodriguez, President of the Latin American Committee on Banking Automation (CLAB);  Mrs. Rosanna Ruiz, Executive President of the Association of Multiple Banks of the Dominican Republic (ABA) and Vice President of FELABAN;  Mr. Joel Santos, Minister of the Presidency;  Mr. Victor Bisono, Minister of Industry and Commerce;  Mr. Alejandro Fernandez, Superintendent of Banks;  Distinguished Presidents and Representatives of Associations and Entities of the Latin American Financial Sector  Distinguished speakers and panelists;  Ladies and gentlemen: It is a great pleasure for me to address you at this important regional congress and to greet you cordially, on behalf of the authorities of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic and on my own behalf. In turn, I would like to thank the Latin American Federation of Banks, in the person of its Secretary General, Mr. Giorgio Trettenero, and the Association of Banks of the Dominican Republic, in the person of its active and appreciated Executive President, Mrs. Rosanna Ruiz, for the invitation extended to us to speak at this important event. so timely for the Dominican Republic and other countries present here, at a time of great financial innovation. As everyone present knows, the banking business has undergone substantial transformations in the last decade, driven by technological development and changes in the needs of financial users, which have motivated the transition of financial activity from physical spaces to digital environments. Likewise, financial technology companies or Fintechs have emerged, which compete, and also complement, traditional banking. For this reason, and in response to the request made by FELABAN, I would like to divide these words into three different but complementary themes. First, I will refer to regulatory trends in digital banking; then, I will tell you about our recent experiences in terms of cybersecurity in the financial and payment system of the Dominican Republic, and, finally, I will present a brief brushstroke on the vision of our Central Bank with regard to financial innovation. Friends, to talk about regulatory trends in digital banking, it is necessary to first refer to the process of digital transformation that Dominican banking has undergone, starting with the reforms implemented from 2006 that created the Payment System of the Dominican Republic. To give you an idea, in our country, Internet Banking users, who in 2014 totaled 1.4 million, as of September of this year, reach a community of 5.9 million users. Saying 5.9 million users of digital banking services in a country of 11 million inhabitants is an important figure. But more importantly, the trend of Dominican banks towards the digitization of their services is increasing. I am even very pleased to announce here that the Monetary Board approved and is already operating in the country the first completely digital multiple bank, with local capital. This is a milestone in the history of the Dominican financial system, and I am sure that it will not be the only one. Friends, we certainly have many reasons to be proud of the successes we have achieved and for which we have been the object of recent recognitions, highlighting the one granted by the Senate of the Republic to me for the great contributions in favor of the economic development of the nation and the investiture as Doctor Honoris Causa in Economic and Business Sciences by the APEC University. which constitutes the highest distinction in the academic field that an economics professional can obtain to exalt life achievements and contributions to the well-being of society, distinctions that I have received with joy and of course with the greatest humility. In a similar order, by 2018 there were about 20 financial technology companies, while by 2022, more than 50 of these entities are already operating in the local market, providing services in various segments, such as payments, personal and business finance management, alternative financing, financial assets and capital markets. among others, according to information from the union that groups them. With regard to regulations that promote digitalisation, it is necessary to talk about the Payment Systems Regulation. Its first version was issued by the Monetary Board in 2007 and laid the foundations and motivation for the creation of a dynamic, modern, secure and reliable payment ecosystem in the country. As an example, I would like to mention the Instant Payments service, whose growth has maintained an exponential trend, reaching for the period January-October 2022 an increase of 47.3% in the volume of payments settled in the Central Bank's RTGS system, compared to the same period of the previous year, and an extraordinary 338.9%, compared to 2019. Fourteen years after the issuance of this regulation, we have a new version that includes the lessons learned in all these years, in which the country's payment ecosystem has not stopped evolving and growing. One of the main novelties is the creation of Electronic Payment Companies (EPEs), which come to occupy a market niche that has not been served until now. Of these, one is already operating and another authorized to operate by the Monetary Board. These companies, with their agility, will play a complementary role to traditional banking. Before moving on to the second topic of these words, I cannot fail to refer in this forum to the digital currencies that could be issued by central banks (CBDCs), which would be their obligations, originated and transferred by digital means, and which would have the support of the issuing entities. In this regard, like other central banks, we are exhausting a phase of analysis and exploring the nature, monetary impact and functionality of these schemes; with the advice of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the accompaniment of the Center for Latin American Monetary Studies (CEMLA), together with a group of central banks. Following this line, we agree with the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), which in its 2022 Annual Economic Report states, and I quote: "... The monetary and financial system of the future should combine digital features with trust in central banks," and goes on to say, "An explosion of creative innovation in money and payments is taking place, opening up prospects for a future digital monetary system that continuously adapts to serve the public interest. A system based on central bank money offers a stronger basis for innovation, ensuring that services are stable and interoperable, nationally and across borders. " Quite the opposite of what is happening in the cryptocurrency market, which are highly volatile and speculative virtual assets, without legal support or guarantees, and many of them used in Ponzi schemes. This year, they have lost more than half their value, and experts predict that they will continue to decline. On this, the Central Bank warned citizens in 2017 and again in 2021, that operating with these assets is risky. I quote: "Any person who acquires this type of virtual asset, either as an investment or with the interest of using it as a means of payment, as well as anyone who accepts them as a form of payment in commercial transactions, will do so at their own risk." Dear friends, in my opinion, one of the most important considerations for the technological transformation of the financial sector is the challenge posed by cybersecurity. Cybercrime is an activity whose growth we must try to stop at all costs. It is estimated that its annual cost to the world economy is around 6 trillion dollars, by 2021. This figure is more than the national income of many countries, including some emerging economies. In view of the above, in 2016, the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, aware that advances towards digitization in financial systems cause a great dependence on technology, observed with concern the consequent increase in cyberattacks on financial infrastructures in other countries. For this reason, we have taken the decision to carry out a series of actions aimed at strengthening the cybersecurity and information security functions of all regulated entities, in order to contribute to the protection of the technological platforms of the direct and indirect participants of the Payment System of the Dominican Republic (SIPARD). critical infrastructure that is the heart and circulatory system of financial activity in our country. Of these actions, I would like to mention two. The first was the preparation of the Cybersecurity and Information Security Regulations, approved by the Monetary Board in November 2018. I would like to take this opportunity to tell you that, thanks to the implementation of this Regulation, the entities of the national financial system were better prepared to face the increase in cyberattacks worldwide during the pandemic, and we had nothing to regret in that regard. The second action I want to refer to is the creation of a centralised structure, the Sectoral Cyber Security Incident Response Centre for the Financial and Payments Sector (SPRICS). This center, under the administrative dependence of the Central Bank, aims to support the entities of the system in mitigating the effects and propagation of possible cybersecurity events, which in turn could become a systemic or reputational risk. The Monetary Board of the Dominican Republic approved this project, which came into operation in 2020. It currently has 80 connected participants: banks, stock market and payment system administrators. This Center follows up on the cybersecurity events reported by the participants and then generates the alerts and reports that allow the necessary measures to be executed in order to prevent cyberattacks from materializing. With this, we are greatly contributing to reducing the systemic risk of such attacks and, therefore, to protecting our country's financial and payment system. I want to take this opportunity to give you the scoop that the central banks of Central America, with which we operate the regional payment system (SIPA), will be interconnected to our Sectoral Incident Response Center, since the Central American Monetary Council approved it at its last meeting. With this, the process of generating threat intelligence will be enriched and deepened, for the benefit of all the financial institutions that participate and the central banks that I have mentioned. These, gentlemen, are two of the main weapons we have to face cyber threats: communication and collaboration. The last topic of my words is Financial Innovation. But before I talk to you about technology and innovative initiatives, I would like to allow me to make a brief reflection that will serve as a framework and backdrop for what follows. It is well known that the reality we live in today is totally different from the one we knew decades ago, and even from the reality of two years ago, before the pandemic. The world is moving towards total digitalization, at breakneck speed. As individuals, we have to live adapting to this new reality every day, every hour. Whoever is not able to do so, will become obsolete. This state of affairs presents us with challenges, but also opportunities. Why am I telling you this? Simple. Because I believe that technology exists to serve man, for the COMMON GOOD. Innovation, in itself, is empty if it does not have a purpose. That is why the challenge as islands. And the opportunity is to take advantage of all the resources that are within our reach to be more efficient, more productive, but working as a team and contributing to the common good.
