Title: Speech by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Hctor Valdez Albizu, before the Association of Industrialists of the Northern Region (AIREN)
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Speech by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Hector Valdez Albizu, to the Association of Industrialists of the Northern Region (AIREN) May 24, 2023 Good morning, I want to begin my words by expressing my sincere gratitude to the board of directors of the Association of Industrialists of the Northern Region (AIREN) and especially to its president, Juan Ventura, for the invitation to present the Central Bank's vision of the economic performance of the Dominican Republic and the leading role of this region in national development. I would also like to extend a cordial greeting to the members of the various business and academic sectors, as well as to the public officials present. For us it is always a pleasure to be able to visit Cibao, to exchange opinions and see first-hand the strength of its productive sectors. Perfect Storm: Multiple Shocks and Policy Backlash Since I last shared with you, in October 2018, the international environment has become complex and convulsive. As you know, in 2020 the world faced its biggest health emergency in a century, a pandemic that has affected more than 760 million people and cost almost 7 million human lives. This crisis forced all governments in the world to implement confinement and border closure measures to combat the spread of COVID-19, extraordinarily affecting the productive capacity of companies and deteriorating household incomes. Particularly for our country, the shock of COVID-19 caused an abrupt drop in economic activity of approximately -30% in the month of April 2020. As a result, the labor market weakened, with a significant increase in the open unemployment rate, which reached 8.0% during the pandemic. Faced with this monumental challenge, the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic reacted in a timely manner, applying a set of expansive monetary and financial measures with the purpose of mitigating the impact of the health crisis. In this sense, the monetary policy rate was reduced to its lowest historical level, of 3.00%, while resources for some RD215 billion (equivalent to 5% of the gross domestic product -GDP-) were channeled through financial intermediaries, being the most extensive monetary stimulus plan in the Central American and Caribbean region. The execution of this monetary program was complemented by a successful management of the health crisis, led by the President of the Republic Luis Abinader, through the implementation of a social subsidy plan to protect the most vulnerable families and the efficient vaccination campaign of the Health Cabinet, which was coordinated by Vice President Raquel Pena and recognized by the World Health Organization (WHO). Dear friends, this adequate coordination of policies contributed to our country experiencing one of the fastest economic recoveries in Latin America after the unprecedented shock generated by the pandemic. Indeed, the economy managed to rebound progressively, going from the drop of almost -30% mentioned above to a variation of -6.7% by the end of 2020. Subsequently, economic activity experienced a great boost by growing 12.3% in 2021 and 4.9% in 2022. As a result of this dynamism, nominal GDP in dollars has increased by 45% since 2020, from less than US79 billion to US114 billion at the end of 2022; while GDP per capita increased from US7,544 to US10,733 during the same period. Similarly, a significant improvement has been achieved in the labor market, with an increase of about 528 thousand employed since the second quarter of 2020, allowing the level of employment to be currently above that registered prior to the pandemic. These results have contributed to a reduction in the open unemployment rate, from the aforementioned peak of 8.0% to 4.8% at the end of 2022. After having overcome the worst phase of the pandemic, and as the economic recovery process progressed, significant increases in commodity prices, mainly oil and food, began to materialize. In addition, distortions were generated in global supply chains that caused significant increases in the cost of transporting goods through containers. These inflationary pressures worldwide were exacerbated by the outbreak of the war between Russia and Ukraine at the beginning of 2022, due to the influence of these countries in international markets as important producers of raw materials. In this second stage, the main challenge for the world's central banks, including Latin American countries, has been to face inflationary pressures by applying restrictive monetary measures. In this sense, in an environment of higher interest rates and restricted liquidity, financial turbulence was generated in the United States and Europe, which triggered bankruptcies and mergers of several banking entities. As I have pointed out on more than one occasion, this combination of shocks constituted a perfect storm, which has substantially increased the level of uncertainty and deteriorated the global economic outlook. Fortunately, the economy of the United States, our main trading partner, has been more resilient than expected, with the unemployment rate remaining at historically low levels, boosting consumption and allaying concerns of a possible recession in that country. In the domestic context, faced with the challenge of global inflationary pressures, the Central Bank implemented a gradual process of monetary tightening since the end of 2021, being the first to react in the Central American region and anticipating advanced economies. In this sense, the monetary policy rate was gradually increased by 550 basis points, going from 3.00% to 8.50% annually between November 2021 and October 2022. As a result, interest rates have been adjusted upwards, while monetary aggregates have slowed significantly. Specifically, the growth rate of the circulating medium (MI) went from a maximum of 30% year-on-year during 2021 to 8.5% in April 2023; while the expanded money supply (M2) and broad money (M3) expand by 9.7% and 8.0%, respectively, consistent with the variation in nominal GDP and with what is contemplated in the monetary program. During the last six months, the Central Bank has paused the adjustments to its reference interest rate, since the monetary policy transmission mechanism has been successful in moderating inflationary pressures. In this way, the monetary measures, together with the subsidies applied by the Government, have contributed to a reduction of 449 basis points in year-on-year inflation, going from a maximum of 9.64% in April 2022 to 5.15% in April 2023. Dear friends, these advances allow me to share with you the good news and scoop that, according to the latest estimates, inflation would enter the target range of 4% 1% by the end of this month of May, earlier than expected. This achievement would provide the necessary space for the Central Bank to adopt timely measures that contribute to relaunching growth during the rest of the year, preserving macroeconomic stability. On the other hand, I would like to highlight the dynamism of foreign exchange-generating activities. Tourism is spearheading the economy, generating revenues of more than US8,400 million in 2022 with the arrival of 8.5 million non-resident visitors, of which 7.2 million arrived by air and 1.3 million on cruise ships. It is important to note that in 2022 the Northern Region received more than 1.1 million tourists through its airports and 80% of cruise passengers. Likewise, remittance flows during 2022 stood at almost US10 billion, of which 40% were received in Cibao. Meanwhile, foreign direct investment exceeded US4 billion last year, of which about US1 billion was allocated to projects located in this area. These good results and the confidence of investors in our country have contributed to the stability of the foreign exchange market. In this context of high foreign exchange generation and to avoid an abrupt appreciation of the Dominican peso that would harm the competitiveness of the activities of the external sector, the Central Bank has been buying significant amounts of dollars from financial intermediaries through auctions on its electronic platform. Just to give you an idea, during 2022 the Central Bank made net purchases of foreign currency for about US1,600 million, which has contributed to the strengthening of international reserves, which stand at around US16,300 million to date. Economic importance of the Northern region Dear friends, in this part of my presentation I would like to highlight the fundamental contribution of the North region to the national economy. Aware of the importance of Cibao, the Central Bank created in 2017 the Division of Regional Studies and Statistics, based in the Regional Office of Santiago. The objective of this team is to carry out research, build indicators and carry out meetings in the different provinces of the region that allow a better understanding of their economic performance; serving as support for entrepreneurs, investors and public policy makers. Below, I will present the main findings of the studies and reports carried out by this technical team, which will be available at the conclusion of this discussion. In this regard, allow me to inform you that different investigations by the Central Bank indicate that the fourteen provinces of this geographical enclave contribute between 32% and 38% of the national economic activity. Moreover, during the pandemic, Cibao was the region that exhibited the smallest drop in its productive activity and, subsequently, was the one that recovered the fastest. In this context, employment levels in the North region were the least affected during the health crisis, reflected in an unemployment rate significantly lower than the national total in that period. In particular, Cibao has remained a leader in agricultural production, being the main supplier of food in our country, supplying about 55% of national agricultural production. Additionally, the North region has a preponderant role in several agricultural products that have positioned themselves as leaders in international markets. Thus, Cibao concentrates 77% of the area planted with cocoa and more than 90% of the national production of tobacco for cigars. On the other hand, the North region stands out in the free zone sector, concentrating more than half of the country's industrial parks, which are home to almost 400 companies of this type. In addition, this activity was one of the most important in the recovery process after the pandemic and has contributed to sustaining employment, generating more than 200 thousand direct jobs nationwide, of which about 70 thousand are in the Cibao region. In turn, according to estimates by the Central Bank, the North region has an incidence of 40% of construction activity at the national level, in addition to being home to several of the main cement and steel production companies in the country. Likewise, the region is home to the largest mining companies that contribute the most to the national GDP. This economic boost of Cibao is reflected in the development of the financial system, concentrating 37% of the country's bank offices, which has allowed greater access to financing for companies and households. In addition, around 40% of banknote processing, deposits and cash withdrawals by financial intermediaries are carried out through the Regional Office in Santiago. These positive results reaffirm the need to continue supporting projects that enhance productive activities in the region and contribute to job creation. For example, the various road and mass transport infrastructure works being built in the region, as well as the expansion project of the port of Manzanillo, will significantly improve the competitiveness of Cibao. Likewise, in Manzanillo, the installation of 1,200 megawatts of energy stands out, which would complement the energy production matrix of the region, where half of the country's hydroelectric plants are located. Additionally, in the tourism sector, the Punta Bergantin project in the province of Puerto Plata stands out, which includes the construction of hotels, a film studio and a campus aimed at promoting innovation; which will be an important source of quality job creation for the region. Challenges and prospects Finally, dear friends, I would like to refer to the prospects and challenges of the Dominican economy going forward. First, some uncertainties persist related to the financial turbulence experienced in advanced economies. It is important to reiterate that the domestic financial system does not have direct interaction with the entities that have presented problems and maintains a solid performance. Specifically, the solvency of the financial system stands at 16.7%, well above the 10% required and the delinquency rate is only 1.0%. While the return on equity (ROE) of 26.7% and on assets (ROA) of 3.3% as of March 2023. On the other hand, extreme weather events pose a permanent risk to our economy. For example, the occurrence of floods, tornadoes and Storm Fiona at the end of last year, as well as the current drought, have posed a great challenge to national agricultural production. In addition, the growing arrival of sargassum to our coasts represents a great challenge to tourism and other areas of the economy. In this regard, the Central Bank is making progress in the design of measures that facilitate the channeling of financing to the sectors most vulnerable to climate change. These policies would complement the government's actions in recent years, such as the technical strengthening of agricultural producers, a massive reforestation plan throughout the national geography and the increase in electricity generation through renewable sources, such as wind and photovoltaic. In addition, our country has great opportunities for mining exploitation that must be taken advantage of, implementing measures that guarantee environmental sustainability. On the other hand, the Dominican Republic has ideal conditions, such as social peace, political stability and a good business climate, to attract investment in the current environment of geopolitical tensions and the reconfiguration of international trade. Given this, the geographical location and logistics processes of our country are favorable for attracting companies that seek to bring their production chains closer to the markets, which is known as nearshoring. In addition, we must continue to take advantage of the tourism potential of our country, which is attracting important investment projects throughout the national geography. It is worth mentioning that, in the first four months of 2023 alone, more than 3.7 million non-resident visitors have been received, with the goal of about 10 million tourists expected to be reached by the end of the year. Dear friends, the Dominican economy has maintained a good performance, despite the complex situation. Thus, it is emerging as one of the fastest growing countries in the region during this year 2023, with an expansion of around 4.0% and with inflation that will be within the target. Indeed, this positive assessment was endorsed by the IMF's recent Article IV mission, which highlighted that "the economy of the Dominican Republic has been one of the most dynamic and resilient in the Americas in the last two decades" and that the outlook for our country is favorable, thanks to the proper implementation of policies and solid economic fundamentals. I would like to conclude my remarks by expressing my confidence that the Dominican Republic will continue to successfully overcome future challenges and preserve the macroeconomic stability that has characterized us, supported by the strength of its economy and the commitment of its productive sectors, such as those represented here. These conditions will continue to be the basis for sustained growth, generating more and more jobs and better living conditions for Dominicans. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Discurso del gobernador del Banco Central de la Repblica Dominicana, Hctor Valdez Albizu, ante la Asociacin de Industriales de la Regin Norte (AIREN) 24 de mayo de 2023 Buenos das, quiero iniciar mis palabras expresando mi ms sincero agradecimiento a la junta directiva de la Asociacin de Industriales de la Regin Norte (AIREN) y especialmente a su presidente, Juan Ventura, por la invitacin para presentarles la visin del Banco Central sobre el desempeo econmico de la Repblica Dominicana y el rol protagnico de esta regin en el desarrollo nacional. Asimismo, quiero extenderles un cordial saludo a los miembros de los distintos sectores empresariales y acadmicos, as como a los funcionarios pblicos presentes. Para nosotros siempre es un placer poder visitar el Cibao, para intercambiar opiniones y constatar de primera mano la pujanza de sus sectores productivos. Tormenta perfecta: Mltiples choques y reaccin de polticas Desde la ltima ocasin en que compart con ustedes, en octubre de 2018, el entorno internacional se ha tornado complejo y convulso. Como es de su conocimiento, en el ao 2020 el mundo enfrent su mayor emergencia sanitaria en un siglo, una pandemia que ha afectado a ms de 760 millones de personas y ha costado casi 7 millones de vidas humanas. Esta crisis oblig a todos los gobiernos del mundo a implementar medidas de confinamiento y de cierre de fronteras para combatir la propagacin del COVID-19, afectando de forma extraordinaria la capacidad productiva de las empresas y deteriorando los ingresos de los hogares. De manera particular para nuestro pas, el choque del COVID-19 provoc una cada abrupta de la actividad econmica de aproximadamente -30 % en el mes de abril de 2020. Como consecuencia, se debilit el mercado laboral, con un aumento significativo de la tasa de desempleo abierta, que alcanz un 8.0 % durante la pandemia. Ante este monumental desafo, el Banco Central de la Repblica Dominicana reaccion de forma oportuna, aplicando un conjunto de medidas monetarias y financieras expansivas con el propsito de mitigar el impacto de la crisis sanitaria. En ese sentido, la tasa de poltica monetaria se redujo a su nivel histrico ms bajo, de 3.00 %, a la vez que se canalizaron recursos por unos RD$215 mil millones (equivalente a 5 % del producto interno bruto -PIB-) a travs de los intermediarios financieros, siendo el plan de estmulo monetario ms amplio de la regin de Centroamrica y el Caribe. La ejecucin de este programa monetario se complement con a una gestin acertada de la crisis sanitaria, encabezada por el presidente de la Repblica Luis Abinader, a travs de la implementacin de un plan de subsidios sociales para proteger a las familias ms vulnerables y de la eficiente campaa de vacunacin del Gabinete de Salud, que fue coordinada por la vicepresidenta Raquel Pea y reconocida por la Organizacin Mundial de la Salud (OMS). Estimados amigos, esta adecuada coordinacin de polticas contribuy a que nuestro pas experimentara una de las ms rpidas recuperaciones econmicas en Amrica Latina luego del choque sin precedentes que gener la pandemia. En efecto, la economa logr repuntar progresivamente, pasando de la cada de casi -30 % mencionada anteriormente a una variacin de -6.7 % para el cierre del ao 2020. Posteriormente, la actividad econmica experiment un gran impulso al crecer 12.3 % en 2021 y 4.9 % en 2022. Como resultado de este dinamismo, el PIB nominal en dlares se ha incrementado en un 45 % desde el ao 2020, al pasar de menos de US$79 mil millones a US$114 mil millones al cierre del ao 2022; mientras que el PIB per cpita aument de US$7,544 a US$10,733 durante el mismo perodo. De igual forma, se ha logrado una mejora importante en el mercado laboral, con un incremento de unos 528 mil ocupados desde el segundo trimestre del 2020, permitiendo que actualmente el nivel de empleo se encuentre por encima del registrado previo a la pandemia. Estos resultados han contribuido a una reduccin de la tasa de desempleo abierta, del mximo de 8.0 % mencionado anteriormente a 4.8 % al cierre de 2022. Luego de haber superado la peor fase de la pandemia, y conforme se avanzaba en el proceso de recuperacin econmica, comenzaron a materializarse incrementos importantes en los precios de los commodities, principalmente del petrleo y los alimentos. Adems, se generaron distorsiones en las cadenas de suministros globales que provocaron aumentos significativos en el costo del transporte de mercancas a travs de contenedores. Estas presiones inflacionarias a nivel mundial se exacerbaron al estallar la guerra entre Rusia y Ucrania a inicios del ao 2022, debido a la influencia de estos pases en los mercados internacionales como productores importantes de materias primas. En esta segunda etapa, el principal reto de los bancos centrales del mundo, incluyendo a los pases de Amrica Latina, ha sido enfrentar las presiones inflacionarias aplicando medidas monetarias restrictivas. En este sentido, en un entorno de mayores tasas de inters y de liquidez restringida, se generaron turbulencias financieras en Estados Unidos y en Europa, que desencadenaron quiebras y fusiones de varias entidades bancarias. Como he sealado en ms de una ocasin, esta combinacin de choques constituy una tormenta perfecta, que ha incrementado sustancialmente el nivel de incertidumbre y deteriorado el panorama econmico mundial. Afortunadamente, la economa de Estados Unidos, nuestro principal socio comercial, ha sido ms resiliente de lo previsto, con una tasa de desempleo que se mantiene en niveles histricamente bajos, impulsando el consumo y disipando las preocupaciones de una posible recesin en ese pas. En el contexto domstico, ante el desafo de las presiones inflacionarias globales, el Banco Central implemento un proceso gradual de restriccin monetaria desde finales de 2021, siendo el primero en reaccionar de la regin de Centroamrica y anticipndose a las economas avanzadas. En ese sentido, la tasa de poltica monetaria se increment de forma paulatina en 550 puntos bsicos, al pasar de 3.00 % a 8.50 % anual entre noviembre de 2021 y octubre de 2022. Como resultado, las tasas de inters se han ajustado al alza, mientras los agregados monetarios se han desacelerado de forma importante. Especficamente, la tasa de crecimiento del medio circulante (MI) pas de un mximo de 30 % interanual durante 2021 hasta 8.5 % en abril de 2023; mientras que la oferta monetaria ampliada (M2) y el dinero en sentido amplio (M3) se expanden en 9.7 % y 8.0 %, respectivamente, consistente con la variacin del PIB nominal y con lo contemplado en el programa monetario. Durante los ltimos seis meses el Banco Central ha hecho una pausa en los ajustes a su tasa de inters de referencia, ya que el mecanismo de transmisin de la poltica monetaria ha sido exitoso en moderar las presiones inflacionarias. De esta forma, las medidas monetarias, unidas a los subsidios aplicados por el Gobierno, han contribuido a una reduccin de 449 puntos bsicos en la inflacin interanual, al pasar de un mximo de 9.64 % en abril de 2022 a 5.15 % en abril de 2023. Estimados amigos, estos avances me permiten compartir con ustedes la buena noticia y primicia de que, segn las ltimas estimaciones, la inflacin entrara al rango meta de 4 %  1 % al cierre de este mismo mes de mayo, antes de lo que estaba previsto. Este logro otorgara los espacios necesarios para que el Banco Central adopte oportunamente medidas que contribuyan a relanzar el crecimiento durante el resto del ao, preservando la estabilidad macroeconmica. Por otro lado, quiero destacar el dinamismo de las actividades generadoras de divisas. El turismo est siendo la punta de lanza de la economa, generando ingresos por ms de US$8,400 millones en el ao 2022 con la llegada de 8.5 millones de visitantes no residentes, de los cuales 7.2 millones arribaron por va area y 1.3 millones en cruceros. Es importante resaltar que en el ao 2022 la Regin Norte recibi ms de 1.1 millones de turistas por sus aeropuertos y el 80 % de los cruceristas. Asimismo, los flujos de remesas durante el ao 2022 se ubicaron en casi US$10 mil millones, de los cuales un 40 % se recibieron en el Cibao. En tanto, la inversin extranjera directa super los US$4 mil millones el pasado ao, de los cuales cerca de US$1 mil millones se destinaron a proyectos ubicados en esta zona. Estos buenos resultados y la confianza de los inversionistas en nuestro pas han contribuido con la estabilidad del mercado cambiario. En este contexto de alta generacin de divisas y para evitar una apreciacin abrupta del peso dominicano que perjudique la competitividad de las actividades del sector externo, el Banco Central ha estado comprando montos importantes de dlares a los intermediarios financieros por medio de subastas en su plataforma electrnica. Slo para que tengan una idea, durante el ao 2022 el Banco Central realiz compras netas de divisas por unos US$1,600 millones de dlares, lo que ha contribuido al fortalecimiento de las reservas internacionales que se ubican en torno a los US$16,300 millones a la fecha. Importancia econmica de la regin Norte Estimados amigos, en esta parte de mi presentacin quisiera resaltar el aporte fundamental de la regin Norte a la economa nacional. Conscientes de la importancia del Cibao, el Banco Central cre en el ao 2017 la Divisin de Estudios y Estadsticas Regionales, con sede en la Oficina Regional de Santiago. El objetivo de este equipo es realizar investigaciones, construir indicadores y llevar a cabo encuentros en las distintas provincias de la regin que permitan una mejor comprensin de su desempeo econmico; sirviendo de apoyo para empresarios, inversionistas y hacedores de polticas pblicas. A continuacin, les presentar los principales hallazgos de los estudios y reportes realizados por este equipo tcnico, que estarn disponibles al concluir este conversatorio. En ese sentido, permtanme informarles que distintas investigaciones del Banco Central apuntan a que las catorce provincias de este enclave geogrfico aportan entre un 32 % y un 38 % de la actividad econmica nacional. Ms an, durante la pandemia, el Cibao fue la regin que exhibi la menor cada en su actividad productiva y, posteriormente, fue la que ms rpido se recuper. En ese contexto, los niveles de empleo en la regin Norte fueron los menos afectados durante la crisis sanitaria, reflejndose en una tasa de desempleo significativamente inferior al total nacional en ese perodo. De manera particular, el Cibao se ha mantenido como lder en la produccin agrcola, siendo el principal abastecedor de alimentos de nuestro pas, supliendo cerca de un 55 % de la produccin agrcola nacional. Adicionalmente, la regin Norte tiene un rol preponderante en varios productos agropecuarios que se han posicionado como lderes en los mercados internacionales. As, el Cibao concentra el 77 % de la superficie sembrada de cacao y ms del 90 % de la produccin nacional de tabaco para cigarros. Por otro lado, la regin Norte se destaca en el sector de las zonas francas, concentrando ms de la mitad de los parques industriales del pas, que albergan casi 400 empresas de este tipo. Adems, esta actividad fue de las ms importantes en el proceso de recuperacin luego de la pandemia y ha contribuido a sostener el empleo, generando ms de 200 mil puestos de trabajos directos a nivel nacional, de los cuales unos 70 mil se encuentran en la regin del Cibao. A su vez, segn estimaciones del Banco Central, la regin Norte tiene una incidencia de un 40 % de la actividad de construccin a nivel nacional, adems de albergar a varias de las principales empresas cementeras y productoras de acero del pas. Asimismo, en la regin se encuentran las empresas mineras ms grandes y que ms aportan al PIB nacional. Este empuje econmico del Cibao se refleja en el desarrollo del sistema financiero, concentrando el 37 % de las oficinas bancadas del pas, lo que ha permitido un mayor acceso al financiamiento de empresas y hogares. Adems, a travs de la Oficina Regional de Santiago se realiza alrededor del 40 % del procesamiento de billetes, de los depsitos y del retiro de efectivo por parte de los intermediarios financieras. Estos resultados positivos reafirman la necesidad de seguir apoyando proyectos que potencien las actividades productivas de la regin y contribuyan con la creacin de empleos. Por ejemplo, las distintas obras de infraestructura vial y de transporte masivo que se estn construyendo en la regin, as como el proyecto de ampliacin del puerto de Manzanillo, mejorarn significativamente la competitividad del Cibao. Asimismo, en Manzanillo se destaca la instalacin de 1,200 megavatios de energa, que complementara la matriz de produccin energtica de la regin, donde se encuentra la mitad de las hidroelctricas del pas. Adicionalmente, en el sector turismo se destaca el proyecto de Punta Bergantn en la provincia de Puerto Plata, que contempla la construccin de hoteles, un estudio de cine y un campus destinado a fomentar la innovacin; que ser una fuente importante de generacin de empleos de calidad para la regin. Desafos y perspectivas Finalmente, estimados amigos, quisiera referirme a las perspectivas y los desafos de la economa dominicana hacia adelante. En primer lugar, persisten algunos factores de incertidumbre relacionados a las turbulencias financieras experimentadas en las economas avanzadas. Es importante reiterar que el sistema financiero domstico no posee una interaccin directa con las entidades que han presentado problemas y mantiene un slido desempeo. Especficamente, la solvencia del sistema financiero se ubica en 16.7 %, muy por encima del 10 % requerido y la morosidad es de apenas 1.0 %. Mientras que la rentabilidad sobre el patrimonio (ROE) de 26.7 % y sobre los activos (ROA) de 3.3 % a marzo de 2023. En otro orden, los fenmenos climticos extremos suponen un riesgo permanente para nuestra economa. Por ejemplo, la ocurrencia de inundaciones, tornados y la tormenta Fiona a finales del ao pasado, as como la actual sequa, han significado un gran desafo para la produccin agrcola nacional. Adems, la llegada creciente de sargazo a nuestras costas, representa un gran reto al turismo y a otras reas de la economa. En ese tenor, el Banco Central est avanzando en el diseo de medidas que faciliten la canalizacin de financiamiento a los sectores ms vulnerables al cambio climtico. Estas polticas complementaran las acciones del Gobierno de los ltimos aos, como el fortalecimiento tcnico de los productores agropecuarios, un plan masivo de reforestacin en toda la geografa nacional y el incremento de la generacin elctrica a travs de fuentes renovables, como elica y fotovoltaica. Adems, nuestro pas posee grandes oportunidades para la explotacin minera que debe aprovecharse, implementando las medidas que garanticen la sostenibilidad del medio ambiente. Por otro lado, la Repblica Dominicana posee condiciones idneas, como la paz social, la estabilidad poltica y el buen clima de negocios, para atraer inversiones ante el actual entorno de tensiones geopolticas y de reconfiguracin del comercio internacional. Ante esto, la ubicacin geogrfica y los procesos logsticos de nuestro pas son favorables para captar empresas que busquen acercar sus cadenas productivas a los mercados, lo que se conoce como el nearshoring. Adicionalmente, debemos continuar aprovechando el potencial turstico de nuestro pas que est atrayendo importantes proyectos de inversin en toda la geografa nacional. Vale la pena mencionar que, slo en los primeros cuatro meses del 2023, se han recibido ms de 3.7 millones de visitantes no residentes, previndose que se alcanzara la meta de unos 10 millones de turistas para el cierre del ao. Estimados amigos, la economa dominicana ha mantenido un buen desempeo, a pesar de la compleja coyuntura. As, se perfila como uno de los pases de mayor crecimiento en la regin durante este ao 2023, con una expansin en torno a 4.0% y con una inflacin que estar dentro de la meta. En efecto, esta valoracin positiva fue avalada por la reciente misin de Artculo IV del FMI, la cual resalt que la economa de la Repblica Dominicana ha sido una de las ms dinmicas y resilientes del continente americano en las ltimas dos dcadas y que las perspectivas para nuestro pas son favorables, gracias a la implementacin adecuada de polticas y a fundamentos econmicos slidos. Deseo concluir mis palabras expresndoles mi confianza de que la Repblica Dominicana seguir sorteando exitosamente los retos futuros y preservando la estabilidad macroeconmica que nos ha caracterizado, apoyada en la fortaleza de su economa y el compromiso de sus sectores productivos, como los aqu representados. Estas condiciones seguirn siendo la base de un crecimiento sostenido, generando cada vez ms empleos y mejores condiciones de vida para los dominicanos. Muchas gracias.

Title: Remarks by the Governor of the Central Bank, Hctor Valdez Albizu, at the opening ceremony of "Expo Mercado de Valores 2023"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Remarks by the governor of the Central Bank, Hector Valdez Albizu, at the ceremony of opening of "Stock Market Expo 2023" October 3, 2023 Good morning: It is an honor for me, in my capacity as Governor of the Central Bank and President of the Monetary Board and the National Securities Market Council, to welcome you most cordially to this prestigious opening ceremony of "Expo Mercado de Valores 2023", the first Capital Market fair in the Dominican Republic, an initiative that arises with the purpose of unifying efforts and providing a space where economic agents and the general public can To know the benefits and opportunities offered by the capital market of our country, through its entire offer of products, both for investors and issuers. I am pleased to see here gathered regulators, business leaders, investors, market participants, issuers of securities, other economic agents and the general public, who make up the fabric that drives the development of our economy, so these days will be conducive to the exchange of knowledge and reflect on the challenges posed by the immediate and future trends of our stock market. in the context and evolution of markets at a global level. Your presence here demonstrates your commitment to the continued development of our capital market and to the progress of our country. As many of those present are aware, the Central Bank has been immersed, since its inception, in promoting the emergence, strengthening and development of the stock market in our country, as an alternative source of financing for the productive sectors and due to its importance for the implementation of monetary policy, with the ultimate aim of promoting macroeconomic stability and resilience and the development of the country. The actions adopted by the Central Bank have been aimed at three important areas: the development of the legal and institutional framework of the market; the reform of the Securities Payment and Settlement System of the Dominican Republic (SIPARD) and the dematerialization of our securities issues in CEVALDOM. Of these actions, I would like to highlight the following aspects:  With regard to the development of the legal and institutional framework of the market, it is necessary to highlight the support of the Central Bank in the formulation of the regulatory framework with the enactment of the former Law 19-00, as well as the support provided to the Superintendence of the Securities Market with specialized human capital and physical space for its initial installation.  Similarly, we made a joint effort with the Superintendence of the Securities Market for the approval of the current Law No. 249-17, as well as the preparation of its implementing regulations.  Regarding the reform of the Securities Payment and Settlement System of the Dominican Republic (SIPARD), the Central Bank has promoted important initiatives in the regulatory, technological and operational fields, among which I highlight the implementation of the Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system administered by this Institution, which has had a primary impact on the development of the local securities market. because it efficiently allows the settlement of securities transactions in the primary market and facilitates the delivery against payment, in real time, of transactions traded in the secondary securities market.  With regard to the dematerialization of the Central Bank's securities issues as part of open market operations, within the framework of the implementation of monetary policy, since the beginning of 2000 we have been largely adopting the regional standards promoted by the Central American Monetary Council (CMCA), which I have the honor to chair. the most relevant being the dematerialization of securities issues that were previously carried out in physical form, thus helping to promote the formation of prices in the secondary market of these instruments. For this important task of dematerializing our securities issuances, it was necessary to decisively support CEVALDOM in its beginnings, as a private entity that would offer the services of Centralized Securities Depository. As part of its strengthening, that entity achieved more adequate levels of capitalization; reached a strategic alliance with a securities depository in Peru; and complied with the requirements of the Central Bank to successfully connect with the securities payment and settlement system and with the electronic auction mechanism used in our open market operations. Today, after two decades of constant development of our securities market, we can affirm with great satisfaction that the Central Bank's commitment to this market has borne tangible fruits, measured by the volumes traded in securities and the levels of efficiency of its different infrastructures, as well as by its security, reliability and transparency. all elements, which have an important impact on the protection of investors, as the main pillar enshrined in our Securities Market Law. In fact, at the end of 2022, the volume of public offering securities in national and foreign currency in CEVALDOM's custody represents 36% in relation to GDP, having doubled in the last ten years. This new regulatory framework, in addition to its focus on a greater projection of investors, is oriented towards transparency in operations, the creation of new trading mechanisms and the opening to new issuers of public offerings. As a result of this opening, recently, the first placement of publicly offered shares of a private company in the Dominican stock market was made, deserving to highlight the role played by the Securities Market Promotion Law No. 163-21 enacted by President Luis Abinader on August 3, 2021. It is important to note that the development of the local capital market generates significant advantages for the economy of the Dominican Republic through several mechanisms. First, it provides local companies with an additional way of direct financing through the issuance of financial instruments such as stocks and bonds and indirectly through investment funds and trusts, allowing investment in infrastructure, innovation, technology projects, among others, promoting greater economic activity with its consequent generation of new jobs. On the other hand, the development of the capital market is an axis of attraction for local and foreign investors, which in addition to generating greater capital flows to the economy, increases confidence in the country's investment environment. In other words, a dynamic capital market, with adequate and timely regulatory practices, must reflect positively on the country's credit rating and on the promotion of a culture of transparency, contributing to reducing borrowing costs for the country. We understand that the achievements achieved so far by the stock market of our country should encourage us to continue identifying potentialities for greater growth and efficiency, such as: continuing to promote the issuance of securities such as corporate bonds and publicly offered shares; achieving greater volumes traded in centralized trading mechanisms such as stock exchanges; and to promote a greater use of reference price vectors in the determination of the value of financial instruments, to avoid possible regulatory arbitrages that could occur with the existence of different price references for the same security. I think, my friends, that with these advances, our stock market is on its way to firmly placing itself among the global benchmark financial markets, strengthening itself as an important link in our sustained economic growth. In the current challenging and turbulent international environment, the positive evolution of the Dominican stock market constitutes an element of strength for the Dominican economy, which contributes to the fact that, from the Monetary Board and the Central Bank, we can continue to adopt timely and precise measures in the face of the changes that occur in the domestic and international environment and that we permanently monitor. Finally, I want to thank you for your presence and your contribution to make this fair a successful event, while urging you to continue betting with firm steps on our stock market, so that it continues to develop competitively and efficiently, as an alternative financing for investment projects and a greater diversification of pension fund investments. that contributes to a greater development of our country, a significant improvement in living conditions for all Dominicans and continues to look to the future with optimism, certainty and confidence. Thanks a lot!
text_original: Palabras del gobernador del Banco Central Hctor Valdez Albizu, en el acto de apertura de Expo Mercado de Valores 2023 3 de octubre de 2023 Buenos das: Es un honor para m, en mi condicin de Gobernador del Banco Central y Presidente de la Junta Monetaria y del Consejo Nacional del Mercado de Valores, darles la ms cordial bienvenida a este prestigioso acto de inauguracin de Expo Mercado de Valores 2023, primera feria del Mercado de Capitales de la Repblica Dominicana, iniciativa que surge con el propsito de unificar esfuerzos y proporcionar un espacio donde agentes econmicos y pblico en general puedan conocer los beneficios y oportunidades que ofrece el mercado de capitales de nuestro pas, a travs de toda su oferta de productos, tanto para inversionistas como para emisores. Me complace ver aqu reunidos a reguladores, lderes empresariales, inversionistas, participantes del mercado, emisores de valores, dems agentes econmicos y pblico en general, que conforman el tejido que impulsa el desarrollo de nuestra economa, por lo que estos das sern propicios para el intercambio de conocimientos y reflexionar sobre los retos que nos plantean las tendencias inmediatas y futuras de nuestro mercado de valores, en el contexto y la evolucin de los mercados a nivel global. Su presencia aqu demuestra su compromiso con el continuo desarrollo de nuestro mercado de capitales y con el progreso de nuestro pas. Como es del conocimiento de muchos de los presentes, el Banco Central ha estado inmerso, desde sus inicios, en promover el surgimiento, fortalecimiento y desarrollo del mercado de valores de nuestro pas, como fuente alternativa de financiamiento para los sectores productivos y por su importancia para la implementacin de la poltica monetaria, con el fin ulterior de fomentar la estabilidad y resiliencia macroeconmica y el desarrollo del pas. Las acciones adoptadas por el Banco Central han estado orientadas a tres importantes mbitos: el desarrollo del marco legal e institucional del mercado; la reforma del Sistema de Pago y Liquidacin de Valores de la Repblica Dominicana (SIPARD) y la desmaterializacin de nuestras emisiones de valores en CEVALDOM. De dichas acciones me permito destacar los aspectos siguientes: 1) En torno al desarrollo del marco legal e institucional del mercado, es preciso resaltar el soporte del Banco Central en la formulacin del marco regulatorio con la promulgacin de la antigua Ley 19-00, as como el apoyo brindado a la Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores con capital humano especializado y espacio fsico para su instalacin inicial. 2) De igual forma, realizamos un esfuerzo mancomunado con la Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores para la aprobacin de la Ley vigente Nm. 249-17, as como la elaboracin de sus reglamentos de aplicacin. 3) Sobre la reforma del Sistema de Pago y Liquidacin de Valores de la Repblica Dominicana (SIPARD), el Banco Central ha impulsado importantes iniciativas en el mbito normativo, tecnolgico y operativo, entre las que destaco la implementacin del sistema de Liquidacin Bruta en Tiempo Real (LBTR) administrado por esta Institucin, la cual ha tenido un impacto primordial en el desarrollo del mercado de valores local, debido a que permite, de manera eficiente, la liquidacin de las operaciones de valores en el mercado primario y facilita la entrega contra pago, en tiempo real, de las operaciones transadas en el mercado secundario de valores. 4) Con relacin a la desmaterializacin de las emisiones de valores del Banco Central como parte de las operaciones de mercado abierto, en el marco de la instrumentacin de la poltica monetaria, desde inicios del 2000 hemos venido adoptando en gran medida los estndares regionales impulsados por el Consejo Monetario Centroamericano (CMCA), el cual me honro en presidir, siendo el ms relevante la desmaterializacin de las emisiones de valores que se realizaban anteriormente de forma fsica, coadyuvando de esta manera a promover la formacin de precios en el mercado secundario de dichos instrumentos. Para esta importante tarea de desmaterializar nuestras emisiones de valores, fue necesario apoyar decididamente a CEVALDOM en sus inicios, como entidad privada que ofrecera los servicios de Depsito Centralizado de Valores. Como parte de su fortalecimiento, esa entidad logr niveles ms adecuados de capitalizacin; arrib a una alianza estratgica con una depositara de valores de Per; y cumpli con los requerimientos del Banco Central para conectarse de manera exitosa con el sistema de pagos y liquidacin de valores y con el mecanismo electrnico de subastas utilizado en nuestras operaciones de mercado abierto. Hoy da, luego de dos dcadas de desarrollo constante de nuestro mercado de valores, podemos afirmar con mucha satisfaccin que la apuesta por parte del Banco Central a dicho mercado ha dado frutos tangibles, medidos por los volmenes transados de valores y los niveles de eficiencia de sus diferentes infraestructuras, as como por su seguridad, fiabilidad y transparencia, elementos todos, que tienen un impacto importante en la proteccin a los inversionistas, como principal pilar consagrado en nuestra Ley del Mercado de Valores. En efecto, al cierre de 2022 el volumen de los valores de oferta pblica en moneda nacional y extranjera en custodia de CEVALDOM representa un 36% con relacin al PIB, habindose duplicado en los ltimos diez aos. Este nuevo marco normativo, adems de su enfoque hacia una mayor proyeccin de los inversionistas, se orienta hacia la transparencia en las operaciones, a la creacin de nuevos mecanismos de negociacin y la apertura a nuevos emisores de oferta pblica. Producto de esta apertura, recientemente, se realiz la primera colocacin de acciones de oferta pblica de una empresa privada en el mercado de valores dominicano, mereciendo ser resaltado el rol que jug para este importante logro la Ley de Fomento del Mercado de Valores No. 163-21 promulgada por el presidente Luis Abinader en fecha 3 de agosto del 2021. Es importante destacar que el desarrollo del mercado de capitales local genera ventajas significativas para la economa de la Repblica Dominicana a travs de varios mecanismos. En primer lugar, proporciona a las empresas locales una va adicional de financiamiento directo a travs de la emisin de instrumentos financieros como acciones y bonos y de forma indirecta por medio de fondos de inversin y fideicomisos, permitiendo fomentar la inversin en proyectos de infraestructura, innovacin, tecnologa, entre otros, propiciando una mayor actividad econmica con su consecuente generacin de nuevos empleos. Por otro lado, el desarrollo del mercado de capitales constituye un eje de atraccin para inversionistas locales y extranjeros, que adems de generar mayores flujos de capitales hacia la economa, aumenta la confianza en el ambiente de inversin del pas. Es decir, que un mercado de capitales dinmico, con prcticas regulatorias adecuadas y oportunas, se debe reflejar positivamente en la calificacin crediticia del pas y en el fomento de una cultura de transparencia, contribuyendo a reducir los costos de endeudamiento para el pas. Entendemos que los logros alcanzados hasta hoy por el mercado de valores de nuestro pas deben impulsarnos a seguir identificando potencialidades de mayor crecimiento y eficiencia, como podra ser: continuar fomentando las emisiones de valores como los bonos corporativos y acciones de oferta pblica; lograr mayores volmenes transados en los mecanismos centralizados de negociacin como las bolsas de valores; y promover un mayor uso de vectores de precios de referencia en la determinacin del valor de los instrumentos financieros, para evitar posibles arbitrajes regulatorios que pudieran ocurrir con la existencia de diferentes referencias de precios para un mismo valor. Pienso, mis amigos, que con estos avances, nuestro mercado de valores se encamina a colocarse con firmeza entre los mercados financieros de referencia global, fortalecindose como un eslabn de importancia para nuestro crecimiento econmico sostenido. Ante el actual entorno internacional retador y convulso, la evolucin positiva del mercado de valores dominicano constituye un elemento de fortaleza para la economa dominicana, que contribuye a que, desde la Junta Monetaria y el Banco Central, podamos continuar adoptando medidas oportunas y precisas ante los cambios que se suceden en el entorno domstico e internacional y que vigilamos permanentemente. Finalmente, quiero agradecer su presencia y su contribucin para hacer de esta feria un evento exitoso, al tiempo de exhortarles a que sigamos apostando con pasos firmes a nuestro mercado de valores, para que contine desarrollndose de forma competitiva y eficiente, como una alternativa de financiamiento a los proyectos de inversin y a una mayor diversificacin de las inversiones de los fondos de pensiones, que contribuya a un mayor desarrollo de nuestro pas, una mejora significativa en las condiciones de vida para todos los dominicanos y continuar mirando al futuro con optimismo, certidumbre y confianza. Muchas gracias!

Title: Speech by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Hctor Valdez Albizu, on the institution's seventy-sixth anniversary
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Dominican Republic
text: Speech by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Hector Valdez Albizu, in the seventy-sixth Anniversary of the institution It is with a spirit full of joy and great satisfaction that I appear once again before you to commemorate the 76th anniversary of the founding of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic. Looking back, I confess that I have experienced special and unique moments on each of the twenty-six occasions on which I have had the honor of addressing you on a new anniversary. As always, as this emblematic date arrives, I take the opportunity to show the main achievements in the field of monetary policy and comment on the situation, both international and domestic, and the challenges that the future holds. As a man of faith, I would like to begin by recalling the Sacred Scriptures that invite us, always and for whatever reason, to give thanks to God our Father. I thank the Creator for granting me the strength to, together with an extraordinary team of men and women, guide the destinies of the Central Bank with strict adherence to the Dominican Constitution and the Monetary and Financial Law. I also thank His Excellency President Luis Abinader Corona for the trust placed in me to lead the Central Bank, a commitment that I assume daily with firmness and determination, but with the due respect and humility that a selfless service to the country requires. I would also like to recognize the members of the Honorable Monetary Board, who, in compliance with their duties within the highest body of the Monetary and Financial Administration, have been key players in guaranteeing the success of all the initiatives implemented in the area of monetary, financial and exchange rate policy. I must say that the national and international achievements that today give prestige to our institution would not be possible without the tenacious work of the formidable team of officials and employees of the Central Bank that accompanies me in my daily work. I am convinced, dear friends, that in the little or how much a human being can achieve in his or her journey through life, there is always the family. Therefore, I would like to first acknowledge my beloved spouse Fior for her love, her great understanding and her absolute support for the tasks I have been given. To my dear son Hector Manuel and his spouse Begona who, upon receiving the blessing of becoming parents of Cayetano, gave me the title of grandfather, a decoration that overflows me with immense joy. Also to my siblings whom I love dearly and who, together with my father and my mother who watch over my well-being from heaven, have been my support during all these years. At this time, allow me, as is the tradition on each new anniversary, to share with you the recent behavior of the Dominican economy and its future prospects. Fully understanding the current situation and its possible evolution requires an understanding of how we face the turbulent and complex international environment that generated major disruptions in the global economy. Let's start with the role of monetary policy in this context and its main results in terms of inflation. MONETARY POLICY AND INFLATION As is well known, in the final phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, the world experienced inflationary pressures as a result of greater liquidity that was necessary to face the problems arising from the health crisis, the increase in commodity prices, mainly oil and food, and the cost of transporting goods through containers. These pressures were aggravated by the war between Russia and Ukraine, generating what I have called a perfect storm on other occasions. In this context, the Central Bank implemented a monetary tightening plan by increasing its policy rate and withdrawing the stimulus provided to the financial system during the pandemic. These measures, although difficult, were necessary to preserve price stability. As I have previously quoted Ben Bernanke, former chairman of the Federal Reserve of the United States and Nobel Prize winner, said in his book The Courage to Act: "Making unpopular decisions for the benefit of the country in the long run is the raison d'etre of a Central Bank. This type of institution is created to do what needs to be done." The Central Bank's measures, together with government subsidies to mitigate the rise in commodity prices, reduced inflation from 9.64% in April 2022 to 4.41% in September 2023. Similarly, core inflation, which excludes the prices of the most volatile components of the basket such as some food, fuel, and other items with regulated prices, decreased from 7.29% in May 2022 to 4.68% in September 2023. It should be noted that both measures of inflation are within the target range of 4% 1% of the monetary program. In essence, price stability was recovered in a highly complex situation. The significance of this major achievement can be seen in the words of Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund at the annual meetings in Marrakesh: "Price stability is critical. It is a prerequisite for growth and protects people, especially the poor." With inflation under control, monetary policy became more expansionary. The Central Bank reduced its monetary policy rate (MPR) by 100 basis points, from 8.50% in May 2023 to 7.50% today. Thus, the rate of the permanent liquidity expansion facility (1-day Repo) stands at 8.0% per annum; while the rate of interest-bearing deposits (Overnight) is at 6.25% per annum. These decisions will contribute to reducing the financing costs of financial institutions and will have an impact on lower interest rates in the financial system. In addition, the Monetary Board approved a monetary expansion program through the liberalization of the legal reserve requirement and the establishment of a rapid liquidity facility for the placement by financial institutions of resources to households and the productive sectors. In the case of the legal reserve, in January some RD21,000 million were released to be lent to the construction and acquisition of low-cost housing, while in June another RD34,000 million were approved for various productive activities and households. In total, the liquidity measures have made it possible to channel some RD126,000 million to sectors such as commerce and MSMEs, consumption and housing, construction, manufacturing, agriculture, among others, in most cases at rates no higher than 9.0%, resources that were placed through financial intermediation entities. The process does not stop here. I am pleased to announce that, in October, the Monetary Board authorized a new rapid liquidity facility (FLR) for RD40,000 million to be directed, this time to the construction, manufacturing, export and agricultural sectors. Of these resources, as of October 19, the financial system has already channeled some RD13,735 million. The increase in liquidity generated by these measures can be seen in the upward trend in monetary aggregates as of September, generally with expansions above nominal gross domestic product (GDP) growth. Specifically, the circulating medium MI registered a year-on-year growth of 11.2% in September; while the expanded money supply M2, which also includes longer-term deposits, increased by 17.0%; and M3 broad money, which adds other foreign currency deposits to M2, expanded by 14.6% during the same period. Another positive result of recent monetary policy is that the decline in the MPR has had an impact on the weighted average of the lending rate, which has been reduced by 200 basis points, from 15.9% in May to 13.9% last September. In turn, during that same period, the passive interest rate fell from 10.4% to 8.4%. In a context of declining interest rates, credit to the private sector in local currency has expanded by around 17% year-on-year in September. In addition, it should be noted that the Dominican Republic has not been the only country to reduce its MPR in Latin America. As inflation in the region has declined in recent months, several countries have begun to normalize their monetary stance. In this sense, so far this year reductions have been observed in Costa Rica (250 basis points), Uruguay (200), Chile (175), Brazil (100), Paraguay (50) and Peru (50). PRELIMINARY RESULTS OF THE ECONOMY Dear friends, it is no secret to anyone that the actions of the Dominican Central Bank were not an isolated phenomenon, but, as in other central banks around the world, were part of an effort to moderate the inflationary pressures generated in the pandemic. In a restricted environment of monetary liquidity at the global level, countries stabilized their price levels, but at the cost of lower economic growth. In the case of the Dominican Republic, despite this unfavorable international environment, the economy is expected to grow above the Latin American average this year. The preliminary results that I am going to share with you and with friends of the press confirm a recovery process that must be maintained as long as the monetary transmission channel continues to operate and public investment continues to be executed. According to the latest available data, I am pleased to share with you the scoop of the monthly indicator of economic activity (IMAE) that grew 3.1% in September 2023, the highest monthly rate of this year, indicating that the monetary policy transmission mechanism is operating. With this result, the year-on-year growth of the quarterly real gross domestic product (GDP) stood at 2.6%, for a cumulative January-September of 1.7%. The largest contribution in January-September came from hotels, bars and restaurants, which grew 10.9%, maintaining the great dynamism exhibited throughout the year. In September alone, the country received 478,792 tourists by air, accumulating a record of 6,023,573 non-resident passengers during the first nine months of the year, with a hotel occupancy rate of 75%. If we add to this 1,607,360 cruise passengers who arrived in the country in that period, the total number of visitors was 7,630,933, another historic milestone for tourism. The numbers speak for themselves. The great work of the Tourism Cabinet led by President Luis Abinader Corona, as well as the work carried out by Minister David Collado, have placed our nation among the main destinations in Latin America, honoring the slogan "The Dominican Republic is in fashion". One aspect that should be highlighted in the results to September is the performance of construction, a sector with a great multiplier effect on other economic activities. After presenting negative records in some months of the first half of the year, largely due to the moderation of domestic demand and high input costs, construction continued to recover by expanding 9.5% in September 2023 compared to the same month of the previous year, standing out as the best performance recorded so far this year. Similarly, agriculture exhibited a year-on-year increase of 3.4% in September, for an increase of 3.8% in January-September 2023. I must say that the international community has recognized as meritorious what has been achieved by the Dominican economy so far this year, despite an unfavorable environment. Just a few days ago, Katie Taylor, director of the Pan American Development Foundation, an independent organization affiliated with the Organization of American States (OAS), said that the Dominican Republic "is a light in the hemisphere, with democratic stability, economic stability and development." Regarding the labor market, I am pleased to share with you the news about the latest data from the Central Bank's Continuous National Labor Force Survey (ENCFT). For the July-September 2023 quarter, total employment reached its highest historical level of 4,855,631 workers, reflecting a remarkable creation of 222,497 jobs in year-on-year terms. The generation of new jobs in the last twelve months was concentrated in formal employment, that is, those who have access to social security benefits through their occupation, verifying a year-on-year increase of 164,498 people in this category, representing 74% of the total increase in employed people in the last year. With these results, the percentage of informality was reduced by 1.5 p.p. in the third quarter of 2023, falling from 58.1% in July-September 2022 to 56.7% in the same period of 2023. The open unemployment rate stood at 5.4% for the third quarter of 2023. EXTERNAL AND FINANCIAL SECTOR Regarding the external sector, in January-September 2023, it is important to note that free zones exported US5,961.6 million during that period, for a growth of 0.7% after having remained in negative territory for much of the year. Led by sales of medical and surgical equipment, exports from free zones showed great resilience to the adverse conditions prevailing in the world. Good news in the external sector is the remarkable evolution of tourism, which registered a year-on-year increase in its revenues of 19.3%, reaching US7,594.4 million in January-September 2023. Likewise, during that period, the country received remittances of US7,597.1 million for a year-on-year increase of 3.9%, a significant contribution to the economy of the Dominican diaspora. Likewise, I must highlight that foreign direct investment (FDI) reached US3,369.5 million in January-September, for a year-on-year growth of 3.9%. This flow of resources, mostly destined for energy, tourism and trade, shows once again the great confidence of foreign investors in the country. It is necessary to recognize the role played in the dynamism of investment (both foreign and local) by the Cabinet led by Vice President Raquel Pena, whose leadership has been fundamental, as it was during the health crisis when the Health Cabinet under her mandate carried out a successful vaccination plan. The large volume of foreign currency received by the Dominican economy during January-September has made it possible to maintain the relative stability of the exchange rate in an environment of accumulation of international reserves. In this sense, at the end of September the Dominican peso accumulated a depreciation of just 0.8%, while international reserves stood at approximately US15,900 million, equivalent to 13.2% of GDP and 5.9 months of imports, above the metrics recommended by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Friends, in a dynamic economy that reflects strong macroeconomic fundamentals such as ours, it is important to recognize the role of the financial sector as a support for private productive activity. For this reason, the strength of its indicators is essential for the proper functioning of the economy. According to the most recent information published by the Superintendency of Banks, the solvency position of the financial system reached 16.5% as of August 2023, comfortably complying with the 10% required by current regulations. Likewise, the return on average equity (ROE) was 26.3% and on average assets (ROA) was 3.1%, while the NPL ratio stood at just 1.1%, with that of multiple banks being lower than 1.0%. INSTITUTIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS AND PLANS Below, allow me to present some institutional achievements achieved during the last year by our Central Bank, while commenting on cutting-edge issues that the institution has a special interest in developing or in knowing in depth. First, the commitment assumed by the Central Bank in cybersecurity issues continues and only during the last year, our Cyber Security Incident Response Center provides protection and support due to its interconnection with the Dominican Financial System, one of the most modern in Latin America and which has served as a pilot for other central banks to replicate the model. In this regard, during this year technical missions and senior officials from the central banks of Honduras and Guatemala visited with the aim of learning about the Dominican experience. Likewise, important steps forward were taken with the issue of financial inclusion, by completing the fieldwork of the National Survey of Financial Inclusion and Education (ENIEF 2023), which is part of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2022-2030. I am also pleased to report that the Central Bank has agreed to develop, together with the financial system, a project to promote women's entrepreneurship and its relationship with financial issues. In this regard, measures are being studied to deepen and promote female leadership in productive activity. This proposal goes hand in hand with the approach to economics with a gender perspective that recently earned the Nobel Prize in Economics to Harvard professor Claudia Goldin. Another issue in which the Central Bank has been involved is climate change, recognizing that it constitutes a risk not only for societies and the environment, but also for economic and financial stability. In this regard, the bank maintains an active role in the National Council on Climate Change, conducts studies that it publishes in its magazine "Econoclima" and works on the design of measures that facilitate green financing and environmental risk management in the financial system. Although progress in these areas is important, in the current global situation there is no more relevant issue for monetary authorities than that related to the so-called central bank digital currencies (CBDCs). According to the IMF, "CBDCs are digital versions of cash issued and regulated by central banks. As such, unlike cryptocurrencies, they are more secure and are not volatile." Currently, more than 100 countries in the world are studying the issue of a possible issuance of digital currency backed by the Central Bank. The Dominican Republic is no exception. Like other issuing banks, it has been carrying out an in-depth investigation of the costs and benefits that could be involved in the issuance of a digital currency with the support of the Central Bank, for which it has technical assistance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) through its Department of Monetary and Capital Markets. It is expected that this process will take several years and that any decision on the introduction of a CBDC in the country would be contingent on its impact on the effectiveness of monetary policy and financial stability, its role in the efficiency of payment systems and its role as a promoter of financial inclusion. among others. It is important to note that the Central Bank is in the final stages of analysis to offer results of the "National Survey of Micro, Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (MSMEs) 2022-2023". For the survey survey, the directory of MSME establishments was used as a framework, which was carried out through a national sweep that yielded a result of more than 465,000 economic units throughout the national territory, of which approximately 85% were identified as MSMEs. This survey fulfilled the objective of identifying and capturing economic and financial information of this segment of companies so relevant in the development of national economic activity, representing a great step towards being able to develop a policy that serves as a boost to this sector. On the other hand, the Central Bank has maintained its commitment to institutional social responsibility through different areas. This is circumscribed in the interest of guiding all citizens in the neuralgic issues of the institution and of promoting altruism and solidarity in employees and their families for the execution of actions in favor of the collective good. Specifically, the various economic and financial training activities for employees and the external public within the "Central Classroom" program are highlighted. We can also mention the reforestation days, beach cleanups, donations and delivery of specific infrastructure works to less favored communities within the "Bancentraliano Volunteering". In the end, these and other achievements show that the best offering of the human being is to give oneself in the face of the need of others. PERSPECTIVES AND FINAL THOUGHTS Before concluding, allow me to tell you that at the Central Bank we maintain positive prospects for the Dominican economy to the extent that monetary policy continues to have its effects and a complete dynamization of public investment is achieved. This vision is shared by multilateral organizations such as the IMF, which, in its most recent global economic prospects report, projects economic growth for the country of 3.0% in 2023 and 5.2% in 2024. The greater dynamism of the economy would be achieved in a context of stable prices with inflation around the center of the target of 4% 1%. The evolution of growth in an environment of stability in recent years has led to great progress in the nation's GDP per capita. In this sense, from a level of US8,583.1 in 2019, the pre-pandemic year, GDP per capita went to US10,732.9 in 2022 and is expected to exceed US11,200 in 2023, ranking it as the seventh country in Latin America with the highest GDP per capita. Regarding the indicators of the external sector, by the end of 2023 a flow of foreign direct investment is expected to exceed US4,300 million. Tourism revenues are also expected to exceed US10 billion, supported by an arrival of visitors that would reach 10 million by air and sea. Likewise, remittances would close the year at around US10,000 million. Bancentraliana Family, as I approach the end of my speech, I want to close with some reflections that allow us to maintain optimism for the future that awaits the Dominican economy. The great crises of the 21st century, despite being related to events of historical connotations for humanity, have given us the opportunity to show the strength of Dominicans. As a country we have remained united by showing the world our great capacity to overcome critical moments and adapt to new realities, without losing the ultimate goal of achieving sustainable development that improves the living conditions of all Dominicans. This, friends, is proof that the people who make up our nation are resilient and that this characteristic is observed in the daily tasks we perform, in the effort to do them correctly and in the sense of transcendence we give to our work. Having this wonderful human capital is one of the reasons that makes me remain optimistic about the future of the Dominican economy. I invite you to make this optimism your own as well. It is time to continue climbing steps towards development. As the famous author of Les Miserables, Victor Hugo, said, "the future has many names. For the weak it is the unattainable. For the fearful, the unknown. For the brave it is the opportunity." Let's bet on the future. God bless you and thank you very much!
